title: QM-01 Warm-started quantum replica-exchange Langevin (QSVT/Witten-Laplacian) sampler for the esmprior (θ,τ) posterior at ≥60 aa
protein_question: Can posterior-averaged structures be obtained at 60–150 aa for less than the best classical sampler costs? These are the S33 soft readout (soft Boltzmann beat hard tails by 1.40× MDE, but only as an exact sum over 262,144 enumerated states), now needed over a non-enumerable (θ,τ) space.
quantum_primitive: Operator-level quantum acceleration of replica-exchange Langevin diffusion (QRELD; Leng, Ding, Chen, Lin, PNAS 2026 [A44]). QSVT singular-value thresholding of a block-encoded, symmetrised Witten-Laplacian/RELD generator is applied to a classically derived warm start. Discrete fallback: Szegedy/QSA walk on a PT chain over the same energy.
mechanism: Reversible chain P with gap δ: classical powers P^t damp the slow mode as (1−δ)^t, so ~1/δ steps are needed per independent sample. A unitary walk (Szegedy) or a QSVT polynomial implements Chebyshev polynomials T_k(P), and degree k ≈ 1/√δ already separates eigenvalue 1 from 1−δ. Chebyshev polynomials have signed coefficients (combinations of P^j with negative weights). A sampling-based classical algorithm can realise only nonnegative mixtures of P^j; realising signed ones needs the full exponentially large vector or incurs a sign problem. The unitary realises them natively through interference. Some chains let classical lifting/nonreversibility capture part of this gain [A14, A18], so the twin must be the lifted chain where one exists. The gain is √ of the RELD gap / Poincaré constant, C_PI ~ e^{βΓ}. That halves the barrier exponent; it does not remove it.
oracle_and_state_prep: Coherent ∇E_A80 over all L(L−1)/2 pair terms: fixed-point distance, sqrt, soft-bin interpolation of the pair's 28-bin −log p table, (θ,τ) head and sterics. The pair index is classical loop control, so each pair needs only a 28-entry lookup (~10^2 Toffolis). Reversible reverse-mode AD costs ~3–4× the energy, about 10^7–10^8 Toffolis per gradient query at L=100 (I(prog), extending lit_A §3.9). Replica exchange multiplies registers by R ≈ 10–30. The warm start requires |⟨φ|σ⟩| = Ω(1). The candidate is a Laplace/Gaussian-mixture state over K classical basin minima (coherent affine map, ~d² multiplications ≈ 10^7 Toffolis). Its overlap is unmeasured, and if γ(L) decays as e^{−cL} a 1/γ factor erases the speedup. No cloning: each of the tens of samples the soft readout needs costs a fresh preparation. The oracle cost makes C_q/C_c ≈ 10^5–10^9 per step, which likely erases the wall-clock gain unless K ≥ 10^10–10^16 classical steps per sample.
strongest_classical_competitor: Portfolio: tuned PT/REST2 + HMC in (θ,τ) with feedback-optimised ladders; adaptive SMC; lifted/nonreversible chains (underdamped Langevin); an amortised flow/diffusion generator trained on PT samples, used as an independence proposal with MH/importance correction; a random-prior + L-BFGS pool reweighted by Laplace basin masses (the S33 random prior sampler beat VQE).
information_vs_computation: All information is classical: ESM-2 → esmprior pair distributions and (θ,τ) head define π. The quantum stage only samples the same π faster. The ceiling on its value is the soft-readout gain from exactly converged samples, which is measurable classically at ≤60 aa.
relation_to_S29_S33: OLD MECHANISM: CVaR-VQE or tempered Born machines shaping a diagonal register distribution, consumed by argmin/prefix/convex readout (K-001–K-007, QX-28/29). OLD FAILURE: solver-equivalence, condition C, and Metropolis closer to exact Gibbs than the circuit on an enumerable 18-qubit space. NEW MECHANISM: provable Chebyshev/QSVT acceleration of mixing for a specified continuous posterior, consumed as unbiased samples for a posterior average. Whole-distribution consumption falls outside H-001's argmin/prefix/convex class. WHY OLD CONTROL NO LONGER APPLIES: the space is non-enumerable, so the exact sum is unavailable, and the twin is a mixing-limited MCMC rather than an exact solver. The condition-C analogue (samples must transmit to the chain) and the equal-tuning twin still apply in full.
kill_result: Any one of: (a) at T_read the best portfolio's steps per independent sample extrapolate to <10^10 at L=150, below break-even for C_q ≥ 1 s; (b) hardness appears only at T below the readout-optimal T_read, i.e. it is manufactured by over-counted pair likelihoods; (c) the sampled (not enumerated) soft readout fails to beat decoder argmin by ≥1.0× MDE on long40; (d) the warm-start Bhattacharyya overlap γ(L) falls so fast that 1/γ > √K at L=100.
minimal_classical_first_test: All mid30 (41) and long40 (45) targets, plus tuning126 for the scaling fit. Four independent tuned PT runs per target (16 replicas, HMC moves in (θ,τ), ~4×10^6 energy+gradient evaluations per run; roughly 10 h on 8 cores). Measure: τ_int of E and of RMSD-to-decoder; replica round-trip time; cross-run disagreement in topology-cluster populations; and the chain RMSD of the sampled soft readout vs decoder argmin under the S33 MDE contract, with T_read chosen on dev folds. Fit log(steps per independent sample) against L (9→60 aa) and report the 150-aa extrapolation with a CI. Side measurement: AIS log Z to estimate the Bhattacharyya overlap of a K-basin Laplace-mixture warm start.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low. The speedup is provably at most quadratic, and a per-step cost ratio C_q/C_c ≈ 10^5–10^9 puts the break-even runtime T* = P·C_q²/C_c at days to centuries. Funnels plus PT make barriers polynomial. It stays top-ranked only because K(L) has never been measured.
classical_primitive_replaced: Only the mixing/decorrelation phase of tuned REMD/PT+HMC (burn-in plus τ_int per independent sample). Energy, decoder, alignment and soft averaging stay classical.
expected_speedup: Quadratic in 1/Gap(RELD): Õ(√(βd/Gap)) vs Õ(βd/Gap)-type. Wall-clock break-even needs K ≥ (C_q/C_c)² steps per independent sample: ~10^10 (C_q = 1 s) to ~10^16 (C_q = 10^3 s) at C_c ≈ 10 µs.
measurement_readout: Computational-basis measurement of d·b grid qubits (d = 2L−5, b ≈ 6–8) gives one structure per coherent preparation. Classical L-BFGS polish (optional), alignment, then soft average → built chain.
prior_art_known: Leng et al. PNAS 123 e2512789123 (2026) arXiv:2505.05301 [A44]; Childs et al. arXiv:2210.06539; Ozgul et al. arXiv:2310.11445; Motamedi–Ronagh arXiv:2210.08104; Somma et al. arXiv:0804.1571; Szegedy quant-ph/0401053; Sanders et al. arXiv:2007.07391; Babbush et al. arXiv:2011.04149. Within the repo corpus (448 papers) the search found no evidence of a costed coherent gradient oracle for a learned protein energy (gap G-2).
representation: π_T(x) ∝ exp(−E_A80(x)/T), x = (θ_i, τ_i) ∈ T^{2L−5} on 2^b grids, fixed 3.8 Å CA–CA bonds; T_read is selected on the dev split.
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: An amortised flow/diffusion generator trained on PT output, used with importance reweighting, gives independent samples at ~ms each after training. If its ESS stays ≥10% at 60–150 aa, it removes exactly the per-sample mixing cost that QRELD accelerates. MPS over residue index captures chain-local correlations but not the all-pairs esmprior terms cheaply.

title: QM-02 Classical PT + quantum narrow-well discovery (hide-and-seek amplifier) + classical basin-mass refinement
protein_question: At length, does the learned-energy posterior contain narrow, deep wells that carry mass (for example a native-like topology) yet are almost never visited by random-prior restarts or PT? If so, can a quantum subroutine find them for roughly the square root of the classical query cost?
quantum_primitive: Olivucci et al. 2026 continuous Gibbs sampler, provable Ω(α) classical vs Õ(√α) quantum queries with α = e^{βΔ} [A45]. Minimal form: fixed-point amplitude amplification of the product (θ,τ)-head prior state onto the sublevel set {E(x) < E_thr}. There is no decoder in superposition. E_thr is set native-free from energy quantiles of the classical pool.
mechanism: A Grover/AA iterate rotates the prior state by angle 2·arcsin√p per oracle pair, so amplitudes add: after k calls the marked amplitude is ~k√p, while k classical trials give probability ~k·p. A classical method would need signed interference (a sign problem) to copy this. Olivucci et al. prove the classical Ω(α) bound for any value/gradient/higher-derivative query algorithm on hide-and-seek instances. Once one point in the well is known, its mass is estimated classically (local PT/Laplace/MBAR), so the quantum part is only discovery. Crucial caveat: classical restarts relax to the minimum, so their target is the basin of attraction (fraction p_att), which is far larger than the sublevel set (p). Without coherent relaxation the quantum search targets p, and it wins only if 1/√p < 1/p_att. Enlarging p with coherent gradient steps costs one gradient oracle per step.
oracle_and_state_prep: Threshold oracle on E(x) (energy only, all pairs): ~10^6–10^7 Toffolis at L=100. The prior state costs O(L·2^b), as 2L small Grover–Rudolph loads of 1D/2D per-residue marginals from the classical (θ,τ) head, a legitimate classical information source. No native indicator is allowed; E_thr comes from classical pool statistics. The full Olivucci sampler also needs a gradient oracle plus O(β²Δ²) annealing steps. The speedup survives the oracle cost only if classical p_att < ~10^-10 per mass-carrying basin (with C_q/C_c ≥ 10^5).
strongest_classical_competitor: Random-prior + L-BFGS restarts (saturated at 32–64 restarts at 44–60 aa); PT/REST2 with many replicas; basin hopping; nested sampling, which targets small-volume high-mass regions; Wang–Landau.
information_vs_computation: Information comes from the esmprior pair terms and the (θ,τ) head, both classical. The subroutine can only find wells that the learned energy already makes deep. If the native basin is not such a well, nothing is gained (H-002).
relation_to_S29_S33: OLD MECHANISM: amplitude-amplified decoder restarts (M9, killed) and CVaR-tail search on structural registers (K-002, K-005). OLD FAILURE: restart saturation (≤0.14 Å decoder–floor gap), condition C, and the cost of a reversible decoder. NEW MECHANISM: sublevel-set search of the raw continuous energy under a product prior, used to discover modes for a posterior average rather than to supply the argmin. It is relevant only in the persistence/golf-course regime. WHY OLD CONTROL NO LONGER APPLIES: it still applies at ≤60 aa, where restart saturation (p_att ≳ 1/64) kills this card directly. It could matter only at ≥100 aa if p_att collapses.
kill_result: Any one of: every basin carrying ≥5% posterior mass at T_read has classical p_att ≥ 10^-8 at all lengths tested; no narrow-deep basin exists (volume ratio ≤ e^-5 with mass ≥ 5%), i.e. a funnel; or E_thr cannot be set native-free below the classical pool's minimum.
minimal_classical_first_test: Landscape census on mid30/long40: 512 random-prior L-BFGS minimisations per target (~6 h on 8 cores). Cluster minima by contact-map topology. Per basin, record min energy, Laplace log-volume (Hessian log-det), p_att (hit frequency) and PT-visitation mass (from the QM-01 runs). Run nested sampling on 5 targets for p(E < E_thr) under the head prior. ORACLE diagnostic (labelled): relax the native under E and report whether the information-floor basin is narrow and deep, and its p_att. Fit log p_att against L.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low. Restart saturation at 44–60 aa implies p_att ≳ 1/64 for the relevant basin, and natural funnels argue against hidden needles. The only open regime is an unmeasured one at ≥100 aa.
classical_primitive_replaced: Only rare-mode discovery (the fraction of restarts/PT excursions meant to find low-p_att basins). PT, basin-mass estimation and polishing stay classical.
expected_speedup: At most quadratic in rarity (√(1/p) vs 1/p_att). The ratio becomes exponential only if log(1/p) = Ω(L), and then both sides are exponential.
measurement_readout: One measurement of the grid registers per amplification gives a point in the well. Then classical L-BFGS, local PT and Laplace/MBAR mass feed the soft readout.
prior_art_known: Olivucci et al. arXiv:2608.24527 [A45]; Brassard–Høyer–Mosca–Tapp quant-ph/0005055; Woodard–Schmidler–Huber EJP 14:780 (2009) [E39]; Machta PRE 80 056706 [E33]; Skilling, Bayesian Anal. 1:833 (2006). Within the repo corpus the search found no evidence of any landscape census of learned protein energies (gap G-3).
representation: (θ,τ) grid registers loaded with the product of per-residue head marginals; the energy is a threshold oracle on E_A80.
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: Nested sampling and high-recall learned proposals (flows trained across many proteins) attack the same rarity classically. No TN shortcut exists for all-pairs terms.

title: QM-03 Non-thermal QSA paths: residue-growth and likelihood-tempering annealing from the learned per-residue prior
protein_question: Start from a cheaply prepared coherent prior (the product of (θ,τ)-head marginals). Is there a path to the full pair posterior whose consecutive stages overlap Ω(1) but mix slowly within a stage? If so, walk-based transport (√δ per stage) would beat SMC with MCMC rejuvenation.
quantum_primitive: Quantum simulated annealing along a slowly evolving sequence of Markov chains: Wocjan–Abeyesinghe arXiv:0804.4259 [A7]; Orsucci–Briegel–Dunjko arXiv:1503.01334 [A9]; Harrow–Wei adaptive QSA for Bayesian inference arXiv:1907.09965 [A31]. The path parameter is either the number of residues grown, k, or the likelihood exponent λ ∈ [0,1] on the pair term.
mechanism: Each stage reflects about |π_λ⟩ using phase estimation on the stage's Szegedy walk, which has phase gap Θ(√δ_λ) by the same Chebyshev/interference mechanism as QM-01. With ℓ stages of Ω(1) overlap, each qsample costs Õ(ℓ/√δ_min) walk steps, vs Õ(ℓ/δ_min) for classical annealed MCMC. The path choice matters. Temperature paths can cross first-order-like transitions that stay slow whatever the schedule (Bhatnagar–Randall [E40]), while growth or likelihood paths may avoid them. That helps classical SMC equally, which is the catch. SMC's resampling has no quantum analogue (no cloning), so the quantum side cannot use population enrichment.
oracle_and_state_prep: Start state: a product prior, O(L·2^b), cheap. Stage oracle: coherent ΔE_λ of the pair terms among grown residues plus a Lemieux-style Metropolis coin, up to 10^6–10^8 Toffolis per step at L=100. No reversible decoder is needed, which is the obstacle that killed M6. One sample per full anneal. The oracle overhead (C_q/C_c ≥ 10^5) erases the gain unless per-stage δ_min ≤ 10^-10.
strongest_classical_competitor: Adaptive SMC samplers (Del Moral–Doucet–Jasra) with MCMC rejuvenation; PERM chain growth (Grassberger PRE 56 3682 [E53]); energy-guided fragment regrowth (Zhang–Kou–Liu JCP 126 2007); AIS; plus the improved classical cooling schedules published alongside the quantum result [A32].
information_vs_computation: Head marginals and pair distributions are both classical (ESM-2). The quantum part only transports the state along the path.
relation_to_S29_S33: OLD MECHANISM: trained tempered Born machines and VQE registers (K-007, QX-29). OLD FAILURE: a Metropolis twin came closer to exact Gibbs on an enumerable space. NEW MECHANISM: an untrained, provable walk-step speedup per stage along a non-thermal path over a continuous non-enumerable space. WHY OLD CONTROL NO LONGER APPLIES: exact enumeration is unavailable and the twin is SMC with rejuvenation, which is stronger than the old Metropolis twin; the new control applies fully.
kill_result: Either: adaptive SMC (1,000 particles) matches the PT-converged soft readout within ≤10^8 energy evaluations at 60 aa, with per-stage rejuvenation τ ≤ 10^3 steps, so the quantum saving is ≤ ~30× per stage, far below C_q/C_c. Or conditional ESS collapses within a stage at any λ increment (no Ω(1) overlap), making the stage count exponential for both.
minimal_classical_first_test: On tuning126/mid30/long40, run adaptive SMC along (a) the λ-path and (b) the residue-growth path from the head-product prior. Record stage count ℓ(L) at conditional ESS 0.5, per-stage rejuvenation τ_int, total evaluations needed to match the PT-converged soft readout, and weight-degeneracy events. Report the fitted scaling of ℓ and τ against L. ≤12 h on 8 cores.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low. The stage count is not reduced (adaptive schedules help classical SMC equally), and per-stage rejuvenation on a funnel-like landscape is unlikely to have δ ≤ 10^-10.
classical_primitive_replaced: The MCMC rejuvenation inside SMC/AIS stages. Resampling and weighting have no quantum replacement.
expected_speedup: Quadratic in the per-stage gap δ_min only.
measurement_readout: Measure the grid registers after the final stage (one sample per anneal), then classical polish and soft average.
prior_art_known: arXiv:0804.4259, arXiv:1503.01334, arXiv:1907.09965, arXiv:2009.11270 (all verified in repo); Del Moral et al. JRSS-B 68:411 (2006); Grassberger PRE 56:3682 (1997). Within the repo corpus the search found no evidence of a residue-growth annealing path in any quantum sampling proposal.
representation: (θ,τ) grids; π_λ ∝ q_head(x)·exp(−λ·E_pair(x)/T), or π_k over the first k residues.
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: SMC itself is the classical reproduction. An autoregressive residue-by-residue model or MPS proposal trained on SMC output emulates the growth path.

title: QM-04 Quantum rejection sampling from a cheap coherent product prior (no decoder in superposition)
protein_question: Is the learned pair likelihood close enough to the per-residue (θ,τ)-head prior that a single stage of amplitude amplification (prior → posterior) is feasible at 44–60 aa and beyond?
quantum_primitive: Quantum rejection sampling (Ozols–Roetteler–Roland arXiv:1103.2774 [A36]; Low–Yoder–Chuang arXiv:1402.7359 [A37]) with acceptance amplitude √exp(−(E_pair − E_lb)/T) under fixed-point amplitude amplification.
mechanism: The accepted branch has amplitude √P_acc. Amplitude amplification rotates it to Ω(1) in O(1/√P_acc) prior preparations and oracle calls, vs O(1/P_acc) for classical rejection, because amplitudes add under the Grover iterate while classical trials add probabilities. It needs a certified lower bound E_lb on E_pair (the sum of per-pair minima) so the coin is normalised.
oracle_and_state_prep: Product-state preparation O(L·2^b). A coherent E_pair costs 10^6–10^8 Toffolis at L=100, plus an arcsin coin rotation. Unlike killed M6, the prior is a product state rather than a reversible decoder. However log(1/P_acc) is a max-divergence between π and q, which grows with the number of pair terms. The quadratic gain on an exponential stays exponential, so it almost certainly erases the value.
strongest_classical_competitor: SMC/AIS from the same prior with intermediate stages (polynomial where overlaps are constant); importance sampling with ESS monitoring; PT.
information_vs_computation: All inputs are classical. The quantum part changes only the number of prior draws.
relation_to_S29_S33: OLD MECHANISM: not in S29–S33. The literature's M6 (WEAK) required running the learned decoder coherently. OLD FAILURE: the prohibitive state preparation of a coherent decoder. NEW MECHANISM: a product prior removes the decoder from superposition. WHY OLD CONTROL NO LONGER APPLIES: the decoder obstacle is gone, but it is replaced by the P_acc exponent.
kill_result: Measured log(1/P_acc) at 44–60 aa exceeds ~28 nats (the quantum side then needs >10^6 oracle calls per sample while SMC stays polynomial), or grows linearly in L. Kill is near-certain.
minimal_classical_first_test: On tuning126/mid30/long40, estimate log Z_π − log Z_q and the bound E_lb per target with AIS/SMC. Report log(1/P_acc), Rényi-2 divergence (importance ESS) and the Bhattacharyya coefficient against L (≤2 h). The Bhattacharyya output also feeds QM-01's warm-start audit.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low. The acceptance exponent is expected to be tens to hundreds of nats at 60 aa, and a square root of an exponential is still exponential.
classical_primitive_replaced: Rejection/importance sampling from the head prior.
expected_speedup: Quadratic in 1/P_acc, with both sides exp(Θ(L)).
measurement_readout: Flag qubit plus grid registers measured once per amplification.
prior_art_known: arXiv:1103.2774, arXiv:1402.7359 (verified in repo). No protein application is known.
representation: Product of per-residue (θ,τ)-head marginals on grids; the pair term acts as the likelihood.
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: SMC/AIS is the classical reproduction.

title: QM-05 Fault-tolerant cost of a coherent esmprior walk/energy oracle, and the landscape-independent break-even runtime T* = a²·P·C_q²/C_c
protein_question: What is the cheapest coherent implementation of one Metropolis/Szegedy step and one gradient query for the A80/esmprior energy at L = 60, 100 and 150, and does any quadratic-speedup card survive the resulting break-even?
quantum_primitive: Coherent fixed-point arithmetic oracle (Häner–Roetteler–Svore arXiv:1805.12445 [A59]); unary-iteration QROM for per-pair 28-bin tables (Babbush et al. arXiv:1805.03662 [A60]); Lemieux et al. Metropolis coin and walk circuits (arXiv:1910.01659 [A55]) inside a Szegedy walk.
mechanism: This is a costing card: it defines which card's resource matters. With a quadratic speedup, sequential oracle calls fall from K to a·√K. Let C_c and C_q be the classical and quantum per-call times and P the classical parallelism. Break-even is K* = (a·P·C_q/C_c)², and the quantum runtime at break-even is T* = a²·P·C_q²/C_c, which does not depend on landscape hardness (the argument form of Babbush et al. arXiv:2011.04149). A practical advantage within T_max therefore requires C_q ≤ √(T_max·C_c/(a²P)). For T_max = 1 week, C_c = 10 µs and a = 1: C_q ≤ ~2.5 s at P = 1, ≤ ~0.25 s at P = 100. At a 10^6 Toffoli/s logical rate that caps the oracle at ~2.5×10^6 or ~2.5×10^5 Toffolis per step. At Sanders' single-factory 170 µs/Toffoli, a 10^6-Toffoli step gives T* ≈ 90 years at P = 1.
speedup_type: walk-steps (costing card; no speedup of its own)
oracle_and_state_prep: Estimate (I(prog), to be validated). Per pair: 3 subtractions and 3 squarings (~400 Toffolis at b = 16), sqrt (~1–2×10^3), bin index and fraction (~300), a 28-entry unary-iteration lookup ×2 (~2×110), an interpolation multiply (~256) and accumulation: about 3×10^3 Toffolis per pair. Pair-specific tables are cheap because the pair index is classical control; only the distance bin is coherent. Cartesian single-residue move at L=100: select residue i (~L·3b ≈ 5×10^3), 2(L−1) pair terms old and new (~6×10^5), Boltzmann coin (~10^4), uncompute ×2, total ~1.2×10^6 Toffolis, ~5×10^3 logical coordinate qubits plus ~10^3 ancillae. It needs CA–CA bond terms and coherent atan2 for the 4 affected torsions. Torsion pivot with a superposed pivot index: all ~L²/2 pairs under control plus downstream rotations, ~3×10^7–10^8. Gradient query: ~4× the full energy, ~6×10^7.
strongest_classical_competitor: Classical ΔE per move with vectorised torch/numba: C_c ≈ 1–10 µs at L=100 on one core, lower on GPUs. Replicas and chains parallelise trivially.
information_vs_computation: Not applicable (costing). It decides whether any computation-side card can matter at all.
relation_to_S29_S33: OLD MECHANISM: S29–S33 ran only in simulators and never costed physical quantum runtime (charter: simulator runtime ≠ physical runtime). OLD FAILURE: not applicable. NEW MECHANISM: the first explicit per-step Toffoli count for a learned protein energy (literature gap G-2, H-008). WHY OLD CONTROL NO LONGER APPLIES: no DNR entry covers it. It gates QM-01/02/03/06/07/09/12.
kill_result: If the cheapest move set costs ≥10^7 Toffolis per step at L=100 (C_q ≥ 10 s at 1 MHz, so T* ≥ 10^7·P s ≥ 4 months at P = 1), every quadratic walk/query card is practically dead regardless of G1; only a super-quadratic mechanism could survive. A cost ≤3×10^5 Toffolis per step keeps them alive, conditional on K(L) ≥ K*.
minimal_classical_first_test: Static operation count from the A80 energy code for Cartesian and pivot moves at L = 60/100/150: pair terms touched per move and arithmetic per pair, mapped to Toffolis using published fixed-point costs. Measure C_c on this CPU (µs per ΔE, batched and unbatched). Take an SVD/CP rank of the L×L×28 −log p tensor on long40 to find the rank for ≤0.05-nat error (does shared-coefficient compression cut lookups?). Tabulate K* and T* for P ∈ {1, 8, 10^3} and Toffoli rates {10^4, 10^5, 10^6}/s. Under 1 day, mostly analysis. Optional: compile an L = 6, b = 8 toy in a resource estimator to check the per-pair count.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low. The literature range of 10^6–10^8 Toffolis per step already implies T* from days to centuries. The card's value is that it decides this definitively.
classical_primitive_replaced: None (enabling estimate).
expected_speedup: None of its own. It outputs K*(L) and T*(L).
measurement_readout: Not applicable.
prior_art_known: Sanders et al. PRX Quantum 1 020312, arXiv:2007.07391 [A56]; Babbush et al. PRX Quantum 2 010103, arXiv:2011.04149 [A57]; Lemieux et al. Quantum 4 287, arXiv:1910.01659 [A55]; Chiang–Nagaj–Wocjan arXiv:0903.3465; Häner et al. arXiv:1805.12445; Babbush et al. arXiv:1805.03662. Within the repo corpus the search found no evidence of a published per-step cost for any learned molecular energy.
representation: Cartesian CA registers (3L·b qubits) or (θ,τ) registers; 28-bin per-pair tables held classically.
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: Not applicable.

title: QM-06 Walk phase estimation / quantum fast-forwarding for metastable-state discovery and escape-rate certification
protein_question: Is a decoded or sampled structure a metastable trap of the posterior, and how slow is escape from it? In other words, is the classical ensemble's uncertainty estimate trustworthy at length?
quantum_primitive: Phase estimation on the Szegedy walk W(P), started from a basin-restricted warm state |π_B⟩ (Szegedy quant-ph/0401053; Wocjan–Temme arXiv:2107.07365); quantum fast-forwarding, which prepares a state ∝ P^t|π_B⟩ in O(√t) walk steps (Apers–Sarlette arXiv:1804.02321); Chowdhury–Somma hitting-time estimation (arXiv:1603.02940).
mechanism: If basin B escapes at rate λ_B, |π_B⟩ has Ω(1) overlap with the slow eigenvectors. Szegedy maps eigenvalue 1−λ to phase ≈ √(2λ), so QPE resolves the slow phase with O(1/√λ_B) walk steps. Classically a transition must be observed, which takes ~1/λ_B steps. Fast-forwarding realises the Chebyshev acceleration of P^t (signed polynomial, the same mechanism as QM-01). The readout is a scalar (the rate), so the one-sample-per-anneal penalty does not apply.
oracle_and_state_prep: Same walk oracle as QM-05. The warm state |π_B⟩ requires sampling inside B, which is local and mixes fast, so a warm start is plausible there (unlike QM-01's global problem). The oracle cost (C_q/C_c ≥ 10^5) means 1/λ_B must be ≥10^10 steps for any wall-clock gain.
strongest_classical_competitor: MSMs/TICA/VAMP from many short parallel trajectories; weighted ensemble; milestoning; forward-flux sampling. For trap detection alone: broad random-prior sampling, which had 0 traps in S33.
information_vs_computation: The energy is entirely classical. The output (kinetics or metastability) bears on the structure endpoint only indirectly, through uncertainty.
relation_to_S29_S33: OLD MECHANISM: none. S29–S33 never studied kinetics; the topology-trap lottery (QX-25) was the nearest issue. OLD FAILURE: concentrated solvers fell into traps, and the broad random-prior sampler avoided them. NEW MECHANISM: scalar rate estimation by walk QPE. WHY OLD CONTROL NO LONGER APPLIES: it probably still applies. Broad classical sampling already solves trap avoidance at ≤60 aa. Only a regime with slow escape and a structurally consequential slow mode is new.
kill_result: Either the classical MSM gives a converged slowest implied timescale ≤10^8 evaluations at 60 aa with modest growth against L, or the slow modes connect structurally equivalent basins (Δ chain RMSD < MDE), so they have no endpoint relevance.
minimal_classical_first_test: From the QM-01 PT runs, build a TICA+MSM on contact-map features at T_read for long40 and mid30. Report implied timescales t_2…t_5 (in evaluations), their growth from 9 to 60 aa, and the chain-RMSD difference between metastable sets. ~4 h analysis on existing trajectories.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low. At the lengths tested, broad classical sampling already avoids traps, and kinetic observables are outside the structure endpoint.
classical_primitive_replaced: Waiting-time-limited trajectory statistics for the slowest escape rate of a basin.
expected_speedup: Quadratic in the slowest timescale 1/λ_B.
measurement_readout: Phase-register bits give a rate estimate, repeated O(log 1/δ) times.
prior_art_known: quant-ph/0401053; arXiv:2107.07365; arXiv:1804.02321; arXiv:1603.02940 (all verified in repo). MSM practice: Prinz et al. JCP 134 (2011); Husic–Pande JACS 140 (2018).
representation: The discrete walk (Cartesian or pivot moves) of QM-05 at T_read.
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: VAMPnets and learned MSMs, plus Timewarp-style learned long-step proposals, reproduce slow-mode identification classically.

title: QM-07 Quantum-walk search for native-free topology-predicate marked sets (non-differentiable long-range constraints)
protein_question: Can posterior structures that satisfy a global, non-differentiable, native-free topological predicate be found faster than by classical hitting? Examples: ESM-predicted strand-pairing registers jointly satisfied, a sheet-handedness class, top-L/5 predicted contacts ≥80% satisfied.
quantum_primitive: Quantum-walk search with a marking oracle: MNRS (quant-ph/0608026), Krovi–Magniez–Ozols–Roland (arXiv:1002.2419), Ambainis–Gilyén–Jeffery–Kokainis (arXiv:1903.07493).
mechanism: The product of the reflection about the marked set and the reflection about π (the latter built from the walk's √δ phase gap) rotates π toward the marked set by an angle ~√(εδ). The marked set is found in O(√HT) walk steps vs classical HT. A classical walk cannot interfere reflections.
oracle_and_state_prep: Walk oracle (QM-05) plus a predicate. Contact-count predicates cost ~#contacts distance comparisons, ~10^5 Toffolis. Knot or threading invariants cost ~O(L³) arithmetic, ≥10^8 Toffolis. The predicate must be native-free (ESM contact/SS predictions only). The oracle cost plus the requirement that the predicate be a rare set under π (HT ≥ 10^10) likely erase the gain.
strongest_classical_competitor: Restrained or biased sampling: add a smooth flat-bottom restraint for the predicate's contacts, so the marked set is no longer rare. Also umbrella/metadynamics along topology CVs, and random-prior + L-BFGS with contact restraints. S33 decoders already use this information.
information_vs_computation: The predicate carries classical information (ESM contacts). The quantum walk only accelerates hitting a set that the classical energy plus restraint can also target.
relation_to_S29_S33: OLD MECHANISM: contact/fragment registers optimised by CVaR-VQE with argmin readout (K-005, DNR-03/08). OLD FAILURE: condition C (register energies did not transmit) and SA/greedy equivalence. NEW MECHANISM: predicate marking on a continuous posterior with walk hitting, yielding one satisfying structure. WHY OLD CONTROL NO LONGER APPLIES: only partly. If the predicate adds nothing beyond E, marking is redundant (condition C analogue), and a smooth bias defeats rarity classically.
kill_result: Either a flat-bottom-restrained classical sampler reaches the marked set in ≤10^6 evaluations for every target (rarity is removable by bias), or predicate-satisfying structures are no better on the chain than unrestricted posterior samples (ORACLE-labelled check).
minimal_classical_first_test: On mid30/long40, define 3 native-free predicates from ESM contact maps and predicted SS. Measure each predicate's posterior mass ε from the QM-01 samples and the random-prior pools. Measure classical hitting time unbiased vs restrained. ORACLE-labelled: compare chain RMSD of predicate-satisfying vs other structures. ≤8 h.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low. Any native-free predicate derived from classical contact predictions can be turned into a smooth classical bias, which removes the rarity the walk accelerates.
classical_primitive_replaced: Unbiased waiting time to hit a topology class.
expected_speedup: Quadratic in hitting time.
measurement_readout: Grid registers measured after the search; the predicate is re-verified classically.
prior_art_known: quant-ph/0608026; arXiv:1002.2419; arXiv:1903.07493 (verified in repo).
representation: The walk of QM-05 plus predicate registers.
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: Restrained classical sampling. AF2/ESMFold-class predictors directly output structures consistent with predicted contacts.

title: QM-08 Quantum backtracking and tree-size estimation for β-sheet topology assembly (multi-hypothesis generation)
protein_question: Given predicted secondary structure and contact probabilities, can the set of β-sheet topologies (strand pairings, orientations, register offsets) be searched and counted faster than classical DFS when the tree is huge (≥100 aa, ≥10 strands)?
quantum_primitive: Montanaro quantum backtracking, O(√T·n^{3/2}·log n) (arXiv:1509.02374 [C57]); Ambainis–Kokainis tree-size estimation (arXiv:1704.06774); Montanaro branch-and-bound (arXiv:1906.10375).
mechanism: Backtracking is a quantum walk on the search tree. Its effective resistance of ~T·n lets phase estimation detect a marked leaf in O(√(T·n)) steps, vs Θ(T) node visits for classical DFS. Tree-size estimation similarly counts leaves at quadratically lower cost. The speedup is relative to the same tree.
oracle_and_state_prep: The partial-pairing consistency predicate (each strand has ≤2 partners, register offsets inside contact-probability support, chirality rules) is cheap reversible logic, ~10^3–10^4 Toffolis per node. Backtracking finds or counts; it cannot list. If all hypotheses must be listed, the output size Ω(#leaves) erases the speedup.
strongest_classical_competitor: CSP and cost-function-network solvers with strong pruning [C82, C83]; DP over strand order; exhaustive enumeration (natural sheets have ≲10 strands); fold-recognition topology enumerators.
information_vs_computation: Information comes from SS and contact probabilities (classical, ESM-2). The value of a hypothesis set depends on being able to select from it, which S32 found discrimination-limited (C-4).
relation_to_S29_S33: OLD MECHANISM: S32 per-residue branch registers and candidate-index search (K-001, QX-15). OLD FAILURE: 'search is not the barrier; discrimination is', and ORACLE ceilings were order-statistic dominated. NEW MECHANISM: a different combinatorial object (the sheet-topology graph) searched with walks on trees, consumed as a hypothesis set for QM-09 mass estimation rather than argmin. WHY OLD CONTROL NO LONGER APPLIES: the order-statistic null and the discrimination limit still apply fully; only the combinatorial object is new.
kill_result: Any one of: tree size T ≤ 10^9 for all mid30/long40 targets and ≤10^12 extrapolated to 150 aa (classical DFS takes seconds to hours); the task needs listing (output-size bound); or the best-hypothesis-in-set ORACLE ceiling is an order statistic.
minimal_classical_first_test: For all mid30/long40 targets with ≥3 predicted strands, and ~20 leakage-controlled 100–200-aa CATH domains (sequence-only ESM predictions), run DFS over strand pairings with contact-probability pruning. Count nodes and leaves, fit T against the number of strands, and compute the ORACLE best-in-set with an order-statistic null. <1 day.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low. Natural sheets have few strands, contact priors prune hard, and multi-hypothesis use needs listing, which kills the quadratic gain.
classical_primitive_replaced: DFS/CSP enumeration of partial strand-pairing assignments.
expected_speedup: Near-quadratic in tree size, for existence and counting only.
measurement_readout: Phase estimation gives existence or count; a found leaf is decoded classically.
prior_art_known: arXiv:1509.02374, arXiv:1704.06774, arXiv:1906.10375, arXiv:2210.03210 (verified in repo). The CSP fault-tolerant estimate in which the advantage 'disappears' [C63] is also in the repo.
representation: Tree over strand pairs (partner, orientation, register-offset bin).
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: Exact classical CSP/DP. Learned topology predictors (AF2-class) collapse the tree.

title: QM-09 Quantum partition-function ratios for posterior masses of competing fold/topology hypotheses (Bayesian model averaging over folds)
protein_question: Given K classically generated topology hypotheses, what posterior mass does each carry under the learned energy? Does mass-based weighting or selection beat argmin on the built chain?
quantum_primitive: Quantum partition-function estimation with walks plus amplitude estimation along an annealing schedule: Montanaro arXiv:1504.06987; Harrow–Wei arXiv:1907.09965; Arunachalam et al. arXiv:2009.11270; Cornelissen–Hamoudi arXiv:2207.08643, Õ(log^{3/4}|Ω|/(ε√δ)).
mechanism: There are two quadratic gains. (i) Precision: amplitude estimation reads a stage ratio as the rotation angle of a Grover-type iterate by phase estimation, giving O(1/ε) vs Θ(1/ε²). (ii) Mixing: walk reflections give 1/√δ vs 1/δ. Both come from interference, which classical estimators cannot realise without sign problems.
oracle_and_state_prep: The walk oracle is restricted to hypothesis k by a coherent restraint potential at each annealing stage. The stage states come from the stage chains, so this inherits QM-01/QM-05 costs. Amplitude estimation over the stage-ratio observable. With C_q/C_c ≥ 10^5, the 1/ε gain pays only if σ/ε ≳ 10^4, which the literature says biomolecular decisions do not need (break-even CA-4).
strongest_classical_competitor: MBAR/BAR; restrained PT; AIS/SMC; Wang–Landau; harmonic/Laplace basin free energies, which are cheap.
information_vs_computation: The masses are properties of the classical learned energy. Whether they rank topologies correctly is a calibration and information question ('condition M'): overcounted pair likelihoods and the choice of T dominate.
relation_to_S29_S33: OLD MECHANISM: amplitude estimation for ensemble expectations (QA-1/C-3, killed in practice; H-005 retired) and hull/convex weighting of candidate pools (R5, K-011). OLD FAILURE: decisions were bias/information-limited, not variance-limited, and convex readouts are classical in milliseconds. NEW MECHANISM: mass estimation of classically discovered, non-enumerable topology basins used for model averaging. WHY OLD CONTROL NO LONGER APPLIES: it largely still applies. Variance limitation (σ/ε ≥ 10^4) must be demonstrated and is unlikely.
kill_result: Either condition M fails (within-target ρ(F_k, chain RMSD_k) ≤ 0.1, or the mass-weighted readout gains <1.0× MDE vs argmin), or the ranking/weight decision is stable with ≤10^4 classical samples per basin (σ/ε ≤ 10^2).
minimal_classical_first_test: On mid30/long40, cluster the QM-01/QM-02 pools into K ≤ 10 topology hypotheses per target. Compute basin free energies with restrained PT + MBAR and bootstrap errors. Compare mass-weighted vs argmin readouts on the chain (S33 contract). Record the sample count at which the decision stabilises. ≤10 h.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low. Masses of a miscalibrated learned energy are likely information-limited, and the precision gain acts on a factor that is not binding.
classical_primitive_replaced: Restrained PT/AIS + MBAR estimation of per-hypothesis free energies.
expected_speedup: At most quadratic in 1/ε and in 1/δ.
measurement_readout: Phase-estimation bits give stage ratios; the product gives Z_k/Z; classical weighting follows.
prior_art_known: arXiv:1504.06987, arXiv:1907.09965, arXiv:2009.11270, arXiv:2207.08643, arXiv:2404.02414 lower bound (all verified in repo); Shirts–Chodera MBAR arXiv:0801.1426.
representation: The (θ,τ) or Cartesian walk with per-hypothesis restraint potentials.
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: MBAR on classical samples, and Laplace approximations at basin minima.

title: QM-10 Committor and transition-rate estimation via quantum linear-system solvers on the discretised backward-Kolmogorov generator
protein_question: Between two metastable conformations of the learned (or a physical) energy, what are the committor and the rate, and can a QLSA with an amplitude-estimated scalar readout beat classical path sampling?
quantum_primitive: Quantum linear-system solving (optimal O(κ·log 1/ε) variants) or QSVT inversion of a block-encoded, sparse, finite-difference backward generator on a grid of 2^{b·d} points, with the flux functional read out by amplitude estimation.
mechanism: The generator is sparse and locally computable, so block encoding costs poly(d·b) per query and the grid size N = 2^{bd} enters only logarithmically. That is an exponential saving over classical grid solvers. The cost is Õ(κ·poly(d)/ε), with κ ~ h^-2·e^{βΔ}, so the slow rate enters linearly through κ. The strongest classical competitor is not a grid solver. Random-walk/Feynman–Kac Monte Carlo and splitting methods (WE, FFS, TPS) estimate the same scalar in poly(d). For heat-equation functionals, quantum advantage over classical random-walk methods has been argued to be at most polynomial (Linden–Montanaro–Shao; UNVERIFIED in repo).
oracle_and_state_prep: Block encoding of the generator from coherent E/∇E at grid points (QM-05 costs, ~10^7+ Toffolis per query at L=100), plus native-free basin indicators (from a classical MSM) for boundary conditions, plus preparation of the right-hand-side boundary flux and an AE readout. With κ carrying e^{βΔ} and C_q/C_c ≥ 10^5, the gain is erased against splitting methods.
strongest_classical_competitor: Weighted ensemble, forward-flux sampling, transition path sampling, milestoning, MSMs, neural-network committor methods.
information_vs_computation: The energy is classical. Rates are kinetic outputs outside the structure endpoint.
relation_to_S29_S33: OLD MECHANISM: none for kinetics. The related killed item is QSVT/HHL for small dense readout convex programs (AA-4/K-011). OLD FAILURE: dequantisation and millisecond classical solves. NEW MECHANISM: inversion of a sparse, exponentially large, well-structured generator, where dequantisation does not apply. WHY OLD CONTROL NO LONGER APPLIES: the old control (small dense problems) does not apply, but a new classical control (random-walk Monte Carlo for PDE functionals) removes the exponential.
kill_result: Either WE/FFS give rates within 20% at ≤10^8 evaluations between the slowest metastable sets found in QM-06 at 60 aa, or a theory note shows the best QLSA's κ-scaling is no better than splitting Monte Carlo (expected).
minimal_classical_first_test: A 2-page theory note comparing Õ(κ/ε) QLSA with WE/FFS cost laws for a d-dimensional double well with barrier Δ. Plus a WE run between the two slowest long40 metastable sets from QM-06 (≤6 h on 8 cores).
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low. The only exponential saving is over grid solvers, which no one uses. Against splitting Monte Carlo the advantage is at most polynomial, and the output is off-endpoint.
classical_primitive_replaced: Path-sampling/MSM rate estimation.
expected_speedup: At most polynomial (≈quadratic in 1/ε); no κ improvement over splitting methods is known.
measurement_readout: AE of the flux observable gives a scalar rate/committor average.
prior_art_known: Fokker–Planck/continuous Gibbs solvers (Motamedi–Ronagh arXiv:2210.08104, verified in repo); Linden, Montanaro, Shao 'Quantum vs. classical algorithms for solving the heat equation' arXiv:2004.06516 (UNVERIFIED in repo); Childs–Liu–Ostrander high-precision PDE algorithms arXiv:2002.07868 (UNVERIFIED).
representation: Grid over (θ,τ) or collective coordinates, with a finite-difference generator.
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: Neural committor functions and TN (TT/QTT) solvers for low-rank high-dimensional PDEs are classical alternatives.

title: QM-11 Quantum Hamiltonian Descent (continuous-space tunnelling) for global minimisation of the learned energy at ≥80 aa
protein_question: Beyond the restart-saturated regime (44–60 aa), does global minimisation of E(x) open a gap that coherent Schrödinger dynamics in a smoothing-then-focusing potential could close faster than classical global optimisers?
quantum_primitive: Quantum Hamiltonian Descent: simulate i∂ψ/∂t = [e^{φ_t}(−½Δ) + e^{χ_t}·E(x)]ψ on a d = 2L−5 dimensional grid, with the kinetic term via QFT and the potential via a phase oracle (Leng, Hickman, Li, Wu arXiv:2303.01471, UNVERIFIED in repo).
mechanism: An early high-kinetic phase delocalises the wavefunction, a coherent analogue of Gaussian smoothing. A later potential-dominated phase concentrates amplitude in low-energy regions. Barrier crossing goes by tunnelling, with amplitude ~exp(−width·√height), rather than thermal activation ~exp(−height/T). Thin, tall barriers are therefore crossed where SA/PT are exponentially slow. Separations are claimed on constructed instances (UNVERIFIED). This is not a quadratic restart speedup.
oracle_and_state_prep: Phase oracle e^{−i·t·E(x)} per Trotter step: a coherent E costs 10^6–10^8 Toffolis at L=100, and thousands of Trotter steps are needed. At 60 aa that is ~115·7 ≈ 800 grid qubits. The start state is a uniform/Gaussian product (cheap). Oracle overhead and step count likely erase any gain on a funnel-like landscape.
strongest_classical_competitor: Multi-restart L-BFGS (saturated at 32–64 restarts at 44–60 aa); basin hopping; PT-annealing; Gaussian homotopy/continuation (the classical analogue of the smoothing phase); CMA-ES.
information_vs_computation: Argmin of the classical learned energy is bounded by the information floor (≤0.14 Å headroom at 44–60 aa, H-002).
relation_to_S29_S33: OLD MECHANISM: CVaR-VQE argmin search on diagonal registers (K-002, K-005, K-006) and killed amplitude-amplified restarts (M9). OLD FAILURE: restart saturation, the information floor, and classical reproduction of argmin readouts. NEW MECHANISM: non-diagonal kinetic dynamics in continuous space, not a variational circuit and not Grover. WHY OLD CONTROL NO LONGER APPLIES: the output is still consumed by argmin, and R10 bounds any global solver's gain at ≤0.14 Å at ≤60 aa, so the control applies in full there. The card opens only if H-004's search gap appears at ≥80 aa.
kill_result: Either the decoder–floor gap is ≤ noise and restarts saturate at every length up to the longest instrument (H-004 kill), or classical Gaussian-homotopy continuation reproduces any residual gain.
minimal_classical_first_test: On long40, and on a leakage-clean 70–120-aa set with ESM-2 priors (labelled as extrapolation beyond esmprior's ≤72-aa training crops), measure E_min against restarts R = 1…512, the energy gap to the relaxed native (ORACLE diagnostic), and Gaussian-homotopy continuation. ≤12 h on 8 cores.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low. Search is saturated and information-limited at the tested lengths, and funnels lack the thin tall barriers where tunnelling beats thermal activation.
classical_primitive_replaced: Multi-restart global minimisation of E(x).
expected_speedup: Unknown for this landscape. It is claimed super-polynomial only on constructed instances.
measurement_readout: Measure the grid registers, then classical L-BFGS polish; best of a few runs.
prior_art_known: Leng et al. arXiv:2303.01471 (UNVERIFIED in repo); Leng, Zheng, Wu, quantum-classical separation in nonconvex optimisation, arXiv:2311.00811 (UNVERIFIED); Zhang, Leng, Li, escaping saddle points, arXiv:2007.10253 (UNVERIFIED); Denchev et al. PRX 6 031015 on finite-range tunnelling (verified in repo).
representation: Continuous (θ,τ) on a 2^b grid per coordinate.
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: Gaussian homotopy/continuation and PT-annealing. Semiclassical instanton estimates can predict classically whether tunnelling helps.

title: QM-12 Formulation redesign: joint (assignment × structure) posterior from sparse ambiguous experimental restraints, sampled by a quantum walk
protein_question: Suppose sparse, ambiguous experimental data supply the missing per-target information (sign, common mode, ~3n−6 numbers): NOE, crosslink or sparse EM distance restraints with unknown assignments. Is decoding the joint discrete-assignment × continuous-structure posterior then classically slow-mixing, so that a walk-based sampler becomes load-bearing?
quantum_primitive: Szegedy/QSA walk on the joint space, or quantum RELD with discrete assignment registers, optionally with QSA along a data-tempering path.
mechanism: The same Chebyshev/√δ gap mechanism as QM-01, applied in a regime designed to escape H-002. The data add per-target information, so the endpoint can move. Multimodality comes from assignment combinatorics (discrete switches correlated through the structure), which could be a first-order-like or persistence regime where tempering is torpid (Bhatnagar–Randall [E40]; Woodard et al. [E39]).
oracle_and_state_prep: Walk oracle over structure plus assignment registers. The restraint term costs #restraints × #candidates distance evaluations (~L·4·3×10^3 ≈ 10^6 Toffolis at L=100), plus the esmprior energy (QM-05). Start state: product prior × uniform assignments. The QM-05 break-even still applies, needing K ≥ 10^10 per sample.
strongest_classical_competitor: ARIA/CYANA/Xplor-NIH ambiguous-distance restraints (r^-6 sums smooth the discrete ambiguity) with simulated annealing; Rosetta or AF2-class models with restraints; PT/Gibbs over assignments; SMC over data tempering.
information_vs_computation: This is the only card where information comes from outside ESM-2 (experiment, new and per-target), so the information limit is lifted by design. The quantum part is still pure computation on classical data.
relation_to_S29_S33: OLD MECHANISM: every S29–S33 architecture consumed only sequence-derived inputs (I-1…I-6). OLD FAILURE: information-limited; K-012/DNR-16 require a new information source. NEW MECHANISM: an explicit new information source (experimental restraints) turns the endpoint into a computational decoding problem over a mixed discrete-continuous posterior. WHY OLD CONTROL NO LONGER APPLIES: DNR-16's condition, new information, is met. Leakage: simulated data derived from natives must be labelled SIM-DATA and never mixed with DEP results. Real deposited restraint sets (e.g. BMRB) are the clean route.
kill_result: Any one of: classical ambiguous-restraint smoothing plus annealing reaches the PT-converged joint-posterior accuracy within ≤10^7 evaluations at every restraint density above the identifiability threshold; joint PT mixing grows with L and ambiguity only as a low-degree polynomial; or wherever mixing is hard, the data are too weak to identify the fold (no transmission).
minimal_classical_first_test: SIM-DATA benchmark on long40. Generate sparse ambiguous restraints from natives (0.5–1 restraint/residue, 2–4 candidate assignments, 10–20% outliers) and build π(x, a) ∝ head prior × esmprior × restraint likelihood. Run (i) an ARIA-style r^-6 ambiguous anneal and (ii) joint PT with Gibbs assignment moves, 4 seeds each. Measure accuracy against evaluations, assignment-flip rates and round trips, against L and ambiguity level. ≤1 day on 8 cores.
track: E hybrid (B fault-tolerant for the sampler)
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low. Mature classical methods smooth assignment ambiguity into a continuous energy, but the torpid-mixing question in this regime has never been measured, and it is the only regime where the information limit is lifted.
classical_primitive_replaced: The mixing phase of joint assignment/structure sampling.
expected_speedup: Quadratic in the joint chain's gap.
measurement_readout: Measure structure and assignment registers (one joint sample per anneal); classical refinement and posterior averaging follow.
prior_art_known: Bhatnagar–Randall J. Stat. Phys. 164:495 (2016), arXiv:1508.04521 [E40]; Woodard et al. EJP 14:780 [E39] (verified in repo). ARIA/CYANA ambiguous-restraint methodology (Nilges; Güntert): standard, but citations not verified in this session (UNVERIFIED). Within the repo corpus the search found no evidence of a quantum sampler proposed for ambiguous-restraint structure determination.
representation: (θ,τ) or Cartesian CA grid plus discrete assignment registers (log2 of the candidate count per restraint).
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: r^-6 ambiguous restraints (smoothing), AF2-class models conditioned on restraints, and Gibbs/PT over assignments.

title: QM-13 Super-quadratic planted-inference primitives (quantum Kikuchi / tensor PCA / DQI) for restraint-based structure inference
protein_question: Does inferring structure from sparse noisy restraints have a statistical–computational gap of the algebraic planted type (information present but classically hard to extract) where a nearly quartic quantum speedup is known?
quantum_primitive: Quantum Kikuchi method for planted inference (Schmidhuber et al. PRX 15 021077, arXiv:2406.19378 [C71]); tensor PCA (Hastings arXiv:1907.12724 [C72]); Decoded Quantum Interferometry (Jordan et al. Nature 646:831, arXiv:2408.08292).
mechanism: The level-ℓ Kikuchi matrix has dimension ~n^ℓ, and classical power iteration pays ~n^ℓ. Quantumly, a guiding state has unusually large overlap with the planted eigenvector because of the planted algebraic structure. Amplitude amplification of that overlap, combined with phase estimation on the sparse Kikuchi matrix, yields a nearly quartic gain (the square of a square). DQI uses a quantum Fourier transform to turn an optimisation problem into a classical decoding problem, which needs algebraic structure. Both require parity/GF(q) constraint structure.
oracle_and_state_prep: Sparse access to a Kikuchi or DQI matrix exists only for parity-type (k-XOR) or algebraic constraints. Distance restraints are real-valued geometric constraints, so no such oracle exists without a reduction. The mismatch erases the speedup unless a reduction is found.
strongest_classical_competitor: SDP and spectral Euclidean-distance-matrix completion, MDS, ARIA/CYANA, and AF2-class priors with restraints.
information_vs_computation: This is the one primitive class built for 'information present but hard to extract'. The program measured the opposite (information-limited) for sequence-only inputs. It becomes relevant only in QM-12's data-supplied formulation.
relation_to_S29_S33: OLD MECHANISM: M12 in the opportunity matrix (WEAK), never built. OLD FAILURE: the endpoint lacked the information, so the planted regime did not exist. NEW MECHANISM: pairs with QM-12's formulation, where data supply the information. WHY OLD CONTROL NO LONGER APPLIES: absent information is no longer the objection. The new obstacle is algebraic mismatch (geometric vs parity constraints) and whether a statistical–computational gap exists at all.
kill_result: (Theory) no reduction from restraint/EDM inference to planted k-XOR or tensor PCA that preserves the hard regime. (Classical) no statistical–computational gap: in simulation, spectral/SDP distance geometry recovers the fold wherever exhaustive posterior sampling does.
minimal_classical_first_test: SIM-DATA at 30–60 aa. Sweep restraint density × noise, and compare PT-posterior recovery (a proxy for the information-theoretic threshold) with SDP/spectral EDM completion + refinement. Look for a density band where PT succeeds and every polynomial method fails. ≤1 day. Plus a 2-page attempted reduction.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low. Geometric distance constraints lack the parity algebra the quartic speedup needs, and EDM completion is classically polynomial near its thresholds.
classical_primitive_replaced: Classical Kikuchi/spectral hierarchy in the hard regime (if one exists).
expected_speedup: Nearly quartic only if a planted k-XOR/tensor-PCA reduction exists; otherwise none is known.
measurement_readout: Phase estimation projects onto the planted eigenvector, and rounding gives restraint assignments or structure.
prior_art_known: arXiv:2406.19378, arXiv:1907.12724, arXiv:2408.08292, Hastings short-path arXiv:1802.10124 (verified in repo). Within the repo corpus the search found no evidence of any application of planted-inference quantum speedups to molecular structure inference.
representation: Restraint graph (sparse noisy distances plus assignment ambiguity) and a Gram/EDM matrix.
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: SDP/spectral EDM completion; AF2-class models conditioned on restraints.

title: QM-14 Quantum distribution-property testing for certifying ensemble convergence
protein_question: Can we certify that a sampled structure ensemble (feeding the soft readout) has converged, i.e. TV/Hellinger-close between independent chains or to the target, using quadratically fewer samples than classical tests?
quantum_primitive: Quantum closeness and identity testing with purified (qsample) access (Bravyi–Harrow–Hassidim arXiv:0907.3920; Gilyén–Li arXiv:1902.00814; both UNVERIFIED in repo), via amplitude estimation of fidelity/overlap between purifications.
mechanism: Given unitaries that prepare purifications Σ√p(x)|x⟩|φ_x⟩, a swap/Hadamard test combined with amplitude estimation estimates overlaps with O(1/ε) queries vs Θ(1/ε²) classical samples. For large supports, testers are also sublinear in support size. Interference measures overlaps directly.
oracle_and_state_prep: Purified access to each ensemble is a coherent sampler, which is QM-01's unsolved problem. A classical sample stream cannot be turned into purified access without QRAM, and once the samples are held classically there is nothing left to speed up. The access model erases the speedup.
strongest_classical_competitor: Two-sample tests on coarse-grained basin labels (with K ≤ 100 basins, ~√K/ε² samples is trivially cheap); cross-seed basin-population disagreement; R-hat. Woodard et al. warn that diagnostics can miss torpid mixing because unvisited mass is invisible.
information_vs_computation: The failure mode of non-convergence is bias (basins never reached), not the statistical sample complexity of testing. No tester detects mass its sampler never reaches.
relation_to_S29_S33: OLD MECHANISM: none directly. It parallels the killed amplitude-estimation line (QA-1/C-3). OLD FAILURE: variance was not binding (bias/information-limited). NEW MECHANISM: property testing of distributions rather than mean estimation. WHY OLD CONTROL NO LONGER APPLIES: it still applies. The binding error is bias, which testers cannot see.
kill_result: (Theory) torpid-mixing failures are invisible to any tester given the same sampler access. (Classical) coarse-grained classical tests reach decision-level confidence with ≤10^3 samples on the QM-01 runs.
minimal_classical_first_test: On QM-01 PT outputs, compute cross-run TV between basin populations with bootstrap CIs, and the sample count at which convergence decisions stabilise. Compare against an ORACLE-labelled long-run reference. ~2 h of analysis.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low (near-certain kill). The binding error is unvisited mass (bias), not the sample complexity of testing.
classical_primitive_replaced: Convergence diagnostics and two-sample tests.
expected_speedup: Quadratic in 1/ε under purified access only.
measurement_readout: Ancilla of the swap/Hadamard test plus AE gives an overlap estimate.
prior_art_known: Bravyi, Harrow, Hassidim, IEEE TIT (2011), arXiv:0907.3920 (UNVERIFIED in repo); Gilyén, Li, ITCS 2020, arXiv:1902.00814 (UNVERIFIED); Woodard–Schmidler–Huber EJP 14:780 (verified in repo); Grossfield et al. LiveCoMS 1 5067 (verified in repo).
representation: Coarse-grained basin labels, or grid registers under purified access.
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: Classical coarse-grained tests and cross-seed agreement.

title: Consumption-factoring theorem with per-primitive quadratic ceilings (generalised H-001), with the GHV/LWWZ exception made explicit
protein_question: Suppose a structure pipeline uses a quantum stage's output only through argmin, an energy-ordered prefix or tail, a convex functional of an E-shaped distribution, or the expectation of a fixed observable. Can that stage ever be load-bearing by more than a quadratic factor? Which access models allow more?
quantum_primitive: Any quantum algorithm with three kinds of access: (i) a coherent value or derivative oracle O_E for a classical (diagonal) learned energy, (ii) a walk oracle W(P) for a local reversible chain, (iii) a prior-state preparation U_0. This covers Durr-Hoyer, amplitude amplification, Szegedy walks and QSA, quantum rejection sampling, QAE and CVaR-VQE/QAOA.
speedup_type: none-known (a no-go. Each primitive's ceiling is query, walk-steps or precision, at most quadratic in its access model. GHV/LWWZ is the explicit query-model exception.)
strongest_classical_competitor: Exact sort, closed-form p*, SA, greedy or PT at equal tuning (the S33 twins), plus random-prior sampling (DNR-06).
information_vs_computation: The information is fixed by E (esmprior_v1/A80). The quantum stage cannot add information (data processing). The factoring lemma shows its only possible contribution is the computational cost of Prim(E), and that cost is capped per primitive.
relation_to_S29_S33: Generalises DNR-02, R1-R4 and R9, and K-001/002/004/011; it is the concrete form of H-009/T1. OLD MECHANISM: CVaR-VQE on diagonal costs. OLD FAILURE: reproduced by sort, p* or SA. NEW: the result extends from the deployed CVaR family to every algorithm in the access model (walks, QAE, rejection sampling) and adds the composition lemma. The GHV/LWWZ exception is new relative to the literature phase. That phase's 'at most quadratic' statement is a bibliographic observation about protein-applied work, not a theorem.
kill_result: Either of these kills it: a QX record or matrix row with a type (a)-(d) consumer that shows a resource-normalised super-quadratic gain; or a proof that a protein-realistic energy family embeds GHV-type structure. The second would turn card 8 positive rather than refute the lemma.
minimal_classical_first_test:
A paper exercise, under 1 day with no compute:
1. Encode the 16 opportunity-matrix rows and the 33 QX experiments as (consumer type, primitive, access model) triples and check coverage.
2. Sanity-check the composition lemma on two toy nested pipelines (SMC with inner MC estimation), using exact enumeration on at most 2^16 states.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low. This is a no-go card. The chance the no-go holds as scoped (with the LWWZ exception) is high: steps 2-4 are proven results and step 1 is bookkeeping over R1-R4.
expected_speedup: None (a no-go). Target claim level: L6 for the ceiling (explicit access model), L0 for the screening rule.
representation: Any register or continuous representation with a diagonal classical energy.
measurement_readout: argmin, E-ordered tail, convex functional or fixed-observable expectation.
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: Closed-form p*, sort and exact Gibbs sums already reproduce every S29-S33 instance.

title: Readout-specific mixing gate: what matters for a quantum sampler is the slow-mode gap the soft readout actually sees (delta_f) and the Bayes-risk headroom H(B), not the global gap
protein_question: The posterior-mean (soft) structure readout gave the only positive S33 signal. How much built-chain accuracy can ANY faster sampler, classical or quantum, still buy at a given budget? And does that readout even see the posterior's slow modes?
quantum_primitive: Walk-based mean estimation (Montanaro-type QMC on a QSA-prepared qsample); quantum RELD sampling [A44].
mechanism:
GATE / NO-GO (theory plus classical measurement).
Setup. For a reversible P with eigenpairs (lambda_k, phi_k), expand the readout as f = sum c_k phi_k.
Classical cost. After t steps the bias is at most sum_k |c_k| |<mu0/pi, phi_k>| lambda_k^t. The autocorrelation time is tau_int(f) = sum_k (c_k^2/sigma_f^2)(1+lambda_k)/(1-lambda_k). Define delta_f(eta) = min{1-lambda_k : |c_k| >= eta sigma_f}. Classical cost is then O~(1/delta_f + tau_f sigma_f^2/eps^2).
Quantum cost. Walk-based estimation prepares |sqrt(pi)> and pays the GLOBAL gap: O~(sigma_f/(eps sqrt(delta))) walk steps plus the anneal.
Consequences.
(i) If delta_f >> delta, the slow mode is invisible to the readout, and classical wins however small delta is. Example: a slow mode that swaps mirror or symmetric states with the same aligned mean.
(ii) The accuracy value of any speedup is bounded by H(B) = RMSD(readout at classical budget B) - RMSD(readout under exact pi). If H at a feasible B is about 0, the posterior itself is the bottleneck (information-limited in the Bayes sense), even when pi is hard to sample.
The proof is spectral decomposition plus the triangle inequality. The new part is making delta_f and H(B) the pre-registered quantities for H-006, in place of global mixing.
oracle_and_state_prep: Same coherent O_E and anneal as card 1. The gate itself needs no quantum oracle.
strongest_classical_competitor: PT/REST2 + HMC, adaptive SMC, batch-means or MSM estimates of tau_f, and exact enumeration where available.
information_vs_computation: H(infinity), the readout under exact pi, is set by esmprior information. H(B) - H(infinity) is the only computational headroom. The quantum part can address at most that, and at most quadratically in delta_f.
relation_to_S29_S33: S33 Q-C18 (soft beats hard, 1.40x MDE) was an exact enumerated sum. It measured the value of pi (H(infinity) vs argmin), not H(B). DNR-10's reopening condition ('measured MCMC mixing failure on the target distribution') is sharpened to 'failure on the readout functional'. There is no new quantum mechanism here: this is the gate that decides whether cards 3, 4, 5 and 10 can matter for the endpoint.
kill_result:
Quantum relevance is killed if either holds on mid30/long40:
- the sampled soft readout at <=1e7 energy evaluations per target lands within 0.3x MDE of a 1e9-evaluation (or exact-register) reference;
- spectral projection shows delta_f/delta >= 100.
Continue only if H at a feasible budget is >= 1x MDE with delta_f close to delta.
minimal_classical_first_test:
10 mid30 + 10 long40 targets, A80 energy at the S33 soft-readout temperature.
1. Run PT (16 replicas, 8 cores) at budgets of 1e5-1e8 energy evaluations and record soft-readout RMSD vs budget (the H(B) curve). Use the S33 enumerated register as the exact reference where it exists.
2. Build an MSM (TICA + 200-state k-means) on pooled trajectories to get delta.
3. Project the aligned mean coordinates onto the 5 slowest eigenvectors to get delta_f.
About 10-20 CPU-hours.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low. At <=60 aa the readout probably converges at modest budgets (R10 restart saturation, funnelled landscapes). Unknown at >=100 aa.
prior_art_known: Montanaro [A30/B12]; Leng et al. PNAS 2026 [A44]; Machta [E33]. The spectral tau_int formula is textbook MCMC (specific citation UNVERIFIED). Under scope 'repo bibliography + this session', the search found no evidence of a paper framing quantum sampling advantage through readout-specific slow-mode overlap for protein posteriors.
expected_speedup: None by itself. It bounds any sampler's accuracy benefit by H(B), with speedup at most quadratic in delta_f. Claim level L0/L1 gate.
measurement_readout: Soft (Boltzmann-weighted) posterior-mean structure, built-chain CA RMSD.
classical_primitive_replaced: PT/SMC sampling for the soft readout.

title: Quantum walk vs every classical lift of the same chain: the advantage ratio is Theta(sqrt(delta)/Phi), and the full quadratic survives only in the metastable (Cheeger-upper) regime
protein_question: When a local torsion or Cartesian chain on the learned-energy posterior is slow, can classical non-reversible lifting (directional drifts, lifted Metropolis, event-chain-type moves) recover the Szegedy walk's quadratic gain? In which landscape regime is that provably impossible?
quantum_primitive: Szegedy walk W(P) with phase-estimation reflections, or QSA [A1, A2, A8].
mechanism:
THEORY, derived here (I(prog)) from standard inequalities.
1. Cheeger: Phi^2/2 <= delta <= 2 Phi.
2. Any lift of P projects its ergodic flow onto P, so a lift cannot raise conductance on fibre unions. The bottleneck-ratio bound then gives t_mix(lift) >= 1/(4 Phi*(P)). This agrees with Chen-Lovasz-Pak's 'at most square root'.
3. The Szegedy phase gap is Theta(sqrt(delta)). With a warm-start path, walk-based reflection or preparation therefore costs O(1/sqrt(delta)), which is at most O(1/Phi) walk steps.
4. Hence T_lift/T_QW >= Omega(sqrt(delta)/Phi).
Two regimes follow:
- Diffusive (delta ~ Phi^2; rough but barrier-free funnels): the ratio is O(1), so lifts can match the walk. This agrees with Dervovic's lift-matches-walk result in the graph-mixing sense.
- Metastable (delta ~ Phi; one dominant bottleneck between basins): the ratio is Omega(delta^-1/2), so the full quadratic survives against every lift of that chain.
The quantum resource is interference in the reflection, which turns the spectral gap delta into a phase gap of order sqrt(delta). A lift cannot copy it because lifting cannot raise conductance.
Caveat: this compares chains one at a time. Changing the chain (PT, better moves) is a different adversary, covered in cards 5 and 10.
oracle_and_state_prep: Needs a coherent sqrt(P(x,y)): coherent Delta-E over O(L) pairs (Cartesian move) or O(L^2) pairs (torsion move), plus a Metropolis coin. The literature-phase I(agent) estimate is 1e6-1e8 Toffolis per step at L=100. The warm start comes from a QSA path (card 10). A cold start adds the sqrt(N) penalty [A9], which is fatal at protein-scale N.
strongest_classical_competitor: Lifted and non-reversible MCMC (Diaconis-Holmes-Neal [A15]; lifts [A14, A17]), and above that PT.
information_vs_computation: Pure computation on a fixed learned energy.
relation_to_S29_S33: S29-S33 never tested walks; this implements THEORY_ROADMAP T2c. OLD FAILURE: the Born machine lost to Metropolis (QX-29), on enumerable spaces. WHY THE OLD CONTROL NO LONGER APPLIES: the relevant control is now the best lift of the chain at non-enumerable sizes, and its power is set by Phi, not by whether the space can be enumerated.
minimal_classical_first_test:
long40 (44-60 aa) plus 4 native-free 80-120 aa sequences, A80 energy at the posterior temperature.
1. Run long local-torsion MCMC and HMC (8 cores, ~12 h).
2. Build an MSM with 200-500 microstates.
3. Take delta from the slowest implied timescale, and Phi as the minimum of flux/pi(S) over PCCA+ two-set partitions.
4. Report delta/Phi and delta/Phi^2 vs L, with bootstrap CIs.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low-medium. The metastable regime is plausible only where the learned posterior really has several basins, and even there the gain is quadratic and multiplied by R.
prior_art_known: Chen-Lovasz-Pak STOC 1999 [A14]; Apers-Ticozzi-Sarlette arXiv 1705.08253 [A17]; Apers-Sarlette-Ticozzi PRA 98:032115 [A16]; Dervovic arXiv 1712.02318 [A18]; Szegedy FOCS 2004 [A1]; Magniez et al. SIAM J Comput 2011 [A2]. The bottleneck-ratio theorem is from Levin-Peres-Wilmer, 'Markov Chains and Mixing Times' (theorem number UNVERIFIED). Under scope 'repo bibliography + this session', the search found no evidence of the walk-vs-lift ratio being stated as a regime diagnostic.
expected_speedup: At most quadratic in delta over any lift, and only when delta ~ Phi. Claim level L6 (derivation) plus L1 measurement.
representation: CA-trace (theta,tau) internal coordinates, or Cartesian CA.

title: Hide-and-seek on the backbone torus: does the Olivucci Omega(alpha) vs O~(sqrt(alpha)) separation survive when the energy is a white-box sum of pair terms? (DMDGP ceiling)
protein_question: Backbone dihedrals live on a torus T^(L-3). Can the only provable continuous-domain Gibbs-sampling separation be realised by protein-realistic learned energies there, given that those energies are white-box sums of 1-D pair tables?
quantum_primitive: QSVT singular-value thresholding plus temperature annealing on a Witten-Laplacian-type operator, with a gradient oracle [A45, A44].
mechanism:
What is known [A45]. On T^d with Gevrey potentials that hide a narrow deep well, every classical algorithm that queries values, gradients or any derivative needs Omega(alpha) queries, alpha = e^(beta*Delta). The quantum algorithm needs O~(sqrt(alpha)) gradient queries. The ratio reaches e^(Omega(d)) when log alpha = Omega(d). The lower bound is a QUERY property: the well's location is information the classical algorithm can obtain only by querying.
New analysis. For E = sum f_ij(d_ij) with tabulated f_ij, a narrow deep well whose mass is comparable to the broad basin needs many pair terms sitting in deep bins at the same time. Two cases:
(A) Each f_ij is unimodal and the sharp pairs form a globally rigid graph. Then distance geometry or EDM-SDP locates the well from the table minima in poly(L); this is exactly the predecessor's quantum-free E308/A80 decoder. A classical mode-jump or mixture-proposal sampler then faces no Omega(alpha) barrier, so white-box access dequantises the separation.
(B) The tables are k-modal (strand-register or topology ambiguity). Locating the well is then a Discretizable MDGP instance, which is NP-hard (Lavor et al. 2012). The best known classical method is branch-and-prune over a tree of size T; quantum backtracking gives O~(sqrt(T) poly) [C57]. That is again quadratic, now in the white-box setting.
Claim to prove: for white-box pair-additive energies on the backbone torus, the separation for locating or sampling hidden wells is at most max(quadratic in alpha, quadratic in T_BP), unless the hiding takes a form other than DMDGP.
oracle_and_state_prep: A coherent gradient oracle for O(L^2) spline pair terms, never costed; the literature I(agent) estimate is 1e6-1e8 Toffolis per call at L=100. Warm start by beta-annealing, O(beta^2 Delta^2) steps [A45]. Oracle cost multiplies the query separation without erasing it; white-box access in case A does erase it.
strongest_classical_competitor: DG/SDP mode enumeration from the table minima plus mode-jump or mixture-proposal MCMC; branch-and-prune for DMDGP; PT/SMC.
information_vs_computation: The pair tables are the information (esmprior). In case A that information makes the well classically findable. In case B the ambiguity is itself informational: the true posterior may spread over the 2^k DMDGP solutions, so computation helps only if the energy resolves the ambiguity.
relation_to_S29_S33: Not tested in S29-S33. Related quantum-free successes: the DG decoder E308 and A80; R10 restart saturation suggests case A at 44-60 aa. OLD FAILURE: register search on candidate sets (DNR-03/07). NEW MECHANISM: a provable continuous sampling separation. WHY THE OLD CONTROL NO LONGER APPLIES: H-001 covers how the output is consumed, not the cost of sampling a hidden well; the relevant control is now white-box mode enumeration, not SA on a register.
minimal_classical_first_test:
long40 plus 5 native-free 80-120 aa sequences, ~1 day on 8 cores:
1. Census the modality of each pair table (bins within 1 kT of the minimum) and count the sharp pairs.
2. Enumerate candidate modes by DG over top-1/top-2 bin choices for ambiguous sharp pairs, using bounded branch-and-prune (<=1e4 leaves).
3. Find modes by running PT (24 replicas) and clustering.
4. Measure how many PT modes the DG modes cover, the Laplace volume of each mode (Hessian log-det), and narrow/broad mass ratios.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low. Mostly unimodal learned pair terms put 44-60 aa in case A. Case B is plausible only for beta-register ambiguity at >=100 aa, and it is capped at quadratic anyway.
prior_art_known: Olivucci et al. arXiv 2608.24527 [A45]; this session confirmed on the abstract page that the lower bound covers value, gradient and higher-derivative queries on T^d. Leng et al. PNAS 2026 [A44]. Lavor-Liberti-Maculan-Mucherino, Comput. Optim. Appl. (2012), DOI 10.1007/s10589-011-9402-6 (listing checked: DMDGP is NP-hard, solved by branch-and-prune). Montanaro backtracking [C57]; Woodard et al. [E39]. Under scope 'repo bibliography + this session', the search found no evidence of a test of whether hide-and-seek separations survive white-box pair-additive energies.
expected_speedup: At most quadratic in alpha (black-box) or in the branch-and-prune tree size (white-box). Claim level L6 target for the ceiling.
representation: CA-trace internal coordinates: tau on T^(L-3), theta in an interval.

title: Cooperative (first-order-like) regime: a quadratic speedup of a stretched-exponential tempering cost, with an explicit fault-tolerant break-even length L*
protein_question: If a learned energy reproduces cooperative two-state folding at 100-300 aa, does tempering become torpid? At what length would quantised tempering (QSA or quantum RELD) pay after fault-tolerant overhead?
quantum_primitive: A quantum walk or QSA on a simulated-tempering or replica-exchange chain [A8, A31]; quantum RELD [A44].
mechanism:
At a first-order-like transition, tempering chains are torpid: the gap is at most e^(-Theta(DeltaF)), where DeltaF is the interfacial barrier. Rigorous for mean-field Potts [E40]; Neuhaus-Hager (2003) show multicanonical autocorrelation grows as e^DeltaF with DeltaF ~ L^(d-1) in lattice boxes. For a globule of L residues the nucleation interface scales as L^(2/3) (capillarity; the protein coefficient is UNVERIFIED).
A walk on the same chain costs gap^(-1/2) = e^(DeltaF/2). The quantum gain is only a square root, but of an exponential, so the absolute saving e^(DeltaF/2) grows exponentially in L^(2/3). This is the only asymptotic route around the 'quadratic does not pay on FT hardware' objection.
Break-even (I(prog)): quantum wins when R * e^(DeltaF/2) < e^DeltaF, i.e. DeltaF > 2 ln R. With DeltaF = sigma L^(2/3), L* = (2 ln R/sigma)^(3/2). For sigma = 1 kT that gives L* of about 180 (R=1e7) to 310 (R=1e10). At L* both costs are about R^2 classical-step equivalents (1e14-1e20 steps), so practical value needs a much smaller R.
A classical computer cannot copy the phase-gap amplification of the SAME chain; it can only change the chain. The decisive adversary is therefore an order-parameter method.
oracle_and_state_prep: Coherent O_E plus a tempering-index register and swap/coin arithmetic. The high-temperature warm start is cheap (close to a product state). Per-step ratio R is about 1e7-1e10.
strongest_classical_competitor: Umbrella sampling, metadynamics or 2-D Wang-Landau along a NATIVE-FREE order parameter: learned-Q (the fraction of esmprior-argmax contacts satisfied) and the energy. Also REST2 and population annealing. Neuhaus-Hager indicates that energy-only multicanonical sampling does not remove interfacial barriers, so the adversary must use a good reaction coordinate.
information_vs_computation: Cooperativity is a property of the learned energy (information); crossing the barrier is computation. Learned-Q uses only model outputs, never the native.
relation_to_S29_S33: S29-S33 never went beyond 60 aa and never measured tempering. OLD FAILURE: quadratic speedups at enumerable sizes (K-001 to K-008).
