NEW MECHANISM: an exponential-cost regime where a quadratic factor becomes an exponential absolute saving. WHY THE OLD CONTROL NO LONGER APPLIES: equal-tuning SA/PT twins were cheap at <=60 aa. Here the twin is torpid by assumption and has to be replaced by the reaction-coordinate adversary.
minimal_classical_first_test:
~1 day on 8 cores:
1. Run PT with 24-32 temperatures on the A80 energy at L = 30, 45, 60 (instrument targets) and L = 80, 100, 120 (native-free sequences), 3 sequences per length.
2. Measure energy histograms at the C_v peak, the Lee-Kosterlitz barrier vs L, C_max/L and round-trip times.
3. Run 1-D umbrella sampling in learned-Q at the peak temperature for two lengths.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low. Smooth pair-distance learned energies are unlikely to be strongly cooperative. If they are, learned-Q umbrella sampling probably restores polynomial round trips.
prior_art_known: Bhatnagar-Randall J Stat Phys 164:495 (2016) [E40]; Neuhaus-Hager J Stat Phys 113:47 (2003), arXiv cond-mat/0201324 (listing checked this session); Woodard et al. [E38, E39]; Machta [E33]; Leng et al. [A44]; Sanders et al. [A56]; Babbush et al. [A57]; Gutin-Abkevich-Shakhnovich [E6]. Finkelstein-type folding-barrier estimates DeltaF ~ N^(2/3) are UNVERIFIED. Under scope 'repo bibliography + this session', the search found no evidence of a break-even analysis of quantum tempering in the first-order regime for protein energies.
expected_speedup: A square root of e^(Theta(L^(2/3))). Absolute saving e^(DeltaF/2); break-even L* of about 180-310 aa if sigma is about 1 kT. Claim level L3/L4 target.
classical_primitive_replaced: Parallel or simulated tempering.

title: Treewidth/entanglement dequantisation of posterior qsamples: exact or truncated tensor-network samplers as the classical twin
protein_question: Can the discretised learned-energy posterior over residue torsions be sampled exactly, or nearly exactly, by tensor-network contraction? If so, any qsample-based quantum sampler (walk, QSA, Born-type) is redundant.
quantum_primitive: Any algorithm whose output is |sqrt(pi)> or samples from pi (QSA, quantum RELD, quantum rejection sampling).
mechanism:
NO-GO, as a sufficient condition (derivation I(prog) from standard ingredients). Discretise each residue to q states, so pi(x) ~ prod over edges ij of psi_ij(x_i,x_j).
(i) Drop pair terms whose log-potential range over the thermally accessible bins is below eps*kT; the TV cost is at most the sum of the dropped ranges. Call the remaining graph G_eps. Exact sampling and exact Z by variable elimination cost O(L q^(w+1)), where w = treewidth(G_eps).
(ii) Across any backbone cut, sqrt(pi) = F(x_A) G(x_B) times the product of sqrt(psi_ij) over edges crossing the cut. Its Schmidt rank is therefore at most q^min(|dA|,|dB|). So |sqrt(pi)> is an exact MPS with chi <= q^pw(G_eps), and Ferris-Vidal perfect sampling draws i.i.d. samples from it.
Consequence: a quantum qsample advantage needs q^(w_eff) to exceed classical budgets.
(iii) Worst case: 3-D contact graphs with bounded ply have O(L^(2/3)) separators (Miller-Teng-Thurston-Vavasis), so w = O(L^(2/3)). Exact contraction then fails at L >~ 60 for q >= 8 unless thresholding prunes the graph, and the remaining question is how accurate truncated-chi contraction is.
Whenever the state's entanglement is low, a classical computer copies the quantum state outright.
speedup_type: none-known (a no-go and sufficient condition for classical reproduction)
oracle_and_state_prep: No quantum oracle. Classical pair tables come from the esmprior soft bins.
strongest_classical_competitor: Exact junction-tree sampling, truncated boundary-MPS, and TN proposals inside MCMC (Christmann et al. [A50]).
information_vs_computation: The tables are information; contraction is computation.
relation_to_S29_S33: Generalises the S33 exact 262,144-state enumeration (QX-28/29, K-007, DNR-10): 'enumerable' becomes 'low effective treewidth'. OLD FAILURE: the Born machine vs exact/Metropolis on enumerable spaces. NEW: the same control extended to spaces that cannot be enumerated.
kill_result: Quantum stays relevant only if both hold: w_eff (eps = 0.1 kT) grows with L, and boundary-MPS at chi = 1024 misses the long-run PT soft readout by >=1x MDE at L >= 60. The no-go holds (quantum killed) if chi <= 256 matches PT within noise.
minimal_classical_first_test:
mid30/long40 targets, numpy on 8 cores, <=1 day:
1. Discretise tau to q = 8-12 bins and theta to 3 bins; build pair tables from esmprior soft bins.
2. Threshold at eps in {0.05, 0.1, 0.3} kT and compute min-fill treewidth vs L.
3. Where q^w <= 1e8, sample exactly with a junction tree; otherwise use a backbone-ordered boundary MPS with chi in {64, 256, 1024}.
4. Compare the samples and soft readouts with PT.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low for quantum advantage. The chance the no-go holds at <=60 aa is medium: low effective treewidth after thresholding is plausible.
prior_art_known: Checked this session: Ferris-Vidal PRB 85:165146 (2012), arXiv 1201.3974; Miller-Teng-Thurston-Vavasis J ACM 44:1-29 (1997) (listing); Verstraete-Wolf-Perez-Garcia-Cirac PRL 96:220601 (2006) (coherent Gibbs states as PEPS). Already in the bibliography: Christmann et al. PRA 111:042615 (2025) [A50]; Xu, tree-decomposition side-chain packing [C83]. Under scope 'repo bibliography + this session', the search found no evidence of a treewidth or entanglement study of learned protein posteriors.
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: This card IS the TN reproduction. Truncated TN samples can also serve as independence proposals with exact MH correction, which gives a consistent classical sampler.
expected_speedup: None if w_eff is small. Claim level L6 for the sufficient condition, L1 for the measurement.

title: Cheap-gradient dequantisation: quantum gradient estimation and value-query speedups vanish on differentiable learned energies
protein_question: Do quantum gradient-estimation speedups (Jordan; Gilyen-Arunachalam-Wiebe), or any speedup whose classical side uses value queries only, give an advantage on differentiable learned protein energies such as A80?
quantum_primitive: Jordan gradient estimation; the GAW smooth-gradient algorithm; value-query quantum optimisers.
mechanism:
NO-GO. Jordan (PRL 2005) needs one quantum query where a classical value-query method needs d+1; GAW (SODA 2019) improve the accuracy dependence quadratically for smooth functions.
But when E is given as an arithmetic circuit of size S (a torch graph), reverse-mode automatic differentiation returns the exact gradient in at most c*S operations. The constant c is small and independent of d (Baur-Strassen 1983, UNVERIFIED here); Hessian-vector products cost the same. The classical baseline therefore has gradient access at O(1) overhead, and any separation stated against value-only classical algorithms shrinks by at least d/c (d = 2L, about 100-300).
Only separations whose classical lower bound already allows derivative queries survive:
- Olivucci et al. [A45] allow derivatives of all orders, so that bound survives;
- Zhang-Li (ICML 2023) prove NO quantum speedup for finding eps-stationary points with p-th-order derivative oracles;
- the LWWZ 2025 continuous lower bound is stated for queries to f(.) and must be re-checked against derivative queries before any transfer (this feeds card 8).
A classical computer copies the gradient by backpropagation, which needs no superposition.
speedup_type: query (claimed d-fold; dequantised to O(1) in the white-box model)
oracle_and_state_prep: Jordan's algorithm needs a coherent value oracle with b-bit precision on a finite-difference grid. Each call costs about R = 1e7-1e10 times a classical evaluation, so even under the value-query framing the quantum side loses in wall-clock.
strongest_classical_competitor: Reverse-mode AD with L-BFGS or HMC (the A80 decoder itself).
information_vs_computation: No change in information; this is pure arithmetic cost.
relation_to_S29_S33: The A80 decoder is register-free autodiff L-BFGS and is restart-saturated (R10, DNR-07). S29-S33 has no analogue; this is a screen applied in advance to 'quantum gradient' proposals.
minimal_classical_first_test: Time cost(grad E)/cost(E) for A80 at L = 30, 60, 120 and 240 with batched torch on CPU; expect a constant 2-5. Compare with the d+1 count for finite differences. Minutes.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low. For energies that support autodiff the no-go is near-certain.
prior_art_known: Checked this session: Jordan PRL 95:050501 (2005), arXiv quant-ph/0405146; Gilyen-Arunachalam-Wiebe SODA 2019, arXiv 1711.00465; Zhang-Li ICML 2023, arXiv 2212.03906. UNVERIFIED: Baur-Strassen, Theor. Comput. Sci. 22:317 (1983); Griewank-Walther, 'Evaluating Derivatives'.
expected_speedup: O(1) after dequantisation. Claim level L6 (no-go).
classical_primitive_replaced: Gradient evaluation for decoding or sampling.

title: Transfer test for the only provable (sub)exponential separations on classical objectives (GHV to LWWZ QHD): explicit geometry and white-box pair energies
protein_question: The only provable super-quadratic quantum speedups for optimising a classical objective are oracle constructions: poly(n) vs exp(n^(1/5-o(1))) queries. Can any protein-realistic energy (explicit coordinates, chain connectivity, pair-additive smooth terms) realise them? Or is there a structural no-go?
quantum_primitive: A stoquastic adiabatic path (GHV) and Quantum Hamiltonian Descent H(t) = -Laplacian + t f + nu(t) g on a box domain (LWWZ).
mechanism:
What is known.
- GHV prove a poly-time quantum algorithm for EXIT-finding with an adjacency-list oracle, while every classical algorithm fails with exp(n^delta) queries, delta = 1/5 - o(1).
- LWWZ compile this into objective functions f: {0,1}^n -> [0,1] and into box-constrained continuous f. They get poly(n) quantum queries (adiabatic or QHD) vs exp(n^Omega(1)) classical queries, proven in the oracle model, which 'ignores the complexity of implementing f'.
- The quantum resource is coherent transport along a gapped path whose intermediate eigenstates spread over exponentially many vertices, where a classical walker gets lost.
Candidate NO-GO (new, conjectural):
(i) Explicit-naming lemma. With explicit coordinates and a known move group, hardness that comes from random vertex names in an adjacency oracle disappears: any neighbour can be computed and non-local proposals are free. The separation would then have to be carried entirely by the values of f.
(ii) Description-complexity barrier. f = sum f_ij(d_ij) with O(L^2) tables of B = 28 bins has a polynomial-size description. Hiding a GHV graph in f would require its values to act as a pseudo-random labelling. Conjecture: pair-additive energies on R^(3L) cannot do this without k-body terms whose k grows, or exponentially fine features.
Either outcome is new: a proof gives a scoped no-go; an explicit embedding gives a positive L6 result for a protein-shaped class. The search found no evidence of either (scope: this session).
speedup_type: query ((sub)exponential in the oracle model; unknown in the white-box model)
oracle_and_state_prep: LWWZ assume a black-box f. A white-box version needs a circuit that keeps the hidden structure hidden (cryptographic-like), and learned pair tables contain nothing like that. The oracle assumption is exactly what may erase the protein relevance.
strongest_classical_competitor: Any classical algorithm that can read the tables: DG/SDP, branch-and-prune, message passing on the contact graph, PT. Also SQA/PIMC: Crosson-Harrow show SQA can be exponentially faster than SA on spike instances, so classical simulation of stoquastic paths is a real adversary.
information_vs_computation: In GHV/LWWZ the instance hides information (the graph) from classical queries, and quantum interference exploits it. Learned energies expose their information in their own description, so any separation here would have to be computational, not informational.
relation_to_S29_S33: S29 lane X (a transverse-field mixer) was killed as DNR-11; its reopening condition is 'non-commuting terms that encode problem information'. GHV/LWWZ paths are problem-informed, gapped and non-local. OLD MECHANISM: a generic mixer on <=24 qubits. NEW MECHANISM: a provable stoquastic-path separation. WHY THE OLD CONTROL NO LONGER APPLIES: DNR-11's control (the BESTOFN tie) tested a mixer carrying no problem information.
minimal_classical_first_test:
A paper exercise plus small numerics, <=1 day:
1. Extract from LWWZ's continuous construction the structural requirements on f: body order, Lipschitz/Gevrey constants, number and arrangement of minima, dimension scaling.
2. Compute the same quantities for the A80/esmprior energy at L = 60 (Lipschitz and curvature bounds from the tables via autodiff).
A single incompatible requirement gives a scoped no-go for this energy class.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low. The constructions are highly contrived. Even so, this is the most important open theory question for the program: it is the only known route past the quadratic ceiling for classical energies.
expected_speedup: (Sub)exponential only if the transfer succeeds, which has a low prior. Claim level L6 either way (no-go or embedding).
representation: Continuous CA-trace or torsion coordinates on a box or torus.

title: Tunnelling through tall thin barriers (QHD / quantum Langevin) vs soft-core Hamiltonian replica exchange and path-integral Monte Carlo
protein_question: Do learned protein energies contain tall but thin barriers (for example chain crossing through soft sterics), where coherent tunnelling beats thermal activation? Does classical soft-core replica exchange already remove them?
quantum_primitive: Quantum Hamiltonian Descent or Schrodinger-operator evolution on d = 2L dihedral registers; quantum Langevin.
speedup_type: none-known (a heuristic tunnelling-rate mechanism; no protein-relevant proof)
oracle_and_state_prep: A coherent value oracle on a grid of b bits per dihedral (d*b qubits, about 1e3-1e4 for L = 100, b = 16), plus Schrodinger evolution. Per-step cost R.
strongest_classical_competitor: Soft-core HREX, pivot moves, SQA/PIMC, PT.
information_vs_computation: The energy sets the barrier geometry (information); crossing is computation.
relation_to_S29_S33: S29 lane X, a transverse-field mixer (DNR-11, QX-04), is the discrete analogue; it was killed on enumerable spaces without barrier measurements. NEW: continuous tunnelling with measured barrier geometry. S33's random-prior sampler avoided topology traps (SP-2), which suggests non-local classical proposals already bypass these barriers.
minimal_classical_first_test:
long40 targets, <=1 day:
1. Find basins by PT clustering.
2. Compute minimum-energy paths between basins by nudged elastic band on the A80 energy (torch autodiff).
3. Extract Delta and w (FWHM) for each barrier, and split Delta-E into steric and pair-distance contributions.
4. Compare round-trip times of 8-replica soft-core HREX against plain PT.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low
prior_art_known: Checked this session: Leng-Hickman-Li-Wu arXiv 2303.01471 (QHD); Leng-Zheng-Wu arXiv 2311.00811 (classical hardness only empirical); Crosson-Harrow FOCS 2016, arXiv 1601.03030. Already in the bibliography: Isakov et al. PRL 117:180402 (2016) [A64]; Denchev et al. PRX 6:031015 (2016) [C40].

title: QSA vs SMC from the exactly loadable (theta,tau) product prior: the stage count is the same, and the only gain is at most quadratic per stage
protein_question: Start from the esmprior per-residue (theta,tau) product prior, the only warm start that can be loaded exactly and cheaply. How many annealing stages does it take to reach the full pair-energy posterior? Can quantum simulated annealing gain anything over classical SMC beyond quadratic per-stage mixing?
quantum_primitive: QSA along a tempering path [A7, A8, A31], with exact product-state preparation.
mechanism:
State preparation is honest. p0 = prod_i h_i(theta_i, tau_i) is a product of 1-D laws, so |sqrt(p0)> needs O(L) controlled rotations (Grover-Rudolph is efficient for products). The path is pi_k ~ p0 e^(-beta_k E_pair).
QSA needs consecutive Bhattacharyya overlaps BC_k = Omega(1). SMC needs incremental chi^2_k = O(1).
Lemma (I(prog)): the map r -> E_p[w^r], with w = q/p, is log-convex, which gives BC >= (1+chi^2)^(-1/2). So SMC's condition implies QSA's.
For tempering increments Delta-beta with sub-Gaussian energy fluctuations, ln BC is about -Delta-beta^2 Var(E)/8 and ln(1+chi^2) is about Delta-beta^2 Var(E). Both therefore need K = Theta(sqrt(Var E) * total Delta-beta) stages.
Consequences:
- the stage count gives no separation;
- the whole separation is sum_k delta_k^(-1/2) (quantum) vs sum_k tau_k * particles (classical), at most quadratic per stage;
- SMC's particles are embarrassingly parallel, while QSA returns one sample per anneal (no cloning).
The only stage-count loophole is heavy-tailed increments (chi^2 infinite while BC = Omega(1)), and that is measurable.
oracle_and_state_prep: Coherent Delta-E_pair per move plus a Metropolis coin (R about 1e7-1e10). Preparing the product state is cheap and legitimate; it is not a free state prep.
strongest_classical_competitor: Adaptive tempered SMC with HMC rejuvenation (Del Moral-Doucet-Jasra [E74]); AIS [E75].
information_vs_computation: The prior and the pair energy are both esmprior information; the annealing path is computation.
relation_to_S29_S33: The product prior is exactly the 'random prior sampling' that beat VQE (QX-25, K-006, DNR-06). OLD FAILURE: register argmin on top of that prior. NEW: sampling along a path from the same prior, with explicit quantum-vs-SMC accounting. There is no register, so DNR-05/06/07 do not apply.
kill_result: Killed if both hold: per-stage rejuvenation tau_k <= 1e3 steps at every L <= 120 (so the quadratic gain is at most ~30x per stage, far below R), and no heavy-tailed increments (chi^2 finite at every stage).
minimal_classical_first_test: Adaptive tempered SMC (1,000 particles, ESS-triggered steps, HMC rejuvenation) from the product prior to the A80 posterior. Run on mid30, long40 and two native-free 100 aa sequences. Record K(L), per-stage BC and chi^2 from the weights, per-stage tau_int, log Z, and the soft-readout RMSD (transmission). <=1 day on 8 cores.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low
prior_art_known: Wocjan-Abeyesinghe PRA 78:042336 (2008) [A7]; Somma et al. PRL 101:130504 (2008) [A8]; Harrow-Wei SODA 2020 [A31]; Orsucci-Briegel-Dunjko [A9] (cold-start penalty); Grover-Rudolph [B36]; Herbert [B37]; Del Moral-Doucet-Jasra [E74]. Under scope 'repo bibliography + this session', the search found no evidence of a stage-count comparison between QSA overlap conditions and SMC ESS conditions.
expected_speedup: At most quadratic in per-stage mixing, with no stage-count gain. Claim level L6 (lemma) plus L1 measurement.
classical_primitive_replaced: SMC/AIS from a learned prior.
representation: CA-trace (theta,tau), product prior from the esmprior head.

title: Splitting lemma: whenever a classically computable progress coordinate exists, quantum hitting-time speedups for finding rare events and native-like basins vanish asymptotically
protein_question: To find rare, low-probability native-like basins or transitions under a learned energy, can quantum-walk hitting or search (sqrt(HT)) beat classical multilevel splitting driven by native-free progress coordinates?
quantum_primitive: MNRS, Krovi or AGJK quantum-walk search and hitting [A2-A4]; nested amplitude amplification.
mechanism:
NO-GO lemma (an I(prog) framing of known results). Let the target set A have probability p. Direct classical cost is about 1/p; quantum-walk hitting is about p^(-1/2), a quadratic gain.
With a coordinate aligned to the committor, adaptive multilevel splitting has relative variance about log(1/p)/N (Cerou-Guyader and follow-ups). Its cost is polylog(1/p)/eps^2, exponentially better than p^(-1/2).
With n imperfect interfaces with conditional probabilities p_i (product = p), classical cost is sum_i 1/p_i. The best quantum analogue, amplification per interface, costs sum_i p_i^(-1/2). That is at most quadratic per interface, with no asymptotic gain when p_i = Theta(1).
A quantum rare-event advantage therefore requires that NO classically computable coordinate gives Theta(1) interface probabilities, which is exactly the hide-and-seek regime of card 4. Classical splitting captures the rare event by breaking it into steps that are not rare, leaving the quantum walk nothing to accelerate.
speedup_type: query (hitting; at most quadratic per interface)
oracle_and_state_prep: A native-free marking predicate (E < E*, or learned-Q > q*), computed from the model with no native oracle. The coherent chain is as in card 3.
strongest_classical_competitor: Adaptive multilevel splitting, forward-flux sampling or weighted ensemble using learned-Q, energy or TICA coordinates; metadynamics.
information_vs_computation: The progress coordinates come from model outputs (information); splitting is computation.
relation_to_S29_S33: Matrix row M3 (WEAK); not tested in S29-S33. NEW: turns M3's qualitative 'WE/TPS remove the waiting-time exponential' into a checkable lemma with a native-free coordinate.
kill_result: Kills quantum relevance: FFS/AMS with learned-Q or energy reaches the lowest-energy basin found by long PT with every interface probability >= 0.05 and at most 20 interfaces, at 44-120 aa. Supports quantum: interface probabilities fall below 1e-4 for every native-free coordinate tried (energy, learned-Q, TICA, distance to the DG mode).
minimal_classical_first_test:
A80 energy, long40 plus 3 native-free 100 aa sequences, <=1 day:
1. Identify target basins by long PT.
2. Run AMS with each of the 4 coordinates.
3. Record per-interface probabilities, the variance of log p, and total cost vs L.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low
prior_art_known: Cerou-Guyader, Stoch. Anal. Appl. 25:417 (2007) (listing checked); Magniez et al. [A2]; Krovi et al. [A3]; Ambainis et al. [A4]; WE/TPS/milestoning [E60, E62-E64, E67].
expected_speedup: At most quadratic per interface; asymptotically none when a good coordinate exists. Claim level L6 (lemma).
classical_primitive_replaced: Rare-event and basin discovery by splitting or WE.

title: Planted-inference (Kikuchi) quartic speedup for structure determination from ambiguous restraints: the only super-quadratic family, tested where new information exists
protein_question: Is there a protein structure-determination task inside the statistical-computational gap of a planted noisy k-body problem, where the nearly quartic quantum speedup over the Kikuchi method would apply? Candidates: assigning ambiguous NOE or crosslink restraints, or detecting higher-order (3- and 4-body) coevolution.
quantum_primitive: Guided sparse-Hamiltonian phase estimation on the Kikuchi matrix (Schmidhuber-O'Donnell-Kothari-Babbush [C71]); Hastings tensor PCA [C72].
mechanism:
What is known. For planted noisy kXOR, a quantum algorithm using logarithmically many qubits is nearly quartically faster than the best known classical method (Kikuchi spectral). It uses a guiding state built from the input and phase estimation on a sparse Kikuchi matrix. The gain is relative to the best known classical algorithm, not a lower bound, and exists only between the spectral and information-theoretic thresholds.
Why it could fit here. This planted regime (information present but classically hard to extract) is the OPPOSITE of the predecessor's information-limited endpoint. It becomes the right regime once experimental restraints supply new information.
Mapping. One assignment variable per ambiguous restraint; geometric consistency induces k-body constraints.
Obstacle. kXOR hardness needs random sparse hypergraphs with independent noise. 3-D geometry imposes triangle inequalities and a low-dimensional embedding that DG/SDP exploit, which probably closes the gap.
speedup_type: query (nearly quartic vs the best known classical; not a proven separation)
oracle_and_state_prep: Sparse access to the explicit constraint hypergraph (cheap, from data) and a guiding state from the data, as in [C71]. No free oracle.
strongest_classical_competitor: Iterative assignment plus distance geometry (ARIA/CYANA-type; specific citations UNVERIFIED), SDP/EDM completion, and AMP or belief propagation for spiked tensors.
information_vs_computation: Experimental restraints are NEW information, which satisfies DNR-16's reopening condition. The quantum part only speeds up extracting it.
relation_to_S29_S33: Entirely outside S29-S33. DNR-16 (native-free ranking) requires a new information source, and this card uses experimental data as that source. H-002 (information-limited) does not apply by construction. Matrix row M12 was marked WEAK because the program lacked information; this card changes the information assumption, not the primitive.
kill_result: Build synthetic ambiguous-restraint benchmarks from long40 natives (2-5 candidate assignments per restraint, 10-30% noise). Killed if a polynomial classical method succeeds all the way down to the information-theoretic threshold, estimated by exhaustive or branch-and-prune search on <=25-residue segments. Then there is no statistical-computational gap and no Kikuchi regime.
minimal_classical_first_test:
<=1 day:
1. Generate ambiguous distance-restraint sets from 10 long40 natives. The natives are used only to synthesise data, never as an oracle.
2. Sweep the restraint count m and the ambiguity level.
3. Compare the success of iterative DG/SDP with exhaustive search on short segments.
4. Look for a window where brute force succeeds and polynomial methods fail.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low
prior_art_known: Schmidhuber et al. PRX 15:021077 (2025), arXiv 2406.19378 [C71]; Hastings, Quantum 4:237 (2020) [C72]. Under scope 'repo bibliography + this session', the search found no evidence of planted-inference speedups mapped to protein restraint assignment; the literature phase recorded this as gap G-9.
expected_speedup: Nearly quartic vs the best known classical, only inside a statistical-computational gap. Claim level L0.
representation: Discrete assignment variables per ambiguous restraint, plus continuous embedding.

title: Recasting the posterior as a ground state: stoquastic parent Hamiltonians are exactly classical Markov chains, black-box amplification stops at sqrt(delta), and whether non-stoquastic parents can do better is open
protein_question: Suppose protein structure inference is redesigned as preparing the ground state of a local Hamiltonian whose ground state is the coherent posterior |sqrt(pi)>, the most natural 'quantum-native' reformulation. Can that Hamiltonian's gap exceed what the best classical local chain gives?
quantum_primitive: Adiabatic or gap-amplified ground-state preparation of a parent Hamiltonian of |sqrt(pi)> [A8, A33]; guided phase estimation.
mechanism:
(i) For a reversible local chain P, H_P = I - D^(1/2) P D^(-1/2), with D = diag(pi), is local, stoquastic and frustration-free. Its ground state is |sqrt(pi)> and its gap is exactly delta(P), since it is similar to I - P.
(ii) The converse (via the Bravyi-Terhal similarity transform, I(prog) application). Take ANY stoquastic H with positive ground state psi, shifted to zero ground energy. Then G = -D_psi^(-1) H D_psi has non-negative off-diagonal entries and zero row sums. So G is a reversible generator with stationary law psi^2, the same locality and the same spectrum. The best gap over stoquastic parents therefore equals the fastest-mixing local reversible chain, which is an SDP (Boyd-Diaconis-Xiao). No advantage.
(iii) Somma-Boixo: quadratic gap amplification, delta -> sqrt(delta), is possible for frustration-free H and optimal in their black-box model.
(iv) Open and new: local non-stoquastic parents H' of |sqrt(pi)> with gap >> sqrt(delta*), built efficiently from the pair tables.
A classical computer reproduces (i)-(ii) exactly. Only (iv) could hold a quantum resource: sign structure, and hence interference, in the parent.
speedup_type: walk-steps (at most quadratic, proven for stoquastic parents and in the black-box model; unknown for non-stoquastic parents)
oracle_and_state_prep: A block encoding of H' needs the ratios sqrt(pi_x/pi_y), i.e. a coherent Delta-E (R about 1e7-1e10 per call). The guiding state comes from the product prior (card 10).
strongest_classical_competitor: The fastest-mixing local reversible chain (an SDP), and PT.
information_vs_computation: Same learned energy; purely computational.
relation_to_S29_S33: R12 (non-classicality needs non-commuting terms AND a prepared state that is not an eigenvector) is satisfied by design. OLD FAILURE: S29 lane X, a generic transverse field (DNR-11, QX-04). NEW MECHANISM: parent Hamiltonians derived from the problem. WHY THE OLD CONTROL NO LONGER APPLIES: a generic mixer carries no problem information, while H_P and its non-stoquastic deformations do. Point (ii) shows the stoquastic ones are classical anyway.
minimal_classical_first_test:
Discretised 6-8-residue chains (q = 3-4 torsion bins, <=4,096 states) with esmprior tables. cvxpy on CPU, a few hours:
1. Compute delta* with the FMMC SDP restricted to single-residue moves.
2. Solve the SDP: maximise lambda_2(H) subject to H|sqrt(pi)> = 0, H PSD, 2-local support and ||H|| <= 1, with and without the stoquastic sign constraint.
3. Report the non-stoquastic/stoquastic gap ratio vs size.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low
prior_art_known: Already in the bibliography: Somma-Boixo SIAM J Comput 42:593 (2013) [A33] (quadratic amplification optimal in the black-box model, confirmed from the arXiv abstract); Somma et al. PRL 101:130504 [A8]. Checked this session: Verstraete-Wolf-Perez-Garcia-Cirac PRL 96:220601 (2006); Bravyi-Terhal SIAM J Comput 39:1462 (2009), arXiv 0806.1746 (listing); Boyd-Diaconis-Xiao SIAM Rev 46:667 (2004) (listing); Hamoudi-Le Borgne-Sridhara arXiv 2602.23183 (abstract; its hardness concerns guided stoquastic graph Hamiltonians, not coherent classical Gibbs states).
expected_speedup: None for stoquastic parents, quadratic with amplification, unknown for non-stoquastic parents. Claim level L6 for (i)-(iii); (iv) is open at L0.
representation: Discretised torsion states; local parent Hamiltonian on the residue chain.

title: P1. Many-body 1H dipolar-network forward model for fast-MAS solid-state NMR of fully protonated proteins: quantitative long-range H-H distances past dipolar truncation
protein_question: In fully protonated proteins at >=100 kHz MAS, 1H-1H RFDR and spin-diffusion cross-peaks are turned into binned upper-bound restraints (Andreas et al. PNAS 2016) for two reasons: strong geminal and vicinal couplings (~20 kHz at 1.78 A) truncate weak long-range ones (~1 kHz at 5 A, ~0.2 kHz at 8 A), and transfer is relayed through many spins. If exact many-body simulation of the build-up curves could turn them into quantitative 5-8 A distances, it would supply exactly the per-target long-range pair information that S33 found missing at 44-150 aa.
quantum_primitive: Trotterised or qubitised Hamiltonian simulation of the MAS time-dependent (or rotor-synchronous average-Hamiltonian) homonuclear dipolar Hamiltonian on N 1H qubits. The high-temperature correlation S_ab(t)=Tr[I_z^a(t) I_z^b]/Tr[(I_z^b)^2] is estimated by a Hadamard test with one clean qubit (DQC1) or by random-product-state typicality.
mechanism: Resource: the 2^N-dimensional unitary propagation of the density-operator perturbation. A classical simulator must either store the 2^N state or truncate the Liouville space by spin order (LCL, LR-LCL) or Pauli weight. A quantum processor applies poly(N*t) gates. A classical computer can copy this whenever the transfer is effectively incoherent: z-magnetisation transport dominated by low spin-order operators, which gives hydrodynamic/rate-like dynamics. The quantum part can only be load-bearing if the mixing-time build-ups depend on coherent, high-spin-order operator components (weight > ~6) with non-sparse, sign-oscillating coefficients. The evidence says standard spin-diffusion/RFDR observables are NOT in that regime. LCL reproduced experimental 1H spin diffusion from crystal geometry (Dumez et al. 2010). LR-LCL scales linearly to thousands of spins under MAS with near-exact precision (Perras & Pruski 2019). spinDMFT matches experimental static spin diffusion (Graesser, Uhrig, Ernst 2026).
speedup_type: exponential-simulation (conditional; expected none for standard observables)
oracle_and_state_prep: Input: all-atom H coordinates of a candidate structure. Pair couplings D_ij ~ r^-3 P2(cos beta) are computed classically, O(N*k) with k~45 neighbours inside 6 A (1H density ~0.05/A^3). No free block encoding: every term is an explicit 2-qubit rotation. Initial state: the maximally mixed state plus I_z^a, prepared by random computational-basis states (typicality) or one clean qubit, at negligible cost. Powder averaging over 50-200 crystallite orientations and 20-50 Trotter slices per rotor period multiply cost by ~1e2-1e4 for classical and quantum alike. These overheads do not erase a speedup in principle, but they push each likelihood to FT scale.
strongest_classical_competitor: LR-LCL (Perras & Pruski, J. Chem. Phys. 151, 034110, 2019); LCL (Dumez et al., PCCP 12, 9172, 2010); spinDMFT (Graesser, Uhrig, Ernst, Sci. Adv. 12, eaee6228, 2026; arXiv 2512.15572); sparse Pauli dynamics (Begusic & Chan, PRX Quantum 6, 020302, 2025); phenomenological rate-matrix/ISPA fits plus CYANA with binned restraints; AF2/ESM priors.
information_vs_computation: Information comes from the experiment: per-target cross-peak intensities, a genuinely new source relative to esmprior_v1 (DNR-16). The quantum part adds only the forward model. The structurally valuable content (short and medium distances) is already extracted by classical rate models. The only increment the quantum part could supply is a correction for relayed and truncated coherent multi-spin transfer on the weak long-range couplings.
relation_to_S29_S33: OLD MECHANISM: argmin/prefix/convex readout of diagonal-energy distributions on enumerable candidate registers (H-001, DNR-02/03). NEW MECHANISM: non-commuting physical-spin Hamiltonian dynamics consumed through time-dependent expectation values. WHY OLD CONTROL NO LONGER APPLIES: the Hilbert space is 2^N physical spins, not a candidate index, so DNR-09's dimension counting does not bite. The right twin is a spin-dynamics simulator (LR-LCL, spinDMFT, Pauli propagation), not SA or random prior sampling. OLD FAILURE that transfers: condition C. Forward-model precision may not transmit to structure accuracy, just as register energies did not (within-target rho -0.08).
kill_result: Kill if either holds. (a) For protein-derived 1H clusters (N=12-20, exact), LR-LCL, sparse Pauli dynamics or a rate matrix reproduce the RFDR/spin-diffusion build-ups within 5% at all mixing times <=10 ms and recover 5-8 A distances with bias smaller than the noise-limited sigma at SNR 50. (b) The Fisher information on 5-8 A distances from the exact model exceeds that of the rate model by less than 10%.
minimal_classical_first_test: Download 1UBQ and 2GB1 from the PDB (ORACLE/analysis use only) and add H with OpenMM Modeller, which is installed. Select three probe pairs at 3, 5 and 7 A and build nested clusters of N=12, 16 and 20 nearest 1H. Simulate the zero-quantum recoupled (RFDR-like) Hamiltonian exactly with on-the-fly 2-qubit Trotter gates on 2^20 amplitudes (about 16 MB for the state) with typicality averaging, plus 20 powder orientations. Compare against (i) a rate matrix, (ii) truncated Pauli propagation with weight <=4 and <=6, and (iii) LCL with spin order <=4. Report the max deviation, the finite-difference Fisher information on the probe distances, and the bias of distances fitted with each classical model. Estimated cost: well under 1 day on 8 cores, under 2 GB RAM.
track: E hybrid (B fault-tolerant scale needed for N>=100 clusters)
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low: linear-scaling classical methods already match experiment for spin diffusion; the structure-bearing observables sit in the effectively incoherent regime.
classical_primitive_replaced: Low-order-correlation Liouville-space or rate-matrix simulation of 1H polarisation transfer inside NMR structure calculation
expected_speedup: None expected for standard observables. If a hard window exists: exponential in cluster size for exact simulation, but ~1e11-1e14 T gates per likelihood evaluation (N~100, ~45 neighbours/spin, 300-1000 Trotter steps, 20 mixing times, orientations, 1e2-1e4 shots). Rough, I(agent).
measurement_readout: S_ab(t_m) at 10-30 mixing times per pair to +-0.01: ~1e4 Hadamard-test shots per (time, orientation), or ~1e2 coherent repetitions with amplitude estimation.
prior_art_known: O'Brien, Ioffe, Su, Fushman, Neven, Babbush, Smelyanskiy, PRX Quantum 3, 030345 (2022), arXiv 2109.02163: aligned ubiquitin in membranes, learning 1H dipolar couplings; 466/238/60/8-spin clusters analysed, 6-spin learning demo. This is the closest prior art. It does not benchmark LR-LCL or Pauli propagation and does not quantify structural information beyond pairwise methods. Dumez et al. PCCP 2010; Perras & Pruski JCP 2019; Graesser, Uhrig, Ernst Sci. Adv. 2026; Andreas et al. PNAS 2016 (fully protonated protein structures at 100+ kHz MAS); Savostyanov, Dolgov, Kuprov PRB 90, 085139 (2014) (tensor-train NMR).
representation: All-atom coordinates, reduced to the 1H dipolar coupling graph (~8 H/residue; 60 aa is ~500 1H; local transfer clusters of 50-200 spins).
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: LR-LCL linear scaling to thousands of spins; spinDMFT; tensor-train Liouville propagation; a learned surrogate rate model trained on exact small-cluster data would likely suffice.

title: P2. Protein-scale many-body echo (OTOC / multiple-quantum-coherence) NMR experiments interpreted with a quantum-simulated forward model
protein_question: Can time-reversal echo experiments (OTOC / Loschmidt / MQC) on site-specifically 13C-labelled, oriented or microcrystalline protein samples give geometry information about protons 6-12 A from a labelled 'butterfly' site? Pairwise and spin-diffusion experiments cannot see these protons. Example uses are discriminating competing domain packings or side-chain arrangements in a 60-150 aa protein, provided the only adequate interpreter is a quantum simulation of the echo.
quantum_primitive: Hamiltonian simulation of forward and backward (echo) evolution under the geometry-derived dipolar Hamiltonian, estimating F(t)=Tr[W(t) V W(t) V]/2^N. This follows Zhang et al. 2025 (Willow: CZ + fSim gates, 9 and 15 qubits) scaled to 50-200 qubits, which requires FT qubitisation.
mechanism: Resource: evolution of an operator W(t) whose Pauli support spreads ballistically through the dense coupling graph. The echo signal is F = 1 - (1/2)||[W(t),V]||^2-type. It is therefore sensitive to whether operator paths starting at the perturbed spin reach the observable, which amplifies the effect of weak distant couplings that pairwise experiments truncate. In the scrambling regime the number of Pauli strings with non-negligible, sign-alternating coefficients grows exponentially in t times connectivity, so truncated Pauli propagation fails. TN with belief propagation cannot feasibly simulate Google's 65-qubit OTOC(2) (Bermejo et al. 2026). A quantum device runs the forward/backward circuits with poly(N*t) gates and never stores the operator. A classical computer cannot copy this only in the window where OTOCs are both geometry-sensitive and past the truncation-tractable operator weight. This is the only card in the lane where classical hardness is established for a closely related observable. The tension: late-time dipolar dynamics is universal and loses microscopic detail (Li et al., Nat. Phys. 2024). O'Brien et al. 2022 found learnability improves as ergodicity drops (multifractal-dimension drop), which is the classically easier side. See P3.
speedup_type: exponential-simulation (conditional on a hardness-and-identifiability window existing)
oracle_and_state_prep: The Hamiltonian is explicit from candidate coordinates as in P1, plus the known pulse-sequence scaling of the effective Hamiltonian (e.g. magic-echo sign reversal). No oracle is hidden. State: high-temperature mixed state, via typicality or one clean qubit. Sample geometry constrains everything. In solution, weakly aligned proteins (order parameter ~1e-3) have residual couplings of tens of Hz, too slow compared with protein T2, so the hard regime is unreachable. Proteins must be studied as solids: oriented membranes, microcrystals, or MAS with recoupling. Powders add 50-200 orientations. Protein motions (methyl rotation, water, backbone) add relaxation, so the forward model is a Lindbladian, and dissipation makes classical Pauli propagation easier (Schuster et al. PRX 2025). Costs are rough I(agent). N~100 with ~45 neighbours per spin gives ~2e3 pair terms, ~1e4 rotations per 2nd-order Trotter step and 300-1000 steps, times 4 evolutions per OTOC, for ~1e7-4e7 rotations and ~3e8-1e9 T gates per circuit. Times 20 time points and 1e2-1e4 shots (or amplitude-estimation repetitions), that is ~1e12-1e14 T per likelihood. This does not erase the speedup in principle, but it restricts use to fitting a handful of parameters.
strongest_classical_competitor: Several classical routes compete. Exact statevector with typicality up to ~30-35 spins. Pauli propagation / sparse Pauli dynamics with truncation (Begusic & Chan PRX Quantum 2025; Rudolph et al. PauliPropagation.jl, arXiv 2505.21606; Kemper et al. arXiv 2607.24924, real-time correlators). Noisy-circuit Pauli-path bounds (Schuster et al. PRX 15, 041018, 2025). Average-case Pauli propagation (Angrisani et al. PRL 135, 170602, 2025). spinDMFT; DAOE (UNVERIFIED citation). Or skip OTOCs entirely: sparse isotope labelling with DARR/PAR/REDOR, PREs, cryo-EM, AF2.
information_vs_computation: Information is new per-target experimental echo data. The quantum part only interprets it. It cannot create information absent from the data, and it is load-bearing only if (i) the echo data contain geometry information that pairwise experiments do not, and (ii) extracting it needs operator components beyond classical truncation. Condition (i) is chemistry and experiment; condition (ii) is computation.
relation_to_S29_S33: NEW MECHANISM relative to every S29-S33 kill: non-commuting dynamics, a non-diagonal readout, and a decision space (N spins, geometry) that grows with the target. This formally satisfies S32's P1 condition. WHY OLD CONTROL NO LONGER APPLIES: SA and random prior sampling are not twins here; the twin is the best truncated classical simulator. OLD FAILURE that transfers: 'apparent quantum wins disappearing under stronger classical controls'. Zhang et al. 2025 is logged in the literature phase as F34, 'NO ADVANTAGE (self-declared)'. This card extends it to proteins and adds the identifiability question.
kill_result: Kill if any holds. (i) On protein-derived clusters, less than 10% of the total Fisher information on the target long-range geometry parameters lives in the time window where weight-<=8 Pauli propagation deviates from exact by more than the noise. (ii) Realistic relaxation (T1rho/T2' of 1-10 ms against effective couplings) ends the coherent window before operator weight exceeds ~10-12. (iii) Powder or ensemble averaging brings the signal difference between competing structures below SNR 50.
minimal_classical_first_test: Use the P1 setup: 1UBQ/GB1 with OpenMM hydrogens, a 13C 'butterfly' at a chosen C-alpha, and N=12-20 nearest 1H plus 2-3 target protons at 6-10 A. Simulate the OTOC for one oriented crystal and a 20-orientation powder. Add phenomenological Lindblad dephasing, sampled via quantum trajectories, at gamma set by T1rho = 1, 3 and 10 ms. Compute finite-difference Fisher information for (a) a remote-H distance and (b) a fold-level perturbation (1 A rigid shift of a helix or strand; a chi1 rotamer swap). Compare with the Fisher information from the P1 build-up observable. Run truncated Pauli propagation at weights 4, 6 and 8 and locate the time where it fails. Report the Fisher information inside and outside the tractable window. Cost: 2^20 statevector, well under 1 day on 8 cores.
track: E hybrid (B fault-tolerant at scale; A NISQ only for <=20-spin demos already classically simulable)
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low (the best card in this lane): classical hardness is plausible in dense solids, but universality, relaxation and powder averaging likely erase structure-specific information in the hard window; the only demonstrations (8 and 14 H) are classically simulable.
classical_primitive_replaced: Classical OTOC/MQC simulation (exact up to ~30 spins; truncated Pauli propagation beyond) inside NMR-restrained structure inference
expected_speedup: Exponential in cluster size if a hard and identifiable window exists; practically ~1e12-1e14 T per likelihood (rough), so only for fitting <=10 geometric parameters on oriented samples.
measurement_readout: Hadamard-test estimate of the echo signal at ~20 echo times, precision ~0.01 (1e4 shots, or ~1e2 amplitude-estimation repetitions), per orientation.
prior_art_known: C. Zhang, Cortinas, Karamlou et al. (Google Quantum AI), 'Quantum computation of molecular geometry via many-body nuclear spin echoes', arXiv 2510.19550 (2025). Toluene (8 H, 9 qubits) and DMBP (14 H, 15 qubits) in a nematic LC; 'the classical hardness of OTOC simulation prevents scaling our structure learning protocol to larger systems'; names biomolecules and solid-state NMR as future directions. O'Brien et al. PRX Quantum 3, 030345 (2022). Google OTOC(2), Nature 646, 825 (2025). Bermejo et al. arXiv 2604.15427. Wei, Ramanathan, Cappellaro PRL 120, 070501 (2018). Sanchez et al. PRL 124, 030601 (2020) (Loschmidt echo in solids). Y. Li et al., 'Emergent universal quench dynamics in randomly interacting spin models', Nat. Phys. (2024), arXiv 2406.07625. Y.-C. Li et al., arXiv 2606.31827 (2026): scrambling correlates thousands of solid-state nuclear spins. Under this lane's scope, the search found no study of OTOC-type NMR on proteins.
representation: All-atom H coordinates plus a 13C label site, reduced to the dipolar graph restricted to a 50-200-spin neighbourhood; experiment-specific effective Hamiltonian.
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: Truncated Pauli propagation should reproduce short-time and strongly dissipative regimes; TN-BP fails for random-circuit OTOC(2) but is untested on dipolar protein networks. A neural emulator trained on quantum outputs would turn the quantum device into an offline data generator.

title: P3. Hardness-identifiability trade-off theorem for spin-dynamics structure learning (the physics-lane analogue of H-001)
protein_question: Is there any NMR observable of a protein-like dipolar network whose exact forward simulation is classically hard and whose hard component carries Fisher information about geometry beyond classically simulable observables? This gate decides P1, P2, P5 and P12 together.
quantum_primitive: None is built. The object of study is BQP Hamiltonian simulation (and DQC1 normalised-trace estimation, Knill & Laflamme PRL 81, 5672, 1998) against classical truncated Pauli / Liouville propagation under dissipation.
mechanism: Explicit structure: dO(t)/dD_ij = i * integral_0^t ds Tr(rho [h_ij(s), O(t)]), where h_ij is the pair term. Sensitivity to a distant coupling is therefore itself an OTOC-type commutator, non-zero only once the Heisenberg-evolved operator has spread onto the pair's support. Three claims are to be proved or refuted. (C3-a) With per-spin-order relaxation rate gamma, Pauli components of weight > w are damped by ~exp(-gamma*w*t), as in the noisy-circuit Pauli-path bounds of Schuster et al. 2025. Then the Fisher information carried by weight > w obeys FI_hard <= FI_total * exp(-2*gamma*w*t) + O(truncation error). (C3-b) In the ergodic regime, sensitivity to any single coupling is diluted over exponentially many paths (self-averaging; universality, Li et al. 2024). (C3-c) Fisher information therefore concentrates near the ergodic edge, where localisation lowers entanglement and classical simulability improves. If all three hold, the Fisher information a quantum forward model can uniquely unlock is bounded by f(gamma/J, graph) times the Fisher information available classically. That would be a structural negative result analogous to H-001/H-009.
speedup_type: none-known (theory gate; a positive region would imply exponential-simulation)
oracle_and_state_prep: Not applicable (analysis). Hamiltonians are explicit from coordinates and the state is the high-temperature mixed state, so no oracle assumptions are needed.
strongest_classical_competitor: Noisy Pauli-path simulation with provable error (Schuster, Yin, Gao et al., PRX 15, 041018, 2025); average-case Pauli propagation (Angrisani et al. PRL 135, 170602, 2025); LR-LCL; spinDMFT; exact small-cluster plus cluster-expansion corrections.
information_vs_computation: This card is the explicit separation: Fisher information measures whether the information exists in the data; operator weight and Pauli-string counts measure the classical cost of extracting it. The quantum part adds value only on the product of the two.
relation_to_S29_S33: OLD MECHANISM: H-001 (quantum output consumed via argmin/prefix/convex of a diagonal distribution is classically reproducible). NEW MECHANISM: the analogous screening statement for Hamiltonian-simulation forward models, 'a quantum forward model is load-bearing only if the Fisher information it unlocks lives in operator components beyond classical truncation'. This extends G4 (the generalised H-001 reduction theorem) to the physics lane. WHY OLD CONTROL NO LONGER APPLIES: diagonal-energy arguments say nothing about non-commuting dynamics, so a new screen is needed.
kill_result: The quantum-NMR family (P1, P2, P5, P12) is killed if a proof or numerical phase diagram shows FI_hard/FI_total < 0.1 for all realistic gamma/J (T1rho or T2' of 1-10 ms against 0.2-20 kHz couplings) on protein 1H networks. The opposite result promotes P2: a region with FI_hard/FI_total > 0.3 at operator weight > 12 and retained Pauli strings > 1e7.
minimal_classical_first_test: Take 50 random 12-20-spin clusters from 1UBQ/GB1 (OpenMM hydrogens). For each, run exact Heisenberg-picture evolution via statevector with typicality for three observables (autocorrelation, cross-transfer, OTOC) at gamma/J in {0, 0.01, 0.03, 0.1}. Compute the Fisher information for ~10 geometric parameters (distances, a rigid-body shift) and FI_w, the Fisher information reproduced by Pauli propagation truncated at weights 2-10, together with the number of retained strings. Deliverable: curves of FI_w/FI_exact against w and cost. Kill if FI_w >= 0.9*FI_exact at w <= 6 for all realistic gamma/J. Cost: <=1 day on 8 cores.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low for a positive region (dissipation and universality both work against it); very high value as a decisive, cheap gate for the whole NMR family.
expected_speedup: n/a (gate)
measurement_readout: n/a
prior_art_known: Knill & Laflamme PRL 81, 5672 (1998). Schuster et al. PRX 15, 041018 (2025). Angrisani et al. PRL 135, 170602 (2025), arXiv 2409.01706. O'Brien et al. PRX Quantum 3, 030345 (2022): an empirical link between learnability (Hessian structure) and the multifractal-dimension drop. Y. Li et al. Nat. Phys. (2024), arXiv 2406.07625 (universality). Under this lane's scope, the search found no paper bounding structural Fisher information by classical simulation cost for NMR.
representation: Protein-derived dipolar graphs; observables as Pauli-weight-resolved expansions.
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: This card defines what reproduction means: weight-truncated propagation that captures >=90% of the Fisher information.

title: P4. High-field liquid-state protein NMR forward models (NOESY, J, RDC, PCS/PRE, shifts, relaxation/CPMG/CEST) and quantum approximate Bayesian computation (kill card)
protein_question: Can a quantum simulator improve protein structure determination from standard solution NMR data, as quantum approximate Bayesian computation (QABC) proposes for NMR model inference?
quantum_primitive: Hamiltonian or Liouvillian simulation of the coupled spin system inside approximate Bayesian computation (Sels et al. 2020), or digital NMR spectrum simulation (Seetharam et al. 2023; the Q-CTRL/IBM/IonQ 34-spin demo, arXiv 2512.14513; the Quantinuum 21-spin effective model, arXiv 2609.17102).
mechanism: The claimed mechanism is the 2^N spin Hilbert space. The actual structure is classically benign. (1) At high field the secular, weak-coupling Hamiltonian commutes with every I_z, so spectra factor into first-order multiplets. (2) NOE cross-relaxation under the secular, high-temperature Solomon/Redfield equations closes in the N-dimensional longitudinal-magnetisation subspace, so the full relaxation matrix (CORMA/IRMA-type) is an N x N exponential. (3) RDCs and PCSs are single-pair or single-spin closed forms (PCS uses a fitted 8-parameter delta-chi tensor, so even exchange-coupled metal clusters need no ab initio input). (4) Chemical shifts are closed-shell, weakly correlated electronic structure, handled by DFT or ML. (5) CPMG/CEST use few-state, few-spin Bloch-McConnell matrices. Spinach's restricted state space simulated 2D/3D spectra of 1000+-spin ubiquitin with full Redfield including cross-correlation (Edwards et al. JMR 2014). Linear-scaling clustering 'performs well throughout, and even somewhat beyond, the more typical experimental regimes' (Fratus et al. 2025/26). Hardware demos are validated against classical references. No resource here is exponentially hard.
oracle_and_state_prep: Shifts, J and relaxation parameters come from classical models. The state is the high-temperature equilibrium state. Cost is trivial, but so is the classical calculation.
strongest_classical_competitor: Spinach restricted-state-space simulation (Kuprov); tensor-train propagation (Savostyanov, Dolgov, Kuprov PRB 2014); full-relaxation-matrix NOE; CYANA/XPLOR-NIH/ARIA; CS-Rosetta; AF2-assisted NMR.
information_vs_computation: The bottleneck in solution NMR is information: sparse restraints plus conformational averaging. It is not the spin-physics computation. The hard remnant, averaging over conformational ensembles, is classical-energy sampling, which is the known quadratic family M1/M2.
relation_to_S29_S33: OLD FAILURE, reused: the only quantum-relevant remnant (ensemble averaging) reduces to H-006/M1-M2 posterior sampling, which is quadratic at best. There is no new mechanism. This is a new, literature-backed kill for the QABC-for-proteins framing.
kill_result: Already effectively killed by the literature (Edwards et al. 2014; Fratus et al. 2025/26). Confirmed if the full-relaxation-matrix and first-order models deviate from exact Liouville-space simulation by less than experimental error (10-20%) on protein-derived clusters.
minimal_classical_first_test: Take a 10-12-1H cluster from 1UBQ (OpenMM hydrogens) with a rigid-rotor tau_c of 4 ns at 600 MHz. Compute NOESY build-ups two ways: exact Liouville space (4^12 is too large, so restrict to <=10 spins, or use Spinach-style spin-order truncation) with Redfield including cross-correlation, and the N x N full relaxation matrix. Also compute 1D spectra first-order against exact. Report the maximum deviation at mixing times <=200 ms. Cost: minutes to hours.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low (near zero): polynomial forward models already simulate 1000+-spin proteins; the hardness demonstrated for liquids concerns small, strongly coupled molecules.
prior_art_known: Sels, Dashti, Mora, Demler et al., Nat. Mach. Intell. 2, 396 (2020), arXiv 1910.14221. Seetharam et al., Sci. Adv. 9, eadh2594 (2023). Edwards, Savostyanov, Welderufael, Lee, Kuprov, JMR 243, 107 (2014). Savostyanov, Dolgov, Kuprov PRB 90, 085139 (2014). Fratus et al. arXiv 2508.06448. arXiv 2512.14513 (34 spins, liquid, high field). Stadler et al. arXiv 2609.17102 (21-spin effective model, Quantinuum).
representation: Chemical-shift/J/relaxation spin Hamiltonian from a structure or ensemble
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: Fully reproduced by restricted-state-space, tensor-train and clustering methods.

title: P5. Zero-to-ultralow-field (ZULF) / low-field NMR of proteins as a classically hard spin problem
protein_question: Do ZULF J-spectra of peptides or labelled proteins carry structural information usable for protein structure? Here strong coupling makes the problem genuinely many-body, and both Fratus et al. and Elenewski et al. point to this regime for quantum advantage.
quantum_primitive: Qubitised Hamiltonian simulation of the isotropic J-coupled Hamiltonian H = sum J_ij I_i . I_j plus Redfield relaxation (Elenewski, Camara, Kalev, arXiv 2406.09340). A 4-qubit trapped-ion ZULF demo exists (Seetharam et al. 2023).
mechanism: At zero field the Hamiltonian is a Heisenberg model on the covalent J graph. Eigenstates are entangled across strongly coupled clusters, and lines sit at combinations of J, so exact simulation is exponential in the size of the connected strongly coupled cluster. For proteins, the resource that is hard to simulate carries almost no fold information. J couplings decay beyond 3-4 bonds, so the graph is quasi-1D along the backbone with short side-chain branches, a low-entanglement geometry where MPS/TT methods work. The structural content is local 3J Karplus dihedrals (phi, chi1), which are already measured at high field or predicted from shifts (TALOS-N) and from learned priors. Slow tumbling (tau_c ~ 4-50 ns) gives dipolar relaxation linewidths of ~10-100 Hz, comparable to or larger than the J spread (1-150 Hz). The 0.01 Hz linewidths that motivate the regime apply to small molecules.
speedup_type: exponential-simulation (small molecules only); none for protein structure
oracle_and_state_prep: The J graph comes cheaply from the covalent structure and a Karplus relation. The state is prepolarised magnetisation (classical input).
strongest_classical_competitor: Tensor-train/MPS propagation on quasi-1D J graphs (Savostyanov et al. 2014); spin-dependent clustering (Fratus et al.); high-field HNHA-type 3J measurements plus TALOS-N; learned phi/psi priors (esmprior_v1's theta/tau head).
information_vs_computation: The information is local dihedral preferences, already available more cheaply. Quantum computation would unlock no fold-level information.
relation_to_S29_S33: Materially different physics (a non-commuting physical Hamiltonian), but it fails DNR-16's requirement of a genuinely new information source: the data duplicate the local (theta,tau)-type information esmprior_v1 already has. At 9-16 aa that information is K-012's in-band information limit.
kill_result: Kill if (a) the estimated ZULF linewidth for a 60-aa protein exceeds the J spread, or (b) the only parameters identifiable from simulated ZULF spectra are 3J dihedrals, whose Fisher information is <= that from high-field 3J data.
minimal_classical_first_test: Compute the exact ZULF spectrum of a 13C/15N-labelled dipeptide fragment (12-14 spins) with Redfield relaxation at tau_c = 0.3 ns (peptide) and 4 ns (60-aa protein). Compare with an MPS/cluster approximation. Compute the Fisher information on phi/psi against that from high-field 3J(HN-HA). Cost: <1 day.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low: spin physics may be hard for small molecules, but for proteins the hard part encodes only local dihedrals and is washed out by slow-tumbling linewidths.
prior_art_known: Elenewski, Camara, Kalev, 'Prospects for NMR spectral prediction on fault-tolerant quantum computers', arXiv 2406.09340 (2024/25; covers small-molecule and protein applications at ZULF). Fratus et al. arXiv 2508.06448 (ZULF named as the possible advantage path). Seetharam et al. Sci. Adv. 2023.
representation: Covalent J-coupling graph with Karplus-derived couplings
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: MPS/TT is expected to handle quasi-1D protein J graphs; untested at protein scale (unverified).

title: P6. Quantum-memory learning from nuclear-spin quantum data: quantum-sensor (NV) single-protein NMR with coherent processing
protein_question: Can single-molecule structural information (conformer identity, heterogeneity) be learned from a protein's own nuclear-spin signals, sensed by a quantum sensor, with far fewer experiments if the sensor state is processed coherently in a quantum memory rather than measured and processed classically?
quantum_primitive: Quantum-enhanced experiments / quantum-memory learning (Huang, Broughton, Cotler et al., Science 376, 1182, 2022); quantum computational sensing (Khan et al., npj QI 2026, arXiv 2507.15845; Kannan et al. arXiv 2608.13521); NV sensing with nuclear-spin quantum logic (Lovchinsky et al., Science 351, 836, 2016).
mechanism: Resource: the number of experiments, not computation. Information-theoretic lower bounds show measure-then-process learners need exponentially more copies than learners that store copies coherently and measure jointly, for tasks such as predicting many non-commuting observables' magnitudes, Pauli-channel eigenvalues or purity-type properties. Classical processing cannot copy this because the information is destroyed at single-copy measurement. Structure learning, however, is learning O(N*k) local couplings of a local Hamiltonian, and Heisenberg-limited local-Hamiltonian learning with single-copy measurements and classical processing is already efficient (Huang, Tong, Fang, Su, PRL 130, 200403, 2023). The exponential separations therefore do not obviously apply. A room-temperature protein's nuclear-spin state is also almost maximally mixed (statistical polarisation), and coherently transducing multiple molecules' spin states into a memory is far beyond present technology.
speedup_type: sample-complexity (only for non-local property tasks; none known for local-Hamiltonian/geometry learning)
oracle_and_state_prep: No oracle: data come from the physical sample. The costly step is coherent transduction of sensor/nuclear states into memory, which is unrealised for biomolecules. State preparation is the physical protein.
strongest_classical_competitor: Classical Heisenberg-limited Hamiltonian learning; Bayesian adaptive sensing with classical inference, as in the NV imaging of a 27-13C nuclear-spin cluster (Abobeih et al., Nature 2019), where structure came from classical post-processing; conventional ensemble NMR.
information_vs_computation: This is the one card where the quantum device acquires new information: single-molecule data, directly attacking the S29-S33 information limit. The advantage is in sensing (metrology and the quantum-sensing claim category), not computation. Computation is quantum only if coherent multi-copy processing is required.
relation_to_S29_S33: NEW MECHANISM: information acquisition rather than search or sampling, so it satisfies DNR-16 by construction. WHY OLD CONTROL NO LONGER APPLIES: SA or random prior twins are meaningless. The twin is a sensor with classical processing and the same number of experiments.
kill_result: For computation, kill if (a) the classical Fisher information of the best implementable single-copy measurement is >= 0.5x the sensor state's quantum Fisher information for the geometric parameters (so coherent processing gains <= 2x per copy), and (b) the task is local-Hamiltonian learning, covered by Heisenberg-limited classical-processing results.
minimal_classical_first_test: Simulate an NV electron spin plus a 12-16-spin 1H/13C cluster from a 1UBQ surface fragment (OpenMM hydrogens; 5-10 nm standoff sweep) under dynamical-decoupling correlation spectroscopy. Compute the quantum Fisher information of the sensor state and the classical Fisher information of the standard projective readout for 10 position parameters, then run Bayesian inference on simulated data to estimate the experiment count for 0.2 A precision. Cost: <1 day.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low: exponential learning separations target non-local properties, whereas geometry learning is local-Hamiltonian learning, which classical processing handles efficiently; biomolecular transduction is not realistic.
prior_art_known: Huang et al. Science 376, 1182 (2022). Huang, Tong, Fang, Su PRL 130, 200403 (2023). Lovchinsky et al. Science 351, 836 (2016). Kost, Cai, Plenio Sci. Rep. 5, 11007 (2015) (NV-based single-molecule structure proposals). Abobeih et al., 'Atomic-scale imaging of a 27-nuclear-spin cluster using a quantum sensor', Nature (2019). Khan et al. arXiv 2507.15845. Kannan et al. arXiv 2608.13521. Under this lane's scope, the search found no quantum-memory-learning proposal for protein structure.
representation: Nuclear-spin positions relative to the sensor, with hyperfine/dipolar couplings
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: Classical Bayesian inversion reproduced 27-spin structure imaging.

title: P7. EPR/DEER multi-spin distance forward models and electron-spin decoherence as a structural probe (kill card)
protein_question: Would quantum forward models add structural information to DEER/RIDME distance distributions (multi-spin, short-distance) or to echo-decay/ESEEM data used as local packing and solvent-exposure probes?
quantum_primitive: Hamiltonian simulation of electron spins plus the nuclear bath (central-spin model), Trotterised.
mechanism: (1) DEER at high field in the secular point-dipole limit: V(t) = product over partners of [1 - lambda_k(1 - cos(omega_dd,k t))], an exact closed form for multi-spin clusters. Ghost distances come from this product structure and are removed with known power-scaling corrections (von Hagens et al. 2013). Exchange and pseudo-secular terms matter only below ~1.5-2 nm and involve 2-4 spins, so exact simulation is trivial. (2) Echo decay from the proton bath: cluster-correlation expansion (CCE) was quantitatively accurate from structure with up to 2000 neighbouring protons (Canarie, Jahn, Stoll 2020), and tensor networks give numerically exact bath dynamics (Li et al. arXiv 2509.20604). A hard regime (long times, dense strongly coupled baths, CCE divergence) would probe only local proton density and methyl dynamics within ~1-1.5 nm, not the fold. The dominant DEER uncertainty is the spin-label rotamer ensemble plus the protein ensemble, which is classical-energy sampling.
oracle_and_state_prep: Label rotamer ensembles come from classical libraries. The state is the thermal electron polarisation plus a mixed nuclear bath.
strongest_classical_competitor: DeerLab regularised inversion; rotamer libraries (MMM, chiLife, MTSSLWizard); CCE; TN bath dynamics.
information_vs_computation: Information comes from the experiment (distances, local proton density). The classical forward models are adequate, and the residual difficulty (label and protein ensembles) is not spin physics.
relation_to_S29_S33: The residual hard part is ensemble sampling, which reduces to H-006/M1-M2 (quadratic, conditional). There is no new mechanism.
kill_result: Kill if CCE-4 or TN matches exact bath dynamics within experimental error for protein-like proton baths (already shown for 2000 protons in organic radicals), and if the Fisher information of echo decay on a fold-level variable is ~0 compared with its Fisher information on local proton density.
minimal_classical_first_test: Place a nitroxide (MTSSL, chiLife rotamers) on a 1UBQ surface site, add OpenMM hydrogens and explicit-water protons within 1.5 nm, and take N=20 protons. Compare an exact Hahn echo (2^21 with the electron) against CCE-2/4. Compute the Fisher information of the echo on (a) local proton density and (b) a 1 A shift of a distant helix. For DEER, compare exact 4-electron simulation with pseudo-secular terms against the product kernel at 1.5-4 nm. Cost: <1 day.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low: forward models are closed form or converge under CCE/TN; the structure-limiting uncertainty is classical ensemble modelling.
prior_art_known: Canarie, Jahn, Stoll, J. Phys. Chem. Lett. 11, 3396 (2020). T. Li, Venkatesh, Shitara, Montoya-Castillo arXiv 2509.20604 (2025). von Hagens, Polyhach, Sajid, Godt, Jeschke, PCCP 15, 5854 (2013). chiLife/MMM (rotamer-library approach). Yang & Liu CCE (PRB 2008; UNVERIFIED this session).
representation: Spin-label rotamer ensembles on a backbone model; electron plus proton bath geometry
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: CCE and TN reproduce the bath dynamics; the rotamer-library approach reproduces DEER distributions within label-ensemble uncertainty.

title: P8. Strongly correlated metal cofactors: fault-tolerant QPE energies and spectroscopic properties to decide active-site structure (protonation, ligand identity, intermediates)
protein_question: For multi-metal sites (FeMoco E-states, P-cluster, OEC S-states, Fe-S clusters, P450 Cpd I), which protonation, ligand and oxidation-state structure is consistent with crystallographic density and EPR/ENDOR/Moessbauer/XES data? QM/MM 'quantum refinement' currently relies on BS-DFT.
quantum_primitive: Fault-tolerant qubitised QPE with THC block encoding for low-lying energies of active-space Hamiltonians at candidate geometries and protonation variants. For spectroscopy matching (hyperfine couplings, exchange ladder, Moessbauer isomer shift), QPE state preparation is followed by expectation estimation.
mechanism: Resource: accurate energies and properties of dense, near-degenerate spin ladders of 8 antiferromagnetically coupled metal centres. Classical DMRG cost grows with the bond dimension needed for chemical accuracy, and thermally averaged properties over many low-lying states are harder than ground-state energies. QPE cost is poly(orbitals)/epsilon given a state with good overlap. This is a polynomial, precision-type advantage; the literature finds no generic exponential advantage (Lee et al. Nat. Commun. 2023). The FeMoco 76-orbital model was solved classically to chemical accuracy in ~23 h on Frontier, against a ~8.6 h quantum estimate (Zhai et al. 2026). DMRG mapped the P-cluster landscape (Li, Guo, Sun, Chan, Nat. Chem. 2019). Structural payoff: sub-0.1 A cluster geometry and protonation states, which matter for mechanism but not for the backbone fold.
oracle_and_state_prep: Block encoding of the active-space Hamiltonian via THC costs ~1e9-1e10 Toffoli per QPE at FeMoco scale, ~4 M physical qubits and <4 days (Lee et al. PRX Quantum 2021). State preparation is the crux: small overlap with the true low-lying states can erase the advantage (Lee et al. 2023). The active space is chosen classically and is disputed (Li et al. JCP 2019).
strongest_classical_competitor: DMRG / DMRG-NEVPT2, SHCI, AFQMC, spin-projected BS-DFT; QM/MM quantum refinement (ComQum-X, Phenix/ORCA quantum refinement; Ryde group).
information_vs_computation: Information comes from crystallography and spectroscopy. The computation is energy ranking and property prediction. The quantum part could decide between candidates only where classical methods are unconverged, a shrinking set.
relation_to_S29_S33: This is literature row M14 (WEAK / out of scope) and DE-7 (S29-S33 measured that energy accuracy is not the bottleneck: AMBER in-band rho 0.000). It differs materially only in target: active-site chemical structure, which the built-chain RMSD endpoint cannot register. None of the H-001 family applies (a genuinely non-commuting fermionic Hamiltonian).
kill_result: For protein structure it is killed regardless (out of fold scope). For metal-site structure, kill if classical DMRG/AFQMC energy differences between candidate protonation or ligand states converge to < 1-2 kcal/mol against the gap, or BS-DFT and DMRG geometries differ by < 0.05 A (below data resolution).
minimal_classical_first_test: Install PySCF and block2. Run DMRG-CASCI on a [2Fe-2S](SCH3)4 model (CAS ~(30e,20o), bond dimension 500-2000) for two protonation variants (bridging S protonated or not) at BS-DFT geometries. Test whether the energy ranking is stable with bond dimension and agrees with BS-DFT. Separately, audit published FeMoco E4 and OEC S3 structural proposals for any claim that hinges on energy differences classical methods cannot converge. Cost: <1 day on 8 cores.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low for protein structure (out of scope); low-medium for metal-site chemistry, where the flagship target is eroding under classical DMRG.
prior_art_known: Reiher et al. PNAS 114, 7555 (2017). J. Lee et al. PRX Quantum 2, 030305 (2021). S. Lee et al. Nat. Commun. 14, 1952 (2023). Z. Li et al. JCP (2019), arXiv 1809.10307. Zhai et al. arXiv 2601.04621 (2026). Z. Li, Guo, Sun, Chan, Nat. Chem. 11, 1026 (2019). Goings et al. PNAS (2022), DOI 10.1073/pnas.2203533119 (P450 classical-quantum boundary). 'Combining crystallography with quantum mechanics', Curr. Opin. Struct. Biol. (2021) (Ryde group; author list UNVERIFIED).
representation: Active-space second-quantised Hamiltonian at QM/MM geometries of candidate active-site structures
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: DMRG/AFQMC reproduce the canonical FeMoco benchmark classically; ML potentials are unreliable for open-shell multi-metal clusters (not a limitation of the DMRG route).

title: P9. Nuclear quantum effects in H-bond networks and proton positions (low-barrier H-bonds, proton wires) (kill card)
protein_question: Do quantum proton delocalisation and tunnelling in protein H-bond networks change structural features (heavy-atom H-bond distances, protonation states) that classical methods miss, and does computing them need a quantum computer?
quantum_primitive: Thermal-state preparation or real-time simulation of the quantum nuclear Hamiltonian (Gibbs sampling of quantum nuclei).
mechanism: Equilibrium structural observables of distinguishable nuclei are imaginary-time path integrals with a positive integrand, so there is no sign problem. Proton exchange statistics are negligible in proteins. Path-integral MD (P beads, cost ~P times classical MD, with P ~ 6-32, fewer with PIGLET/colored noise) is therefore exact and polynomial given the potential energy surface. Real-time coherent tunnelling could be exponentially hard, but it decoheres within fs-ps in proteins, and rates are handled by RPMD, CMD or instanton theory. Effect sizes: heavy-atom H-bond shifts of ~0.01-0.05 A. The ketosteroid isomerase 10^4-fold acidity change (Wang et al. 2014) is a pKa/protonation (chemistry) effect, computed classically with PIMD. The accuracy-limiting resource is the potential energy surface, which is electronic structure (see P8), not nuclear quantum statistics.
speedup_type: none-known (equilibrium structure); the potentially hard real-time coherent dynamics is structurally irrelevant
oracle_and_state_prep: Requires a potential energy surface. A coherent PES oracle would dominate cost and duplicate the classical inputs.
strongest_classical_competitor: PIMD/PIGLET/RPMD with ML or QM/MM potentials (i-PI; OpenMM RPMDIntegrator, installed); Markland & Ceriotti, Nat. Rev. Chem. (2018).
information_vs_computation: No new information, and the computation is already polynomial classically.
relation_to_S29_S33: Gibbs sampling of a classical-like (ring-polymer) energy falls into the M1/M2 quadratic family and H-006. There is no new mechanism.
kill_result: Kill if the path integral is sign-free (true by construction for distinguishable nuclei) and PIMD-minus-classical shifts in heavy-atom structure are << 0.1 A on protein H-bond networks.
minimal_classical_first_test: Run OpenMM RPMDIntegrator (16 beads) against classical MD for a solvated beta-hairpin or a KSI active-site fragment with a standard force field, a few ns each. Measure the distribution shifts of H-bond heavy-atom distances and backbone RMSD. Confirm < 0.05 A and linear cost in beads. Cost: <1 day on 8 cores.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low: sign-free Euclidean path integrals make the relevant structure exactly polynomial classically, and the structural effects are far below fold resolution.
prior_art_known: Wang, Fried, Boxer, Markland, PNAS 111, 18454 (2014). Markland & Ceriotti, 'Nuclear quantum effects enter the mainstream', Nat. Rev. Chem. (2018). Ceperley, Rev. Mod. Phys. (1995), path integrals (UNVERIFIED this session).
representation: Ring-polymer (P-bead) extension of an all-atom model
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: PIMD with ML potentials reproduces it.

title: P10. Vibrational, chiroptical and excitonic optical spectroscopy forward models (amide I IR, 2D-IR, Raman/ROA, ECD/VCD, 2DES of pigment-proteins) (kill card)
protein_question: Could exact quantum simulation of vibrational or electronic exciton Hamiltonians make optical spectra informative enough to discriminate folds, not just secondary-structure fractions?
quantum_primitive: Hamiltonian simulation of anharmonic vibrational (bosonic) Hamiltonians (McArdle 2019; Sawaya et al. 2020; Ollitrault et al. 2020; venues UNVERIFIED this session) or open-system exciton dynamics.
mechanism: The spectroscopically active manifolds are small. Amide I IR lives in the one-exciton manifold (an N x N matrix, N = number of amides) and 2D-IR in the two-exciton manifold (~N^2/2), so both are polynomial. ECD uses the matrix method over chromophore transitions, also polynomial (DichroCalc). 2DES of pigment-protein complexes uses HEOM or TN-HEOM over ~7-30 pigments, polynomial at fixed bath depth. Full anharmonic VCI of a protein would be exponential but is unnecessary: spectra at 300 K are inhomogeneously broadened, and their information content is a few secondary-structure numbers. SESCA predicts CD from secondary-structure composition and basis spectra. No classically hard component carries fold-level information.
oracle_and_state_prep: Local-mode frequency and coupling maps come from classical electrostatics or ML (transition dipole coupling / Jansen-type maps).
strongest_classical_competitor: Exciton models benchmarked against localized-mode VSCF/VCI; DichroCalc matrix method; SESCA; HEOM/TN-HEOM.
information_vs_computation: Information content is low (secondary-structure fractions), and computation is polynomial.
relation_to_S29_S33: Relevant to DNR-16: these data are a new source, but a low-information one that adds almost nothing beyond esmprior_v1's (theta,tau) head. There is no new computational mechanism.
kill_result: Kill if exciton-model amide I and matrix-method CD spectra cannot separate natives from 3-6 A decoys (AUC < 0.6 at realistic noise). Then even an exact forward model carries no fold-level information, and the exact forward model is polynomial anyway.
minimal_classical_first_test: For mid30 and long40 native PDB chains (ORACLE analysis only) and A80-decoded decoys at 3-6 A, rebuild backbones (a CA-to-backbone builder, or PDB coordinates for natives). Compute amide I one-exciton spectra (TDC couplings plus a standard frequency map) and matrix-method CD. Compute native-vs-decoy discrimination AUC at SNR 100. Cost: <1 day.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low: polynomial one- and two-exciton forward models, and low structural information content.
prior_art_known: Bulheller & Hirst, DichroCalc, Bioinformatics 25, 539 (2009). Nagy, Igaev, Hoffmann, Jones, Grubmueller, SESCA, JCTC 15, 5087 (2019). Exciton-model protein IR (Husseini et al., J. Comput. Chem. 2017; per search listing). McArdle et al. 2019, Sawaya et al. 2020, Ollitrault et al. 2020 (vibrational quantum algorithms, small molecules; UNVERIFIED venues).
