representation: Backbone amide oscillators and chromophore transition dipoles from a structure
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: Fully classical; exciton Hamiltonians are small matrices.

title: P11. Diffraction and scattering forward models (MicroED dynamical scattering, XFEL, SAXS/WAXS, neutron) (kill card)
protein_question: Does multiple (dynamical) scattering in MicroED/3D ED, or any other scattering forward model used in structure determination, require quantum simulation?
quantum_primitive: Hamiltonian simulation of the scattering wave (a first-quantised grid-based quantum algorithm)
mechanism: Elastic electron dynamical diffraction is a single-particle Schroedinger equation in the crystal potential, solved by multislice or Bloch waves. The cost is O(grid * log(grid) * slices): a linear PDE with no many-body entanglement. A quantum algorithm offers at most polylog-grid gains, which vanish after state preparation and readout of the full diffraction pattern. Inelastic many-body scattering is absorbed into imaginary optical potentials. SAXS/WAXS reduces to the Debye formula or spherical-harmonic expansions. Neutron scattering reduces to the classical van Hove function from MD.
oracle_and_state_prep: Loading the crystal potential and reading out Omega(grid) intensities erases any polylog advantage.
strongest_classical_competitor: Multislice/Bloch-wave dynamical refinement of 3D ED data (Palatinus et al.; UNVERIFIED this session); CRYSOL/FoXS-type SAXS; MD-based neutron spectra.
information_vs_computation: Information comes from the experiment. Computation is linear or polynomial.
relation_to_S29_S33: It fails at the level of dimension counting: the problem is single-particle, the dimension is polynomial, and readout of the full output is required (the analogue of the M15 readout kill). There is no new mechanism.
kill_result: Confirmed by construction: a single-particle wave equation has no exponential state space. Formally a kill; listed only to close the lane.
minimal_classical_first_test: Run a multislice simulation (FFT, 512^2 grid, ~200 slices) of a 1UBQ microcrystal slab, dynamical against kinematic. Record runtime (expected minutes) and the dynamical-kinematic R-factor difference.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low (effectively nil): single-particle linear wave propagation has no many-body hardness.
prior_art_known: Cowley & Moodie multislice (1957; UNVERIFIED this session); dynamical refinement of 3D ED (Palatinus et al.; UNVERIFIED).
representation: Crystal electrostatic potential on a 3D grid
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: Fully classical.

title: P12. Posterior sampling with a quantum-estimated NMR likelihood on top of esmprior_v1/A80 (pseudo-marginal / penalty-method / delayed-acceptance MCMC): cost model and viability gate
protein_question: Suppose a classically hard, geometry-sensitive NMR forward model existed (P2, gated by P3). Could its quantum-estimated likelihood be consumed inside Bayesian structure inference, posterior proportional to exp(-E_A80) times L_NMR, at >=60 aa at acceptable cost, exploiting the one positive S33 signal (value of posterior averaging) with genuinely new per-target information?
quantum_primitive: Hamiltonian-simulation expectation values as a noisy likelihood estimator, optionally sharpened by amplitude estimation, consumed by a classical MCMC (pseudo-marginal, Ceperley-Dewing penalty method, or delayed acceptance with a classical approximate likelihood as the first stage).
mechanism: Explicit cost mechanism (the reason this is probably not viable). For K data points with Gaussian noise sigma and predicted signals mu_k estimated from M shots each, Var(log L-hat) ~ sum_k (r_k/sigma^2)^2 Var(mu-hat_k) ~ K/(sigma^2 M). Efficient pseudo-marginal and penalty-method MCMC need this variance to be O(1) (Doucet et al. 2015; Ceperley & Dewing 1999). So M >~ K/sigma^2 shots per datum per MCMC step: 1e7 for K=1e3 and sigma=0.01. With amplitude estimation, ~sqrt(K)/sigma ~ 3e3 coherent repetitions per datum. At ~3e8-1e9 T per circuit (P2) and >=1e3-1e4 MCMC steps per effective sample, that is >=1e18 T per posterior sample. Delayed acceptance with a classical LR-LCL first stage saves only the stage-1 rejection fraction, a constant factor. The only escape is an offline emulator trained on O(1e2-1e3) quantum evaluations, after which the quantum part is a finite dataset and load-bearing only through the emulator's generalisation ('trainable implies surrogate', F37/F91). The structure also reveals that S32's P1 (a decision space that grows) and P2 (a stochastic energy) are both satisfied here, but P2 is a cost, not a resource: P1 and P2 together are necessary, not sufficient.
speedup_type: none-known (constant-factor losses; any advantage is inherited from P2's exponential-simulation claim and consumed by shot noise)
oracle_and_state_prep: The likelihood oracle is an explicit Hamiltonian simulation per proposed structure (P1/P2 cost), with no free state preparation. Coherent (quantum-walk) use of this likelihood would require a reversible forward-model circuit inside the walk operator: M1-type overhead multiplied by P2-type circuits, which is prohibitive.
strongest_classical_competitor: Classical approximate likelihood (LR-LCL/rate models) in HMC/PT/SMC over the A80 energy; delayed-acceptance MCMC; neural simulation-based inference with classically simulated training data.
information_vs_computation: Information comes from esmprior_v1 (prior) and experimental NMR data (likelihood, the new source). Computation is quantum only in the likelihood. The posterior averaging is classical.
relation_to_S29_S33: OLD MECHANISM: the soft Boltzmann average beat hard tails (1.40x MDE on mid30), but as an exact enumerated sum. NEW MECHANISM: the energy term is a non-diagonal quantum expectation from experimental physics, so H-001/DNR-02 do not apply to the likelihood. The posterior-sampling layer is still the M1/M2 family (H-006), so a quantum walk on top inherits G1/G2's break-even problem. WHY OLD CONTROL NO LONGER APPLIES: the twin must be the same MCMC with the best classical approximate likelihood, not SA or random prior sampling.
kill_result: Kill if either holds. (a) The measured M_min (shots per datum per step for ESS/step within 2x of the noise-free chain) times the P2 circuit cost exceeds 1e12 T per effective posterior sample at K >= 100. (b) Replacing the exact likelihood with a classical approximate one (rate or LR-LCL model) changes the posterior-mean structure by < 0.1 A RMSD or < the posterior sd.
minimal_classical_first_test: On long40 (44-60 aa), sample exp(-E_A80) times a synthetic NMR-like likelihood. Use K=50-500 distance-dependent signals s_k = f(d_ij) generated from natives: ORACLE-labelled synthetic data, never used for selection. Add per-evaluation Gaussian estimator noise of variance 1/M to emulate shots. Run penalty-method MCMC and pseudo-marginal HMC over the M grid 1e2-1e8 and record ESS per step, acceptance and posterior-mean RMSD. Fit M_min(K, sigma) and compare with K/sigma^2. Then swap the exact f for a deliberately biased approximate f' and measure the posterior shift. Cost: batched torch on 8 cores, <1 day.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low: shot-noise requirements of likelihood-in-the-loop inference make per-sample quantum cost astronomical; the viable form (offline emulator) reduces the quantum role to generating training data.
classical_primitive_replaced: The classical approximate-likelihood evaluation inside NMR-restrained posterior MCMC
expected_speedup: None as an online likelihood; only an offline data-generation role survives.
measurement_readout: Per-datum expectation values; M >~ K/sigma^2 shots, or ~sqrt(K)/sigma amplitude-estimation repetitions, per MCMC step.
prior_art_known: Doucet, Pitt, Deligiannidis, Kohn, Biometrika 102, 295 (2015). Ceperley & Dewing, J. Chem. Phys. 110, 9812 (1999). Christen & Fox delayed acceptance (2005; UNVERIFIED this session). Sels et al. 2020 (QABC, the closest in spirit, liquid-state). Under this lane's scope, the search found no shot-noise cost analysis of quantum-likelihood MCMC for protein structure.
representation: Internal coordinates (theta,tau) with the A80 energy, plus an all-atom rebuild for the NMR likelihood
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: Neural simulation-based inference trained on classical (LR-LCL) simulations is the default classical reproduction; the quantum device matters only if those simulations are wrong in the Fisher-relevant regime (P3).

title: Information-annealed QSA: from the exactly preparable (theta,tau) product prior to the calibrated learned-energy posterior
protein_question: Can posterior samples be drawn from the esmprior-class learned-energy posterior at 60-300 aa, including the soft Boltzmann-weighted structural average that beat hard selection at mid30 (1.40x MDE, exact sum)? The case of interest is when the best classical sampler needs >=1e12 steps per independent sample.
quantum_primitive: Quantum simulated annealing (Somma et al. 2008 [A8]; Wocjan-Abeyesinghe 2008 [A7]; Harrow-Wei adaptive QSA for Bayesian inference [A31]). It uses phase-estimation-based projections onto |sqrt(pi_s)> built from Szegedy walks W(P_s) of a reversible (symmetric-scan) Metropolis kernel, along a path s: 0->1 that starts at the learned product prior.
representation: Per-residue joint (theta_i,tau_i) class from the esmprior_v1 head: 9 theta bins x 24 tau bins = 216 classes (8 qubits/residue; s33/esmprior.py), plus r fixed-point sub-bin bits per angle, with the CA trace built by forward kinematics. Path: pi_s ∝ q(x)·exp(-s[E_pair+E_steric]/T*), where q = prod_i q_i(theta_i,tau_i) is exactly the A80 tt term. Alternative data-ordered path (the Harrow-Wei 'data arrives' form): add pair terms by increasing |i-j| band.
mechanism: The speedup is in walk steps per stage. By Szegedy's spectral lemma, a reversible chain with gap delta_k has a walk operator whose nonzero eigenphases are >= ~2·sqrt(delta_k), so phase estimation at precision sqrt(delta_k) projects onto |sqrt(pi_{s_k})>. Given consecutive overlaps >= c, the total cost is O~(l·max_k delta_k^-1/2) walk steps, against O~(l·max_k delta_k^-1) classical kernel steps on the same path. The gain comes from coherent phase estimation on a unitary walk, which amplifies the gap quadratically. It is not parallel evaluation, which is why a classical computer cannot copy it. Lifted or nonreversible classical chains can recover part of the gain (A14/A15/A18) and belong in the classical twin. What the learned prior adds that raw folding lacks: the s=0 state |sqrt q> is a product of 216-dimensional states given as a finite table. It can be prepared EXACTLY with <=255 uniformly controlled rotations per residue. This removes the cold-start sqrt(N) penalty (Orsucci et al. [A9]) and supplies the Omega(1)-overlap warm path that QSA and quantum RELD [A44, A45] assume. Naive adiabatic evolution on the parent Hamiltonian costs O(1/delta) and gains nothing, so the phase-estimation (Zeno) implementation is required. At T=1 the posterior is effectively a point mass: distinct solver-best states on the same targets differ by 50-230 nats (s33 D_decoder NOTES), so sampling reduces to restart-saturated search. The card therefore applies only at a native-free calibrated T* >> 1 (card 4).
expected_speedup: At most quadratic in max_k 1/delta_k, with log factors; the number of stages l is the same on both sides. A wall-clock gain appears only if the classical twin needs >~1e12-1e14 steps per independent sample (card 7 break-even). Each anneal yields one sample (no cloning), so a soft readout needs about 20-50 anneals.
oracle_and_state_prep: State prep is an exact product state, ~L·255 rotations (~2.5e4 at L=100). It does not erase the speedup and sidesteps Herbert's Grover-Rudolph no-go [B37], because the prepared distribution is the given prior, not the posterior. The oracle is a coherent symmetric-scan Metropolis step: a crankshaft or pivot update, O(L) to O(L^2) pair distances, a soft-bin lookup in the per-target pair tables via QROM, Delta-E accumulation, a Lemieux-type Metropolis coin [A55], then uncompute. That is ~1e3 Toffolis per pair update, or ~1e5-1e7 Toffolis per step at L=100 (card 7, I(agent)). The per-target tables are classical ESM output loaded via QROM; no block encoding comes for free. This per-step overhead, not the state prep, is what can erase the speedup.
strongest_classical_competitor: SMC / annealed importance sampling on the IDENTICAL path: adaptive ESS-controlled Delta-s, HMC/MALA rejuvenation, resampling. Also PT/REST2 at the endpoint, nonreversible or lifted kernels, sequential Boltzmann generators [E79], and random-prior + relaxation used as an independence proposal inside SMC. Same energy, prior and move set, with equal tuning.
classical_primitive_replaced: The MCMC rejuvenation kernel inside each SMC/tempering stage. The path, the prior and the readout stay classical.
information_vs_computation: INFORMATION (classical, per target, fixed before any quantum run): q_i(theta,tau) and p_ij(d) from ESM-2 650M + esmprior_v1, and T* calibrated on held-out prots/ (never on long40 RMSD). COMPUTATION (quantum): only the sqrt(delta_k) acceleration of the intermediate kernels. The path and prior are shared with the classical SMC twin, so the learned model contributes identically to both sides. The quantum part adds no information.
measurement_readout: A computational-basis measurement of the (theta,tau)+sub-bin register gives one posterior sample per anneal. Each sample is decoded to a CA trace, and the soft readout is their classical average after optimal superposition. This consumes the full distribution, not an argmin, prefix or convex functional.
relation_to_S29_S33: OLD MECHANISM: A70/A71 tempered Born machine / Gibbs readout on <=18 enumerable qubits (QX-28/29, K-007, DNR-10), and 106-171-qubit (theta,tau) registers warm-started from this same prior (K-006). OLD FAILURE: Metropolis was closer to the exact target on 9/10; random prior sampling beat VQE on the chain. NEW MECHANISM: non-variational QSA with a provable walk-step bound on a non-enumerable 216^L space, sampling a SPECIFIED posterior. H-001 covers optimised distributions consumed through argmin, prefix or convex functionals. Here the open question is whether E_pi[x] can be computed classically at all, so H-001 does not apply. WHY OLD CONTROL NO LONGER APPLIES: not automatically. DNR-10 reopens only on a measured mixing failure, and the DNR-02 escape clause needs a measured classical failure; the minimal test supplies both. This card sharpens M1/H-006 (the T2b warm start); it is not a new kind of mechanism.
kill_result: Any of: (a) SMC on the same path at T* keeps ESS/N >= 0.3 per stage with <=1e3 rejuvenation sweeps, and the extrapolated max_k tau_int at L=150 is <= 1e9 steps (classical cost << B(L)). (b) A first-order transition on the path: a bimodal energy histogram at some s, with overlaps collapsing like e^-cL. This breaks QSA's Omega(1)-overlap premise as badly as it breaks SMC, so there is no quantum rescue. (c) The sampled soft readout at T* fails to beat the A80 decoder by >=1.0x MDE on long40 (no transmission).
minimal_classical_first_test: DEP, 10 dev targets each from mid30 and long40. Run adaptive-tempering SMC from q to pi_1 at T in {1,3,10,30} with 256 particles and MALA/HMC rejuvenation in (theta,tau), using the batched A80 torch energy (~0.55 ms/structure at L=56 in batch, so ~5e5 evaluations take minutes per target per core). Record l(L), per-stage ESS, per-stage tau_int of E and of contact-order observables (a delta_k proxy), the across-run variance of log Z (a mixing/bias diagnostic) and per-stage energy histograms (first-order signature). Fit max tau_int against L from 25 to 60 and extrapolate. The same run also yields Phi for card 2 and the basin-census inputs for card 4. Under a day on 8 cores within the 95% ceiling.
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: If the intermediate states |sqrt(pi_s)> have low sequence-order Schmidt rank (card 5), MPS/TT tracking of the path could dequantise it. Interval-scope kinematic factors make the MPOs high-rank (card 12), so this is not automatic. A flow or sequential Boltzmann generator trained along the same path amortises samples classically.
prior_art_known: Verified in the program bibliography: Somma et al. PRL 101,130504 (2008) arXiv 0804.1571 [A8]; Wocjan & Abeyesinghe PRA 78,042336 (2008) arXiv 0804.4259 [A7]; Harrow & Wei SODA 2020 arXiv 1907.09965 [A31]; Orsucci et al. Quantum 2,105 (2018) arXiv 1503.01334 [A9]; Leng et al. PNAS 2026 arXiv 2505.05301 [A44]; Lemieux et al. Quantum 4,287 (2020) arXiv 1910.01659 [A55]. The search (448-paper bibliography plus this session's targeted web searches, Sept 2026) found no evidence of a QSA or quantum-Langevin sampler that uses a learned protein-structure prior as its warm start or annealing path.
track: B fault-tolerant, gated by C theory (T2) and classical G1
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low (~5%). This is the best-posed card in the lane, and the prior genuinely removes the warm-start obstacle. The gain is still only sqrt(delta), and it needs >=1e12 classical steps per sample on a landscape that funnel theory and PT suggest is polynomial.

title: One-shot quantum conditioning of the learned product prior (quantum rejection sampling / independence walk), killed by a KL-total-correlation identity
protein_question: Can the cheap exact warm start |sqrt q> be turned directly into posterior samples by amplitude amplification, skipping intermediate annealing? That is, is 'prepare the learned prior, then amplify' a viable route?
quantum_primitive: Quantum rejection sampling (Ozols-Roetteler-Roland [A36]; Low-Yoder-Chuang [A37]): amplitude amplification of an acceptance flag with amplitude sqrt(w(x)/w_max), where w = exp(-E_pair/T). Equivalently, the Szegedy walk of the independence Metropolis chain with proposal q.
representation: The same 216-class (theta,tau) register plus sub-bin bits, with target pi ∝ q·w.
mechanism: The quantum cost is O(sqrt(w_max/E_q[w])) = O(e^{Phi/2}), against O(e^{Phi}) for classical rejection, where Phi = log(w_max/E_q[w]). For the independence sampler the gap is exactly delta_IMH = E_q[w]/w_max = e^{-Phi} (Liu 1996, exact eigenanalysis), so the walk version costs the same e^{Phi/2}. KILL IDENTITY: since pi = q·w/E_q[w], D_KL(pi||q) = E_pi[log w] - log E_q[w] <= Phi. For a product q, D_KL(pi||prod q_i) = sum_i KL(pi_i||q_i) + TC(pi), where TC is the total correlation. One-shot quantum conditioning therefore costs >= exp([sum_i KL(pi_i||q_i) + TC(pi)]/2): exponential in exactly the information the pair terms add beyond the per-residue prior. S33's lever-arm law (no local rule folds a 55-mer; tertiary information must come from a global term) and the tt-only ablation rho of 0.32 imply this information is extensive at any fold-informative T*. The quadratic speedup buys e^{Theta(L)/2} instead of e^{Theta(L)}, while SMC with local moves never pays e^{D_KL}. Consequence: the cheap product warm start is useful only inside a multi-stage path (card 1).
expected_speedup: Quadratic over classical rejection only. The absolute cost is exp(Theta(L)), and it loses to SMC once D_KL >~ 2·log(SMC cost).
oracle_and_state_prep: |sqrt q> is exact and cheap. The weight oracle is a coherent full E_pair (O(L^2) terms, ~1e7 Toffolis at L=100) followed by an arcsin rotation. State prep does not erase the speedup; the exponentially small acceptance does.
strongest_classical_competitor: SMC/AIS from q with local rejuvenation; importance sampling with resampling; and random-prior draws + L-BFGS relaxation (S33's winning search twin) used as proposals inside SMC.
classical_primitive_replaced: Classical rejection sampling or independence Metropolis from the prior.
information_vs_computation: INFORMATION: the pair tables supply D_KL(pi||q) nats beyond the per-residue head. COMPUTATION: amplitude amplification converts that information into a cost of e^{D_KL/2}. The more informative the learned pair model, the more expensive one-shot quantum conditioning becomes: the quantum step must pay for exactly the information the classical model supplies.
measurement_readout: Measure the acceptance flag; on success, measure the register to obtain one posterior sample.
relation_to_S29_S33: OLD MECHANISM: the (theta,tau) product prior as warm start for 106-171-qubit CVaR-VQE registers (K-006, DNR-05/06/07), with random prior sampling as the twin that beat VQE (1.35x MDE). OLD FAILURE: the warm-started quantum search was not load-bearing. NEW MECHANISM: coherent full-distribution conditioning with a provable quadratic query speedup. This is not an argmin/CVaR readout, so H-001 does not apply directly. WHY OLD CONTROL NO LONGER APPLIES: the random-prior twin was a search control. It is replaced here by a stronger, representation-independent kill (the KL/TC identity). This closes matrix row M6 for learned priors with a stated reason.
kill_result: Measured Phi(T*,L) >= D_KL grows linearly in L and exceeds ~40 nats by L≈60. Quantum rejection then needs >= e^20 ≈ 5e8 coherent full-energy evaluations per sample, against ~1e5 classical evaluations for SMC. Reopen only if Phi = O(log L) at a fold-informative T*, which would mean the product prior alone already determines the fold.
minimal_classical_first_test: A free byproduct of card 1's SMC run. log E_q[w] is the SMC log-Z ratio, and log w_max comes from the minimum of E_pair+sterics via 64-restart L-BFGS (restart-saturated per E800b). Then Phi = log w_max - log E_q[w]. Also estimate sum_i KL(pi_i||q_i) from the SMC marginals, and plot Phi/L at T in {1,3,10,30} for mid30/long40. Takes hours.
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: Not needed; classical SMC dominates.
prior_art_known: Ozols, Roetteler, Roland ITCS 2012 arXiv 1103.2774 [A36] and Low, Yoder, Chuang PRA 89,062315 (2014) arXiv 1402.7359 [A37] (bibliography-verified). J.S. Liu, Stat. Comput. 6:113-119 (1996), DOI 10.1007/BF00162521 (verified this session; exact eigenanalysis of independence Metropolis). The KL/total-correlation lower bound on quantum rejection cost is elementary. The search found no statement of it for learned protein priors (scope: program bibliography + this session's searches).
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: very low (<1%). The exponential cost follows from an identity, and its only escape (non-extensive pair information) contradicts the S33 evidence.

title: Coherently simulated learned generator (flow / probability-flow ODE, BioEmu-class) as warm start, then amplitude-amplified reweighting to the learned-energy posterior
protein_question: Does a deep generative structure prior, simulated coherently, give a warm start close enough to the learned-energy posterior that amplitude amplification or a short QSA beats classical Boltzmann-generator reweighting / SMC?
quantum_primitive: Coherent simulation of a continuous flow model to prepare the qsample |sqrt(q_phi)>. Layden et al. 2025 ('Wavefunction Flows', arXiv 2510.08462) claim this simulation is efficient; only the abstract was read. It is followed either by quantum rejection sampling / amplitude amplification with weight w = pi/q_phi, or by a short QSA started at |sqrt(q_phi)>.
representation: CA coordinates or (theta,tau), with a sequence-conditioned flow or diffusion generator: BioEmu-class [E83], AlphaFlow/ESMFlow [E80], or a small IAF trained on the target posterior.
mechanism: The speedup is in amplification rounds, O(sqrt(w_max/E_q[w])) versus O(w_max/E_q[w]) for classical rejection, and a good generator shrinks the number of QSA stages. The classical side, however, never uses rejection. It uses importance weighting or SMC with ESS = N/(1+chi^2(pi||q_phi)), and 1+chi^2 <= w_max/E_q[w]. There are two further obstacles. (i) Coherent generator evaluation: ~1e2 ODE steps x a 1e7-1e8-MAC network x ~1e2-1e3 Toffolis per fixed-point MAC gives ~1e11-1e13 Toffolis per qsample. It also needs the exact log-density q_phi(x) inside w, a divergence integral whose usual Hutchinson estimators are stochastic and not directly coherent. (ii) Generators already give INDEPENDENT samples classically at ~ms each on a GPU, so there is no mixing time to accelerate, only reweighting inefficiency. Break-even needs 1+chi^2 >~ (C_q/C_c)^2 ≈ 1e16-1e18. At such ESS, classical SMC with MCMC rejuvenation (sequential Boltzmann generators) wins.
expected_speedup: Quadratic in the rejection ratio against classical rejection. None against importance sampling/SMC at realistic chi^2.
oracle_and_state_prep: Inputs are the classically trained generator weights, the ESM embeddings and the esmprior energy. State prep is the coherent flow simulation: polynomial per Layden et al., but ~1e11+ Toffolis per qsample at 100 aa (I(agent)). The oracle is a coherent E(x) plus a coherent log q_phi(x). This does erase the speedup: per-qsample cost exceeds classical cost by >~1e8.
strongest_classical_competitor: Boltzmann generators with importance reweighting (Noé et al. 2019 [A78/E76]); sequential Boltzmann generators [E79]; transferable BGs [E78]; BioEmu [E83] as proposal + SMC; flow-proposal MCMC. Diffusion sampling is polynomial given an accurate score (Chen et al. 'Sampling is as easy as learning the score', arXiv 2209.11215, UNVERIFIED this session), so the hardness sits in classical learning, not in sampling.
classical_primitive_replaced: Importance reweighting or rejection correction of generator samples.
information_vs_computation: INFORMATION: the generator (trained classically on PDB/MD data) and the energy tables. COMPUTATION: amplification of the reweighting step only. A better generator is a classical ML lever (C-5 / esmprior_v2), and the data-processing inequality means the quantum step adds no information.
measurement_readout: Acceptance flag plus register measurement, giving one sample per success.
relation_to_S29_S33: OLD MECHANISM: quantum generative priors, i.e. the tempered/MPS Born machines of S33 A70/A71 (K-007, DE-6, matrix M13). OLD FAILURE: Metropolis was closer to the target; the random prior beat the trained circuit; trainable implies a classical surrogate [F91]. NEW MECHANISM: the generator is classical and only simulated coherently; the quantum step is amplification, not a trained quantum model. WHY OLD CONTROL NO LONGER APPLIES: the Born-machine kill was about trained quantum models. This card instead needs a resource and ESS kill, and fails it.
kill_result: Either (a) Toffolis per coherent qsample x sqrt(w_max/E w) exceeds classical cost x (1+chi^2) at all L <= 300 for the measured chi^2, or (b) classical SMC seeded by generator samples reaches ESS/N >= 1e-2 with <=1e3 rejuvenation steps, leaving no room.
minimal_classical_first_test: On 10 mid30/long40 dev targets at T*, use two local stand-in generators: the esmprior (theta,tau) product head (the weakest) and a small IAF/RealNVP trained by reverse KL on the target posterior (<=1 h CPU per target). Measure the log-weight distribution, chi^2, ESS/N and w_max/E w against L. Count MACs per flow evaluation analytically for the Toffoli estimate. BioEmu itself (GPU) is not needed for the kill.
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: 'Scalable quantum simulation of continuous-time generative models via tensor networks', arXiv 2608.21700 (search hit only, UNVERIFIED, not read), suggests tensor-network simulation of such coherent flows.
prior_art_known: Layden, Sweke, Havlíček, Chowdhury, Neklyudov, 'Wavefunction Flows: Efficient Quantum Simulation of Continuous Flow Models', arXiv 2510.08462: existence and abstract verified this session, content not audited, NOT in the program bibliography. Noé et al. Science 2019 [#227]; Tan et al. ICML 2025 arXiv 2502.18462 [E79]; Lewis et al. Science 2025 BioEmu [E83]; Jing et al. ICML 2024 arXiv 2402.04845 [E80] (bibliography-verified).
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: very low (<1%). Classical generators already give independent samples, only the reweighting step is left, and the coherent-network overhead is ~1e8x.

title: Composite-likelihood overconfidence as the source of hide-and-seek wells: calibration decides whether the provable continuous quantum-Gibbs separation has any protein instance
protein_question: Does the learned-energy posterior contain narrow, deep, confidently wrong modes whose mass is comparable to the broad native-like basin (persistence / hide-and-seek)? Do those modes survive native-free calibration of the posterior temperature?
quantum_primitive: Continuous quantum Gibbs sampling via QSVT / quantum replica-exchange Langevin (Leng et al. PNAS 2026 [A44]). Olivucci et al. 2026 [A45] prove an Omega(alpha) classical vs O~(sqrt(alpha)) quantum query separation for it on hide-and-seek wells, with alpha = e^{beta·Delta}.
representation: Continuous (theta,tau) or CA Cartesian coordinates. The energy is the A80 soft-bin pair NLL (CA+CB) + the (theta,tau) head + sterics, at temperature T.
mechanism: Where the wells would come from, specific to learned models: E_pair sums ~L^2 pair NLLs as if they were independent, which makes it a pairwise composite likelihood (Varin, Reid & Firth 2011). Its curvature grows with the number of terms (~L^2). The terms share ESM features, however, and carry far less independent information about the 3L-6 degrees of freedom, so the unadjusted posterior is overconfident. A coherent cluster of confidently wrong pair bins creates an alternative basin. S33 measured 1,168 ESM false-positive contacts with median native CA distance 10.2 Å, 57% of them within ±2 register. The basin's depth scales with the number of wrong pairs times their log-odds. Its width is set by the soft-bin width s (A80 D5: p~ -> P_bin as s -> 0). Narrow and deep is exactly the hide-and-seek class. There A45 proves the quantum advantage and Woodard et al. [E39] prove PT/ST torpid mixing. The quantum resource is queries to the energy/gradient oracle. Classical query algorithms need Omega(alpha) to find a narrow well by local exploration, while QSVT filtering of the Witten-Laplacian generator reaches sqrt(alpha). The lower bound holds only in the QUERY model. The learned energy is WHITE-BOX, with explicit per-pair tables, so a classical algorithm can read candidate wells straight from the tables: enumerate high-log-odds contact clusters, run cluster-seeded restarts, and weigh wells by local free energy or bridge sampling. The separation matters for proteins only if narrow high-mass wells (1) survive calibration and (2) are not seeded by identifiable table clusters.
expected_speedup: Quadratic in alpha = e^{beta·Delta} (query model) where hide-and-seek wells exist. Zero if calibration or white-box seeding removes them.
oracle_and_state_prep: A coherent gradient/value oracle for E, built from per-target QROM tables and fixed-point arithmetic; it has never been costed [G-2]. The Omega(1) warm start comes from card 1's product prior plus annealing. At ~1e5-1e7 Toffolis per gradient at L=100 (card 7), the oracle sets the break-even.
strongest_classical_competitor: White-box classical inference: table-cluster enumeration + cluster-seeded L-BFGS restarts + local free-energy / bridge-sampling weights; PT/REST2 with cluster (topology) moves. Decisively, native-free recalibration removes artefactual wells outright: a composite-likelihood magnitude/curvature adjustment, or a T* chosen by held-out coverage of posterior-predictive distances on prots/.
classical_primitive_replaced: PT/Langevin barrier crossing between narrow and broad modes.
information_vs_computation: INFORMATION: the wells are properties of the learned model's calibration, i.e. information artefacts, and the calibrated posterior's mode structure is itself information. COMPUTATION: the quantum part only accelerates crossings between modes. If calibration removes the wells, there was never a computational problem. If well-calibrated narrow modes persist, the hardness is intrinsic to what the model knows and the quantum line stays live.
measurement_readout: Posterior samples, assigned to basins, feeding a soft readout or basin masses (for multi-hypothesis output).
relation_to_S29_S33: OLD MECHANISM: nothing in S29-S33 was sampled. The closest observations are the S33 topology traps (concentrated solvers fall in, the random prior avoids them; OP-05) and the C_contact near-miss lemma. OLD FAILURE: n/a for sampling; the random-prior twin beat VQE only for search. NEW MECHANISM: a named, learned-model-specific source for the only instance class with a provable continuous quantum separation, together with a calibration control that can delete it. WHY OLD CONTROL NO LONGER APPLIES: when weighting narrow against broad modes at T*, the random-prior twin does not produce correct masses. The new controls are recalibration and white-box seeding. This operationalises H-007/G3 for learned priors.
kill_result: Any of: (a) at the native-free calibrated T*, narrow modes hold <5% of posterior mass on all long40 dev targets, or they are not at least 3x narrower than the broad basin (no persistence); (b) >=90% of high-mass narrow modes are seeded by top-k table contact clusters (white-box discoverable at polynomial cost); (c) PT round-trip time at T* grows <= L^3 from 30 to 60 aa.
minimal_classical_first_test: (1) Calibrate T* on held-out prots/ training-distribution chains, never long40: choose T so the 80%/95% posterior-predictive pair-distance intervals cover at their nominal rates (short SMC runs). (2) On 10 long40 dev targets (44-60 aa), run PT with 24 replicas over T in [T*, 30T*]. Cluster samples into basins by contact-map Jaccard or RMSD. For each basin estimate its mass, its width (sample-covariance log-det) and its restart hit probability p_hit (L-BFGS from 1e3 prior draws); the persistence index is mass/p_hit. (3) For each narrow high-mass basin, test whether its discriminating contacts appear among the top-k log-odds clusters of the tables. Repeat at T=1 to show how the artefact scales. About 1 day on 8 cores.
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: TT-cross and other tensor-network methods are also query-like and can miss narrow wells. White-box table enumeration is the stronger classical reproduction.
prior_art_known: Olivucci et al. arXiv 2608.24527 (2026) [A45]; Leng et al. PNAS 123(8) e2512789123 (2026) arXiv 2505.05301 [A44]; Woodard, Schmidler, Huber 2009 [E39] (bibliography-verified). Varin, Reid, Firth, Statistica Sinica 21:5-42 (2011) (verified this session). Composite-likelihood Bayesian adjustments: Pauli, Racugno, Ventura (Stat. Sinica 2011) and Ribatet, Cooley, Davison (Stat. Sinica 2012), UNVERIFIED. The search found no evidence that learned protein pair potentials have been analysed as composite likelihoods or characterised for hide-and-seek structure (scope: bibliography + this session's searches; consistent with gap G-3).
track: C theory + classical landscape census, then B
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low (~5%). Calibration or white-box seeding is expected to remove the wells, but this single measurement decides whether the only provable continuous separation touches learned protein posteriors at all.

title: Schmidt-rank / entanglement audit of the coherent posterior |sqrt(pi)> in sequence order: a dequantisation test for every learned-posterior sampler
protein_question: Is the learned-energy posterior at T* a few-mode object with weak correlations across sequence cuts, whose coherent encoding is a low-bond-dimension MPS/TT (classically representable and, if constructible, exactly samplable)? Or does its bond dimension grow quickly with L?
quantum_primitive: The qsample |sqrt(pi)> produced by any quantum sampler (QSA, quantum Langevin/RELD). The audit bounds what any such sampler can output that a classical tensor-network sampler cannot.
representation: Sequence-ordered discretised (theta,tau) with 216 classes per residue (local dimension 216), optionally coarse-grained to 24-54 classes; MPS/TT in residue order.
mechanism: Across a cut A|B, the Schmidt rank of |sqrt(pi)> equals the rank of the matrix M_ab = sqrt(pi(a,b)). If the posterior consists of M well-separated basins, each with Gaussian-like fluctuations, the rank is about sum_k r_k, where r_k is set by the canonical correlations across the cut inside basin k. Few modes with moderate cross-cut coupling therefore give chi = poly(L), and exact MPS sampling costs O(L·chi^2·d) per sample with no mixing at all. If chi(L) stays small, every quantum sampler's OUTPUT is classically representable. Any remaining quantum claim must then concern PREPARATION, which a classical TT-cross construction on sqrt(pi) (Dolgov et al. 2020) or MPS fitting can also attempt. Caveats: TT-cross is itself a query method and can miss narrow wells (card 4), and interval-scope kinematic factors make naive MPO annealing high-rank (card 12). Low chi is therefore necessary but not sufficient for dequantisation. Conversely, volume-law growth of chi(L) would be positive evidence of glassy many-mode structure, which classical hardness requires, though even then the quantum gain is only sqrt(delta).
expected_speedup: None. This is a dequantisation test: if chi is small and TT-cross succeeds, the quantum speedup is zero.
oracle_and_state_prep: Entirely classical: it needs samples (from the G1 PT runs) or energy evaluations (TT-cross). No quantum oracle is involved.
strongest_classical_competitor: A TT-cross surrogate + conditional-distribution sampler (Dolgov et al. 2020); an MPS Born machine fitted by DMRG-style NLL minimisation (Han et al. PRX 2018, UNVERIFIED this session; the predecessor has MPS Born machine code); importance-corrected MPS samples.
classical_primitive_replaced: The quantum sampler itself; the audit decides whether a tensor-network sampler replaces it.
information_vs_computation: INFORMATION: pi is fixed by the classical learned model and T*. COMPUTATION: chi(L) measures how much classical memory the posterior needs. The quantum part could matter only if chi(L) is large AND classical mixing is slow.
measurement_readout: Held-out NLL as a function of chi, and basin masses and soft readout from MPS samples compared with PT.
relation_to_S29_S33: OLD MECHANISM: the S33 MPS Born machine / tempered circuits (DE-6: 'the MPS Born machine is classically simulable'). OLD FAILURE: the trained quantum model was simulable and the random prior beat it. NEW MECHANISM: the audit targets the posterior's own coherent encoding rather than a variational ansatz, so it bounds any algorithm whose output is |sqrt(pi)>. WHY OLD CONTROL NO LONGER APPLIES: the old control applied to one trained circuit; this is a target-level test.
kill_result: Quantum-sampling claims at a given L are killed if two things hold. First, the chi needed for held-out KL <= 0.05 nats/residue is <= 256 at L=60, with growth no faster than L^2. Second, a sample-free TT-cross construction reproduces the PT basin masses within 10%. The tensor-network sampler then becomes the mandatory classical twin.
minimal_classical_first_test: mid30 first, then long40, 10 targets. Take 1e5 PT samples at T* (from the card 1/4 runs) and discretise them to 216 and 54 classes. Fit an MPS with chi in {8,...,256} by DMRG-style NLL on 80% of the samples, and evaluate held-out NLL and basin masses. Separately, run TT-cross directly on exp(-E/2T*) without samples and compare the masses. Record chi*(L) for L from 25 to 60. Feasible on the CPU, using the d=54 coarse-graining if RAM-bound.
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: This card is itself the tensor-network reproduction attempt.
prior_art_known: Dolgov, Anaya-Izquierdo, Fox, Scheichl, Stat. Comput. 30:603-625 (2020), arXiv 1810.01212, DOI 10.1007/s11222-019-09910-z (verified this session). Han et al. PRX 8,031012 (2018), UNVERIFIED. 'Sampling from Boltzmann densities with physics informed low-rank formats', arXiv 2412.07637 (search hit only, UNVERIFIED). The search found no entanglement or Schmidt-rank characterisation of any protein-structure posterior (scope: bibliography + this session's searches).
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low (~3%). This is a kill test; a high chi would only reopen the sqrt(delta) line, not create a new speedup.

title: Distogram-native state space (per-pair distance bins) conditioned on 3D realizability: exactly preparable pair-product prior with amplitude-amplified feasibility, killed by dimension counting
protein_question: Can the learned distogram be used in its native variables, one 28-bin distance per pair, with the posterior defined as the distogram conditioned on Euclidean realizability? The product prior would then be exactly preparable and quantum search would enforce the geometry.
quantum_primitive: Amplitude amplification / quantum rejection sampling on a coherent realizability predicate (Cayley-Menger or rank-3 Gram test with interval bounds), starting from the pair-product state; or nested/structured search over partial assignments.
representation: b_ij in {1..28} (4-20 Å in 1-Å bins, 22-40 Å in 2-Å bins; s33/esmprior.py), for all L(L-1)/2 pairs (5 qubits per pair) or for the top-k confident pairs.
mechanism: |sqrt(prod p_ij)> is a product of 28-dimensional states, so preparation is exact and cheap. Amplitude amplification gives O(P(F)^-1/2) against O(P(F)^-1) for classical rejection, where F is the set of realizable assignments. Dimension counting kills this. A structure has 3L-6 degrees of freedom (the S29-S33 a≡mu result), while the representation has L(L-1)/2 variables. The realizable assignments therefore occupy dimension ~3L-6 inside a space of dimension ~L^2/2, so P(F) <= exp(-c·(L^2/2-3L+6)) = exp(-Theta(L^2)). The quadratic speedup still leaves exp(-Theta(L^2)/2). Restricting to k≈3L-6 confident pairs (a minimally rigid graph) fixes the count, but interval realizability of sparse distance graphs is strongly NP-hard (Saxe 1979), so the quantum gain over exhaustive search is again only quadratic. Coordinate representations satisfy realizability by construction: the constraint the quantum computer pays for is free classically.
expected_speedup: Quadratic in 1/P(F); the absolute cost is exp(Theta(L^2)) for full distograms.
oracle_and_state_prep: State prep is exact but needs 5 qubits x L^2/2 pairs, ~2.5e4 qubits at L=100, which is prohibitive in itself. The feasibility oracle is a coherent EDM embedding test (fixed-point Gram-matrix eigen- or Cholesky decomposition), which is enormous. Together these erase any gain.
strongest_classical_competitor: Distance geometry (triangle-inequality smoothing + embedding) and the A80 L-BFGS decoder in (theta,tau), which comes within 0.14 Å of the information floor at 44-60 aa (I-5).
classical_primitive_replaced: Distance-geometry embedding.
information_vs_computation: INFORMATION: all of it is in the product distogram. Realizability is known geometry, not information. COMPUTATION: this representation turns a free constraint into an exponentially rare event, so the quantum computer pays for a representation mistake.
measurement_readout: Measure the pair register, then embed the resulting bin assignment.
relation_to_S29_S33: OLD MECHANISM: the S33 contact-subset registers (A30-A34, C_contact; K-005, DNR-08). OLD FAILURE: the subset problem had no headroom (near-miss lemma, inert qubits, QUBO with the wrong sign). NEW MECHANISM: full-distribution conditioning on realizability instead of subset selection. WHY OLD CONTROL NO LONGER APPLIES: moot; a stronger representation-level argument kills it first.
kill_result: Already killed on paper. Confirmation: measured log P(F) falls roughly linearly in the number of included pairs k, with slope <= -0.5 nats per pair, on mid30 targets.
minimal_classical_first_test: On 10 mid30 targets, sample bin assignments from the product distogram for the top-k confident pairs (k = L, 3L, ..., L^2/2). Test realizability with interval distance geometry (bound smoothing + metric-matrix embedding + short refinement) and estimate P(F) as a function of k. Minutes on one core.
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: n/a
prior_art_known: Saxe, 'Embeddability of weighted graphs in k-space is strongly NP-hard' (Allerton 1979), UNVERIFIED this session. Quantum rejection sampling: Ozols et al. [A36] (bibliography-verified).
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: very low (<0.1%).

title: Oracle-aware coherent walk for the actual esmprior_v1 energy: pair-specific QROM tables, symmetric-scan moves and the break-even B(L)
protein_question: What is the cheapest fault-tolerant walk step for a per-target, per-pair tabulated learned energy (28-bin CA and CB tables, a 216-class (theta,tau) table, sterics)? How many classical steps per independent sample must the best classical sampler therefore need before any quantum sampling card can pay off?
quantum_primitive: A Szegedy / Metropolis walk operator (Lemieux et al. [A55] construction) with QROM data loading (unary iteration or select-swap) and reversible fixed-point geometry.
representation: Three choices are compared: (a) (theta,tau) single-angle pivot moves, with O(L^2) pair updates per step; (b) Cartesian crankshaft moves (rotate residue i about the (i-1,i+1) axis), with O(L) pair updates; (c) random versus deterministic symmetric-scan residue selection. The symmetric scan P_1...P_L P_L...P_1 is reversible and keeps the moved residue's index classical, so each table lookup ranges over only 28 bins.
mechanism: The speedup is in walk steps (sqrt(delta)); this card prices one step. The break-even number of classical steps per independent sample is B ≈ (kappa·t_T/t_pair)^2. Here kappa ≈ 1e3 Toffolis per coherent pair-term update (distance squared, inverse sqrt, soft-bin evaluation, accumulation, uncompute). t_T ≈ 1-100 µs per Toffoli, depending on the factories (Sanders/Babbush assumptions). t_pair ≈ 1-10 ns per vectorised classical pair update. That gives B ≈ 1e10-1e16, centred around 1e12-1e14. Classical and quantum pay the same number of pair updates per move, so the representation changes B only weakly; it matters through delta per unit of work, which both sides share. Pair-specific tables (literature gap G-6): with a classical residue index (symmetric scan), each lookup is a 28-entry QROM, ~28 Toffolis << kappa. With a superposed residue index, naive unary iteration costs ~28·L per pair and dominates above L≈70, but select-swap QROM cuts this to ~sqrt(28·L·b). Per-pair learned tables are therefore NOT the dominant cost. This is an I(agent) estimate to be checked in T3, and it corrects the literature phase's 'likely prohibitive' prior.
expected_speedup: None by itself; it turns any measured classical tau(L) into a go/no-go decision.
oracle_and_state_prep: Inputs: the per-target tables (classical ESM-2 + esmprior output, 2·28·L^2 + 216·L numbers) and fixed-point coordinates (b≈16-20 bits). Cost: ~1e5 Toffolis per step (crankshaft) to ~1e7 (pivot) at L=100, plus QROM, on ~1e3-1e4 logical qubits. This overhead erases the speedup unless classical tau >~ B.
strongest_classical_competitor: The same move sets run classically and vectorised (SIMD/GPU), plus PT/HMC, at ~µs per step.

information_vs_computation: INFORMATION: the tables, computed classically and loaded via QROM (no free block encoding). COMPUTATION: walk steps. The card separates data-loading cost from arithmetic cost explicitly.

title: Distogram-to-structure as planted low-rank (rank-3 Gram) inference: a test for the statistical-computational gap where super-quadratic quantum spectral speedups live
protein_question: Is there a regime (length, distogram quality) where the information needed to recover a fold is present in the learned pair distributions but every polynomial-time classical estimator fails to extract it? That hard phase is the only regime where the known super-quadratic (quartic) quantum speedups for planted inference could apply.
quantum_primitive: Quantum phase estimation / amplitude amplification on Kikuchi-type or sum-of-squares spectral matrices (Schmidhuber et al. PRX 2025, quartic speedup for planted inference [C71]; Hastings, tensor PCA [C72]).
representation: The unknown is X in R^{Lx3}, with Gram matrix G = XX^T of rank 3. The observations are the learned pair-bin distributions (order 2) and the (theta,tau) head (local, order 3-4). Higher-order learned observations, such as trRosetta-style inter-residue orientations (Yang et al. PNAS 2020, UNVERIFIED), would make the observation model tensor-like.
mechanism: In planted problems with a hard phase, the best known classical algorithm is a level-l Kikuchi/SoS spectral method costing ~n^l. The quantum algorithm prepares a guiding state and runs phase estimation on the sparse Kikuchi matrix at ~n^{l/4}. That is a genuine super-quadratic speedup relative to the best known classical method: phase estimation on a sparse matrix of dimension n^l never writes the matrix down, whereas classical power iteration must. It is relevant only inside a hard phase. For dense-prior, rank-few matrix observation models, AMP is Bayes-optimal and no hard phase is known (Lesieur, Krzakala, Zdeborová 2017, UNVERIFIED). A hard phase needs sparse or structured priors, or observations of order >=3. The protein evidence so far says the endpoint is information-LIMITED, meaning the information is absent: the opposite regime (H-002; I-5, decoder 4.35 vs information floor 4.21 Å).
expected_speedup: Up to quartic relative to the best known classical Kikuchi method, but only inside a hard phase; zero outside it.
oracle_and_state_prep: A sparse-access oracle to the Kikuchi matrix built from the classical tables (polynomial), and a guiding state from a classical spectral estimate. The speedup is relative to the best known classical method, not a proven lower bound.
strongest_classical_competitor: The A80 L-BFGS decoder with restarts, distance geometry, AMP / spectral MDS on the pair observations, and the long-PT posterior mean (the Bayes estimator; expensive but classical).
classical_primitive_replaced: The spectral/SoS estimator of the fold.
information_vs_computation: INFORMATION: the observation model is the classical learned distogram. COMPUTATION: extracting information that is present but hidden, inside a hard phase. That is the one place where computation rather than information would be the bottleneck, and the test separates the two directly.
measurement_readout: Top eigenvector, converted to coordinates, then decoded.
relation_to_S29_S33: OLD MECHANISM: all S29-S33 inference (selectors, rankers, decoders) at 9-60 aa. OLD FAILURE: information-limited (K-012; DNR-16 requires a new information source, not a new scorer; I-5 decoder at the floor). NEW MECHANISM: a super-quadratic spectral speedup, conditional on a hard phase existing. WHY OLD CONTROL NO LONGER APPLIES: it still applies unless a synthetic planted test finds an SNR window where the Bayes estimator succeeds and polynomial-time estimators fail. The card specifies that measurement.
kill_result: On synthetic planted instances with an esmprior-fitted noise channel, the recovery thresholds (RMSD transition vs SNR) of the Bayes estimator (long-PT posterior mean) and of the polynomial-time decoder coincide within MDE at L = 44-150, and on real long40 the decoder-to-floor gap stays within noise.
minimal_classical_first_test: Take 20 native CA traces (44-150 aa) from prots/, excluding long40 under the R3 leakage rule. Fit a parametric noise channel to esmprior_v1's errors on the training folds (bin confusion vs |i-j|, register-shift false-positive rate). Generate synthetic distograms across an SNR sweep (logit temperature). Compare the 64-restart decoder, the long-PT posterior mean and spectral MDS, and locate each recovery threshold. About 1 day.
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: n/a
prior_art_known: Schmidhuber et al. PRX 15,021077 (2025) arXiv 2406.19378 [C71]; Hastings Quantum 4,237 (2020) arXiv 1907.12724 [C72] (bibliography-verified). Lesieur, Krzakala, Zdeborová, J. Stat. Mech. (2017), UNVERIFIED. The search found no mapping of structure inference from learned distograms onto a planted problem with a hard phase (consistent with gap G-9).
track: C theory/query, with a classical synthetic test
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low (~2%). Every S29-S33 measurement points to absent information, not hidden information.

title: Coarse-grained SSE-topology posterior: learned SSE pairing absorbs the near-miss error mode; walk or backtracking over a non-enumerable topology space
protein_question: At 100-300 aa, is the posterior over secondary-structure-element (SSE) packing topologies (strand order and orientation, helix packing, crossover handedness) under the learned pair model hard to sample or search? Does conditioning the continuous decode on sampled topologies improve the chain?
quantum_primitive: For exact search, Montanaro quantum backtracking [C57] or nested amplitude amplification over partial topologies (Cerf-Grover-Williams 2000, UNVERIFIED). For the topology posterior, QSA / a Szegedy walk over topologies with strand-swap and flip moves.
representation: Hybrid discrete-continuous. There are m predicted SSEs (native-free, from ESM-based SS prediction) and a discrete topology t with m!·2^m raw states: ~2e12 at m=12 and ~2.5e24 at m=20, so non-enumerable at >~150 aa. A continuous decode x|t follows under the A80 energy. The topology free energy F(t) = -T log ∫pi(x|t)dx is approximated by summed SSE-pair log-odds from the distogram.
mechanism: The learned prior creates structure here. S33's near-miss lemma found 57% of ESM false-positive contacts within ±2 residues of a true contact, so the dominant distogram error is a register shift that PRESERVES SSE pairing. Coarse-graining to topology absorbs that error, so the topology-level posterior could pass condition C where residue-level registers failed. The quantum resource is tree nodes: backtracking finds a marked leaf in ~sqrt(T·n) walk steps via phase estimation on the tree walk, against T classically for the same tree. Alternatively it is walk steps over topology moves (sqrt(delta)). Classical search cannot copy the sqrt(T) on the same tree, but exact classical solvers shrink the tree (bounds, DEE, decomposition), and the quantum gain is defined only relative to the same tree.
expected_speedup: At most quadratic in tree size or in 1/delta over topologies, and relevant only if the pruned classical tree exceeds ~1e12 nodes.
oracle_and_state_prep: The coherent partial-topology bound comes from classical SSE-pair tables and is cheap (O(m^2) terms). The continuous decode at each leaf is NOT coherent-friendly (restart-saturated L-BFGS), so the quantum part can act only on the table-level approximation of F(t), whose quality must be checked classically. The uniform root state is cheap.
strongest_classical_competitor: Branch-and-bound / cost-function-network solvers [C82, C83] on the topology tree; beam search; max-weight strand pairing; PT over topologies with strand-swap moves. Also the A80 continuous decoder, which already selects topologies implicitly.
classical_primitive_replaced: Tree search or topology MCMC.
information_vs_computation: INFORMATION: SSE assignments and SSE-pair log-odds from ESM + esmprior. Coarse-graining removes register noise, an information-quality gain that is entirely classical. COMPUTATION: search or sampling over topologies. The likely outcome is that the information gain makes the topology posterior sharp and classically easy: a classical lever, not a quantum one.
measurement_readout: Topology samples, each followed by a conditioned continuous decode, combined into a soft readout over topologies.
relation_to_S29_S33: OLD MECHANISM: structural registers (mosaic, fragment, contact subsets) at 16-90 qubits (K-005; DNR-03, DNR-08), with argmin readouts (H-001). OLD FAILURE: the registers were enumerable, SA/greedy matched, and condition C failed on residue-level energies. NEW MECHANISM: global topology variables that are non-enumerable at m >= ~16, with energies that absorb register-shift errors, consumed as a posterior over topologies. WHY OLD CONTROL NO LONGER APPLIES: DNR-03 lapses because the space is non-enumerable. DNR-08 must be re-tested at topology level, where the near-miss lemma gives a reason it might pass. H-001 still kills any argmin-only use.
kill_result: Any of: (a) the pruned B&B tree at L = 150-300 has <= 1e9 nodes, or the topology posterior entropy at T* is <= 1 nat (classically trivial); (b) topology-level condition C fails on held-out targets (the native topology is not among the low-F(t) states); (c) the topology-conditioned soft readout does not beat the A80 decoder by >= 1.0x MDE.
minimal_classical_first_test: From the existing S33 C_contact rows, recompute the fraction of false-positive contacts that preserve SSE pairing. Then, on long40 plus a 60-150-aa prots/ dev set (R3 leakage rule): run native-free SSE prediction, compute SSE-pair log-odds from esmprior, enumerate exactly or run B&B for m <= 10-14, and record tree size and topology-posterior entropy as functions of m. As an ORACLE diagnostic only, record the native topology's rank. Takes hours.
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: Classical B&B or DP over tree decompositions of the SSE interaction graph.
prior_art_known: Montanaro, Theory of Computing 14(15) (2018) arXiv 1509.02374 [C57] (bibliography-verified); Cerf, Grover, Williams PRA 61,032303 (2000), UNVERIFIED. The search found no quantum treatment of SSE-topology inference from learned contacts (scope: bibliography + this session's searches).
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: very low (~1%) for a quantum advantage; moderate value as a classical representation lever.

title: Learned transport maps shrink what quantum Langevin accelerates: sqrt(C_PI) in raw coordinates (quantum) against C_PI in learned latent coordinates (classical)
protein_question: After classical learned preconditioning, is the Poincaré constant (the inter-basin mixing barrier) of the learned-energy posterior still large enough that a quantum Langevin speedup survives against the best learned-coordinate classical sampler?
quantum_primitive: The quantum replica-exchange Langevin / Witten-Laplacian QSVT sampler (Leng et al. [A44]): O~(sqrt(beta·d·C_PI)) gradient queries against ~C_PI classically.
representation: Raw (theta,tau) or Cartesian x, compared with (i) the prior-quantile transform u_i = F_{q_i}(theta_i,tau_i) from esmprior's own head (no training cost) and (ii) a learned flow latent z = T_phi(x) (NeuTra).
mechanism: C_PI ~ e^{beta·Gamma} for a barrier Gamma. The quantum sampler gets sqrt(C_PI) by singular-value filtering of the generator, a coherent spectral effect rather than parallelism. Learned transports reduce C_PI classically: they straighten anisotropic basins and, if the flow captures the modes, collapse barriers (Hoffman et al. 2019). The quantum sampler could also run in z, but its coherent oracle would then include the network, multiplying cost by ~1e2-1e4. The fair comparison is therefore Q = sqrt(C_PI(x))·C_grad^Q(x) against C = C_PI(z)·C_grad^C(z). If C_PI(z) <= sqrt(C_PI(x)), quantum loses before any overhead is counted. The quantum gain survives only for barriers that learned transports cannot remove, plausibly the narrow wells of card 4, on which flows mode-collapse.
expected_speedup: At most sqrt(C_PI(z_best)) after classical preconditioning; zero if the latent posterior mixes polynomially.
oracle_and_state_prep: A coherent gradient of E in x (~1e5-1e7 Toffolis at L=100, card 7), with the warm start from card 1.
strongest_classical_competitor: NeuTra-HMC (flow-preconditioned), HMC in prior-quantile coordinates, PT/REST2 in the latent space, flow-proposal MCMC and sequential Boltzmann generators.
classical_primitive_replaced: Langevin/HMC mixing between basins.
information_vs_computation: INFORMATION: the transport's geometry comes from the classical prior head or from classical flow training. COMPUTATION: the quantum part improves only the residual barrier crossing. This states the lane's general finding: learned priors mainly remove classical hardness.
measurement_readout: Posterior samples feeding a soft readout.
relation_to_S29_S33: OLD MECHANISM: S33 decoding in CA virtual angles (lesson 15), a representation that made OPTIMISATION easy (restart saturation at 32-64; QX-30, DNR-07). OLD FAILURE: no search gap was left for quantum. NEW MECHANISM: SAMPLING, i.e. inter-basin mixing at T*, in learned coordinates. WHY OLD CONTROL NO LONGER APPLIES: restart saturation concerns the argmin, while C_PI governs the weights between basins, which restarts do not deliver.
kill_result: At T* on long40, the tau_int (slowest observable or TICA timescale) of NeuTra- or u-space HMC is <= sqrt(tau_int of raw-space HMC), or the latent-space round-trip time grows <= L^3 from 30 to 60 aa.
minimal_classical_first_test: On 10 targets each from mid30/long40 at T*, run HMC in raw (theta,tau), HMC in u-space, and NeuTra-HMC with a small IAF (<=1 h CPU per target, reverse KL). Measure tau_int of the energy, contact order and the slowest TICA mode; estimate C_PI from the slowest relaxation; compare the scaling from 25 to 60 aa. Under a day.
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: Flows, NeuTra and Boltzmann generators are the classical ML reproduction.
prior_art_known: Leng et al. PNAS 2026 arXiv 2505.05301 [A44] (bibliography-verified); Hoffman et al., 'NeuTra-lizing Bad Geometry in Hamiltonian Monte Carlo Using Neural Transport', arXiv 1903.03704 (verified this session). The search found no comparison of a quantum sampler with a learned-preconditioned classical sampler (scope: bibliography + this session's searches).

title: Fold-switching sequences as the physically grounded bimodal learned posterior: check that the information exists before asking about sampling hardness
protein_question: For metamorphic (fold-switching) proteins with two populated folds, does a learned-energy posterior represent both folds, and is estimating their relative populations classically hard?
quantum_primitive: QSA / quantum Langevin between two macro-basins (a sqrt gain in e^{beta·Delta} or 1/delta), or quantum-walk hitting between the folds.
representation: (theta,tau) + the A80 energy from esmprior_v1 (or ESM-2 contact maps). The discriminating pair set is the pairs whose native distances differ between the two folds.
mechanism: If the learned energy has two macro-basins of comparable free energy separated by a large barrier (first-order-like), PT/ST mixing is torpid [E39, E40] and a quantum sampler gains a square root in the barrier factor. Classical methods have an easy escape once both modes are known: decodes conditioned on each fold's contact subset, then Delta-F by bridge sampling or MBAR along a restraint path, all polynomial. Quantum matters only if one mode cannot be found by restarts, i.e. it has a tiny basin of attraction but large mass. There is also a precondition. Single-sequence learned models tend to predict one fold (Chakravarty & Porter 2022 [E94]; E105; the AF-cluster claims are disputed [E97-E99]). If the second fold is absent from the ESM features, the posterior is unimodal and the problem is information-limited.
expected_speedup: Quadratic in the barrier factor, but only if both folds are represented and one is invisible to restarts.
oracle_and_state_prep: As in cards 1 and 7.
strongest_classical_competitor: Fold-conditioned restarts + bridge sampling/MBAR; PT/REST2; AF2 subsampling/clustering ensembles [E96, E101]; BioEmu [E83].
classical_primitive_replaced: Inter-fold mixing and relative free-energy estimation.
information_vs_computation: INFORMATION: whether ESM/esmprior encode the second fold at all, which is likely the binding constraint. COMPUTATION: crossing the inter-fold barrier. The card's first test is purely a test of information.
measurement_readout: Fold populations (basin masses) and fold-conditioned soft readouts.
relation_to_S29_S33: OLD MECHANISM: single-native RMSD endpoints, where mirror-rule failures (N29) and topology traps (OP-05) were the only multimodality seen. OLD FAILURE: n/a. NEW MECHANISM: the multimodality is the scientific object (populations), not noise around one native. WHY OLD CONTROL NO LONGER APPLIES: condition C on single-native RMSD is replaced by a population endpoint. DNR-16 (information) still governs.
kill_result: Either (a) the esmprior/ESM-2 pair distributions at fold-discriminating pairs are unimodal (the second fold carries <5% prior mass), so the problem is information-limited and the work stops; or (b) both folds are found within <=1e3 restarts and the bridge-sampling Delta-F converges within <=1e7 steps, so the problem is classically easy.
minimal_classical_first_test: Select ~6 fold-switchers of <=100 aa with both folds in the PDB: e.g. the designed 56-aa GA/GB pairs (Alexander et al. PNAS 2009, UNVERIFIED), the RfaH C-terminal domain, lymphotactin, KaiB. Check leakage against the esmprior_v1 training crops (R3 rule). Run ESM-2 650M on the CPU (<=100 aa fits in ~6 GB) plus esmprior predict. Measure the prior mass on each fold's bins at the discriminating pairs, then run 1e3 A80 restarts and count hits on each fold. Takes hours.
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: n/a
prior_art_known: Chakravarty & Porter, Protein Sci. 31 (2022) [E94]; Wayment-Steele et al. Nature 625 (2024) [E97] and the disputes [E98, E99]; del Alamo et al. eLife 2022 [E96] (bibliography-verified). The search found no quantum-sampling study of fold-switching proteins (scope: bibliography + this session's searches).
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: very low (~1-2%). The second fold is probably absent from single-sequence learned features, and if it is present, two known modes are classically easy.

title: Low-cut-width contact graphs are a false friend: kinematic coupling makes the learned posterior's factor graph dense in every compact representation
protein_question: Does the sparsity, or low treewidth, of the learned confident-contact graph create a structured computational problem that raw folding lacks? Candidates are junction-tree/tensor-network contraction classically, and structured quantum search or quantum tensor-network contraction.
quantum_primitive: Quantum backtracking over tree decompositions / nested amplitude amplification, and Arad-Landau additive-error quantum tensor-network contraction for partition functions.
representation: Three options examined: (i) internal coordinates (theta,tau); (ii) Cartesian or lattice positions; (iii) distance variables on the contact graph.
mechanism: A theoretical kill, one argument per representation. (i) In (theta,tau), the distance d_ij depends on every (theta_k,tau_k) with i <= k < j, so each pair factor has INTERVAL scope. Any long-range contact then makes the factor graph's treewidth Theta(L), whatever the contact graph's treewidth. (ii) In Cartesian or lattice coordinates, factors are pairwise on contacts plus the chain, but excluded volume adds all-pairs factors, and per-residue domains are >~1e4 grid points, so K^tw contraction is infeasible. Lattice classical solvers (PERM/CPSP) already dominate there (G-5). (iii) Distance variables make the factors local but move the difficulty into global realizability (card 6). (iv) Arad-Landau's quantum algorithm has ADDITIVE error relative to a product of tensor norms that exceeds a positive-weight partition function by exp(Theta(L)). That is useless wherever classical multiplicative MCMC/SMC estimates exist. Any structure that would make tensor-network contraction work would also make exact classical DP work. Quantum tensor-network advantages concern complex or unitary-like networks, not positive Boltzmann weights.
expected_speedup: None.
oracle_and_state_prep: n/a (killed before any oracle design).
strongest_classical_competitor: Junction-tree/DP where the treewidth is genuinely small (1D-local energies: S-7), PERM/CPSP on lattices, and SMC/PT otherwise.
classical_primitive_replaced: Exact inference / contraction.
information_vs_computation: INFORMATION: the contact graph is learned information about WHICH pairs interact. COMPUTATION: kinematic coupling, i.e. geometry, is what makes inference dense, and it is the same for classical and quantum. Sparse information does not imply sparse computation.
measurement_readout: n/a
relation_to_S29_S33: OLD MECHANISM: chain-structured (1D-local) energies solved exactly by DP (S-7, QX-17): treewidth 1, no room for quantum. OLD FAILURE: DP was exact. NEW MECHANISM: asks whether learned long-range contacts create exploitable low-treewidth structure beyond 1D. WHY OLD CONTROL NO LONGER APPLIES: DP covers only 1D-local energies; the new kill is the kinematic-coupling argument.
kill_result: Killed on paper. Confirmation: the min-fill treewidth of the interval-scope factor graph is L-O(1) on all long40 targets, while the confident-contact graph has small treewidth, showing the gap is representational.
minimal_classical_first_test: Run the networkx min-fill-in treewidth heuristic on (a) native and esmprior confident-contact graphs (p>0.5) and (b) interval-scope factor graphs, for long40 and mid30. Minutes.
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: n/a
prior_art_known: Arad & Landau, SIAM J. Comput. 39(7):3089-3121 (2010), arXiv 0805.0040 (verified this session); Montanaro backtracking [C57] (bibliography-verified); tree-decomposition side-chain packing (Xu, RECOMB 2005, UNVERIFIED).
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: very low (<0.5%).

title: Learned-energy posterior sampling at 60-150 aa (lead M1: walk/QSA) - full classical twin portfolio and the decisive kill measurement
protein_question: For a fixed, native-free learned energy pi_L ~ exp(-E_esmprior/T) over Calpha internal coordinates (theta,tau), can posterior-averaged (soft) structures be obtained at 60-150 aa? Does the best classical portfolio's cost per independent sample grow past the fault-tolerant break-even B(L)?
quantum_primitive: Quantised Metropolis walk (Szegedy/Lemieux construction) plus adaptive quantum simulated annealing along a beta schedule [A8, A31, A55]. The oracle is a coherent Delta-E over the O(L) pair terms touched by one residue move.
mechanism: The resource sped up is the number of Markov-chain transitions. The walk operator W(P) has phase gap Theta(sqrt(delta)), where delta is the spectral gap of the reversible classical chain P being quantised. QSA along a gapped schedule therefore prepares a coherent pi_L in O~(l/sqrt(delta)) walk steps, against O~(l/delta) classically. A classical computer cannot copy this directly, because the gain comes from phase estimation and reflections on W, not from better proposals. Four caveats bound it: (i) the gain is relative to the SAME chain P, not to a different classical sampler; (ii) classical lifted and non-reversible chains already recover up to a square root on some chains [A14, A15, A18], and non-reversible PT is exactly such a lift on the temperature axis; (iii) from a cold start there is a sqrt(state-space) penalty [A9]; (iv) no-cloning means one sample per anneal.
oracle_and_state_prep: Input: sequence -> ESM-2 650M features -> esmprior pair-distance tables (classical, precomputed once, ~L^2 x 28 numbers). Oracle: Delta-E for one residue move, i.e. O(L) pair terms (sqrt, soft-bin spline, table lookup) plus the Metropolis coin arcsin(sqrt(exp(-beta*dE))). Repo I(agent) estimate: 1e6-1e8 Toffolis per step at L=100 and ~1e4 logical qubits (lit_A section 3.9). Pair-specific tables need QROM loading (gap G-6), which may dominate. State prep: product prior state plus anneal; the warm start needs Omega(1) overlap between consecutive tempered posteriors, which is untested. Verdict: this largely erases the speedup. With a single T-factory at 170 us per Toffoli [A56], the per-step ratio R = t_Q/t_C is ~1e7-1e10, and the quadratic crossover needs ~R^2 classical steps. The repo's optimistic figure with 1e2-1e3 factories is B ~ 1e12 classical steps per independent sample.
strongest_classical_competitor:
Portfolio, all native-free, with equal tuning effort:
(1) Non-reversible PT (Syed et al., JRSS-B 84:321, 2022, 10.1111/rssb.12464). Its round-trip rate does not decay with the number of chains N, unlike reversible PT (diffusive, O(1/N)); the global communication barrier Lambda is measurable from swap rates. Run it over T AND over a Hamiltonian-tempering scale lambda on the long-range pair terms (a REST2 analogue [E47]). Inner moves are HMC/MALA in (theta,tau), which scales as O(d^{1/4}) [E51]; ladders are feedback-optimised [E31, E32].
(2) SMC samplers, AIS and population annealing with MCMC rejuvenation [E74, E75]. These are stable with O(d) stages (Beskos-Crisan-Jasra, AAP 2014, 10.1214/13-AAP951).
(3) Sequential chain-growth SMC/PERM along the sequence [E53].
(4) Optimise-then-sample: prior-initialised multi-start L-BFGS mode discovery (the A80 decoder), then Smart Darting / mode-jumping MH (Andricioaei-Straub-Voter, JCP 2001, 10.1063/1.1358861; Tjelmeland-Hegstad, SJS 2001, 10.1111/1467-9469.00232), within-basin HMC, and bridge-sampling/MBAR basin masses [E69].
(5) Learned-proposal MCMC: flow-augmented MCMC (Gabrie-Rotskoff-Vanden-Eijnden, PNAS 2022, 10.1073/pnas.2109420119), SMC-corrected flows [E79], and the random-prior independence twin (esmprior (theta,tau) plus pair heads as the proposal, with IS/MH correction; this is the DNR-06 analogue).
(6) Tensor-train approximation of the discretised torsion posterior with exact conditional sampling plus IS correction (Dolgov et al., Stat Comput 30:603, 2020, 10.1007/s11222-019-09910-z).
(7) Wang-Landau / multicanonical sampling over E [E56].
(8) Laplace or Gaussian-mixture IS on the decoder minima.
(9) Massive parallelism S; the Babbush break-even T* ~ t_Q^2 * S / t_C [B46].
Known scaling: PT replicas ~ sqrt(N) [E23, E28]; reversible round trips ~ N_rep^2; non-reversible ~ N_rep. Where it breaks: only golf-course, persistence or first-order regimes [E33, E39, E40]. None of these has been measured on a learned energy.
information_vs_computation: Information: every property of pi_L comes from ESM-2 and esmprior, both classical. Computation: the quantum part can only mix faster on that fixed pi_L; it cannot change what the soft readout is worth. If the sampled soft readout does not transmit to chain accuracy (the H-002 information limit), no sampler, classical or quantum, moves the endpoint.
relation_to_S29_S33: OLD MECHANISM: CVaR, argmin or prefix readout of a diagonal register cost (K-001, K-002). OLD FAILURE: solver-equivalence, and random prior sampling beating VQE (DNR-06). NEW MECHANISM: amplifying the spectral gap of a Markov chain whose target is a FIXED continuous posterior, consumed as a whole-distribution soft average, which lies outside H-001's argmin/prefix/convex class. WHY OLD CONTROL NO LONGER APPLIES: R1, R2 and R4 need a circuit that optimises a diagonal cost; here the distribution is specified, not optimised. Still mandatory: DNR-05 (equal tuning) and DNR-06 (random-prior twin, here the prior independence proposal). DNR-10's reopening condition, 'a measured MCMC mixing failure on the target distribution', is exactly the burden of proof. The 1.40x soft-readout signal (QX-28) was an enumerated sum, so it is evidence of value, not of sampling hardness.
kill_result: The single most decisive kill is C_class(L): the energy evaluations the best portfolio member needs to reach CERTIFIED agreement. Certified means: at least 4 independent method-by-seed runs agree on the posterior-mean Calpha structure within 0.1 A and on the masses of every basin carrying at least 1% mass within 0.05, AND a planted narrow-well positive control is detected. Measure it at L = 60, 90, 120 and 150 on at least 10 targets per band. Kill M1 if C_class(150) <= 1e9 (at least 3 decades below the optimistic B ~ 1e12) and the fitted growth keeps C_class(L) < B(L) for all L <= 300. A cheaper, independent kill: at long40, the SAMPLED (not enumerated) soft readout fails to beat the A80 argmin chain by at least 1.0x MDE.
minimal_classical_first_test: Runs in 1 day or less on 8 cores. Instrument: long40 (44-60 aa, 45 targets) with the A80/esmprior energy under a provenance record. Samplers: non-reversible PT (8 chains, HMC in (theta,tau)) and the darting twin, at ~1e7 energy evaluations per target and 4 seeds. Measure (a) sampled soft-readout chain RMSD against the A80 argmin (transmission, with a pre-registered MDE); (b) cost-to-certified-agreement at 44, 52 and 60 aa, plus Lambda(L) and its slope; (c) a positive control: implant a narrow deep well of known mass and check the diagnostics flag it. If (a) fails, M1 is dead at this scale. If (b) is <= 1e7 with a shallow slope, that is a strong prior that C_class(150) << 1e12.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low (~5%): the gain is quadratic, counted in walk steps and needs fault tolerance. It requires >= 1e12 classical steps per sample, while funnels, NRPT and darting are polynomial, and S33 restart saturation at 44-60 aa shows an easily searched landscape at that length.
classical_primitive_replaced: The Metropolis/HMC transition kernel inside PT or SMC (the mixing step).
expected_speedup: At most quadratic in 1/delta of the SAME quantised chain. Wall-clock break-even needs >= ~1e12 classical steps per independent sample under optimistic assumptions (1e14-1e20 against a single core with a single factory).
measurement_readout: One structure per anneal: measure 2L-5 torsions in b-bit registers. A soft readout needs tens of samples, i.e. tens of full anneals.
prior_art_known: [A8] Somma et al., PRL 2008. [A31] Harrow-Wei, SODA 2020 (framed for Bayesian inference). [A55] Lemieux et al., Quantum 2020. [A56] Sanders et al., PRX Quantum 2020. [A65] QFold (<= 1,024 states, matched-Metropolis baseline). Under scope (repo bibliography of 448 papers plus this lane's searches), the search found no evidence of a quantum-walk sampler benchmarked against PT or SMC on any off-lattice protein posterior (repo gap G-4).
representation: Calpha trace in internal coordinates (theta,tau): 2L-5 continuous DOF; b ~ 16-20-bit fixed point in the quantum version.
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: Tensor-train sampling of discretised (theta,tau) (Dolgov 2020), and flows or BioEmu-class generators used as independence proposals with MH/SMC correction. Both are portfolio members and must be tuned with equal effort.

title: Continuous quantum Langevin / replica-exchange sampler (lead M2) vs white-box mode discovery: is the learned landscape hide-and-seek?
protein_question: At 60-150 aa, does the learned-energy posterior contain narrow, deep basins of significant posterior mass (persistence or hide-and-seek) that local descent from the ESM prior fails to find? That is the only instance class with a proven continuous classical lower bound.
quantum_primitive: Witten-Laplacian QSVT / quantum replica-exchange Langevin (Leng et al., PNAS 2026 [A44]), with the provable Omega(alpha) vs O~(sqrt(alpha)) separation, alpha = e^{beta*Delta} (Olivucci et al., arXiv 2608.24527 [A45]).
mechanism: The resource sped up is gradient or value oracle queries. The quantum algorithm singular-value-thresholds an operator whose kernel is sqrt(sigma), costing O~(sqrt(beta*d*C_PI)) with C_PI ~ e^{beta*Gamma}, against ~C_PI for classical Langevin. On hide-and-seek instances, a narrow deep well is hidden in a flat torus and is invisible to values and gradients until probed inside it; any classical query algorithm then needs Omega(alpha) queries, while amplitude-amplification-like interference finds the well's mass in sqrt(alpha). The lower bound is BLACK-BOX. A white-box learned energy is an explicit sum of pair terms whose wells are placed by the distogram, and it offers classical routes the query model forbids: gradient descent from prior-informed starts, and proposals drawn directly from the pair-distance marginals.
