oracle_and_state_prep: A coherent grad-E oracle over 2L-5 torsions: O(L^2) pair terms per gradient (distance, spline derivative, torsion Jacobian). It has never been costed (G-2) and plausibly costs at least the 1e6-1e8 Toffolis of a walk step. Needs d x log(grid) qubits. The warm start |<phi|sigma>| = Omega(1) must come from annealing. Verdict: this erases the speedup unless alpha, counted in oracle calls, is at least ~1e12.
strongest_classical_competitor: The optimise-then-sample twin: prior-initialised multi-start L-BFGS (the A80 decoder), Smart Darting / mode-jumping MH between discovered minima (10.1063/1.1358861; 10.1111/1467-9469.00232), Hamiltonian tempering of the long-range pair scale lambda to widen narrow wells, SMC with distogram-marginal proposals that drop mass directly into narrow distance wells, and non-reversible PT. Scaling: cost = (1/p_hit) x (evaluations per descent, ~1e3-1e4) for mode discovery, plus polynomial within-basin sampling. It breaks only if p_hit decays exponentially in L for significant modes.
information_vs_computation: Information: well positions and depths are encoded in the learned distograms, which are classical. A proposal drawn from those marginals hits a well with probability about equal to its marginal mass; this is how white-box information defeats the black-box lower bound. The quantum part adds query efficiency only where that information is absent from the model.
relation_to_S29_S33: NEW MECHANISM (continuous, query-model separation) that S29-S33 never tested. But S33 E800b is direct evidence AGAINST it at 44-60 aa: min-energy decoy RMSD saturates by 32-64 restarts (7.08 -> 4.40 -> 4.35 A, floor 4.21 A). The deep basins are therefore found by at most 64 local descents, which is the opposite of hide-and-seek. DNR-07 and the killed M9 (amplitude-amplified restarts) bound the related search gain at <= 0.14 A.
kill_result: p_hit(L): for every basin carrying at least 1% posterior mass at L = 60-150, the probability that a single prior-initialised local descent lands in it. Kill M2 at length L if min p_hit >= 1e-4. Then every significant mode is found within 1e4 restarts x 1e4 evaluations = 1e8 evaluations, the darting twin has no hide-and-seek term, and alpha-type barriers do not bind. Cross-check that darting and non-reversible PT agree.
minimal_classical_first_test: Runs in 1 day or less on 8 cores. Take 12 long40 targets and run 1,000 prior-initialised L-BFGS descents each (~12k decodes). Cluster the minima at 1 A Calpha RMSD. Estimate basin masses with a Laplace approximation plus short within-basin HMC and bridge sampling. Report p_hit per basin and the Woodard persistence statistic (mass-to-width ratio across the temperature ladder) [E39]. Positive control: an implanted narrow well of known mass. Kill signal at this length: every basin with >= 1% mass has p_hit >= 1e-3.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low (~3-5%): the separation needs hide-and-seek wells, and funnel theory [E2-E6] and S33 restart saturation argue against them. It is still the best formal match, but the gain is only quadratic in alpha.
classical_primitive_replaced: Langevin / replica-exchange Langevin gradient queries.
expected_speedup: Quadratic in alpha = e^{beta*Delta}, or in C_PI (query model only).
prior_art_known: [A44] Leng et al., PNAS 2026 (arXiv 2505.05301). [A45] Olivucci et al., arXiv 2608.24527 (preprint). [E39] Woodard-Schmidler-Huber, EJP 2009 (torpid PT under persistence). Under scope (repo bibliography plus this lane), the search found no evidence of any landscape census of a learned protein energy (repo gap G-3).
representation: Continuous torsions on a b-bit grid (quantum); continuous (theta,tau) (classical).

title: Converged all-atom equilibrium ensembles of multidomain proteins (300-1000 aa, explicit solvent)
protein_question: What are the Boltzmann populations of interdomain arrangements (open/closed, allosteric and swapped states) of a 300-1000-residue protein under a specified physical force field?
quantum_primitive: Quantum walk, QSA or quantised HMC over the all-atom force field; alternatively, quantum simulation of the classical dynamics.
mechanism: The only candidate mechanism is the quadratic gap amplification of card 1, applied to an all-atom chain. There is no super-quadratic route. MD is chaotic; quantum nonlinear-ODE solvers need dissipation to dominate (R < 1; Liu et al., PNAS 118, 2021, arXiv 2011.03185). When Lyapunov exponents are positive, any algorithm that outputs the normalised solution state costs exponentially in integration time (Lewis-Eidenbenz-Nadiga, Quantum 8:1509, 2024, arXiv 2307.09593).
oracle_and_state_prep: Local MC move: a coherent Delta-E over ~1e3-1e4 short-range LJ and real-space Ewald pairs plus a reciprocal-space update, at ~1e3-1e4 Toffolis per pair, i.e. ~1e7-1e8 Toffolis per step. But local-move MC mixes far worse than MD in explicit solvent. A quantised HMC step needs a reversible full-system force evaluation: ~1e8 pair terms at 1e6 atoms, ~1e11-1e12 Toffolis. Anton 3 runs more than 100 us/day at 1e6 atoms [E18], ~2 us per 2.5-fs step. Per-step ratio R >= ~1e12 (I(prog), order of magnitude), so the quadratic break-even is ~R^2 ~ 1e24 classical steps, against ~4e11 steps for a full millisecond. The speedup is fully erased.
strongest_classical_competitor: Anton-class brute-force MD [E15, E18]; REST2 [E47]; non-reversible PT; MSMs from distributed short trajectories [E66, E67]; metadynamics/OPES on learned CVs [E41-E45]; ML coarse-grained transferable models, >= 1e3x faster [E85, E86]; BioEmu amortised ensembles (~L^2: 4, 40 and 150 min per 1,000 samples at 100, 300 and 600 aa on one GPU; ~1 kcal/mol) [E83]. Scaling: T-REMD replicas ~ sqrt(N_atoms) [E23, E28]; reversible round trip ~ N_rep^2, non-reversible ~ N_rep. MD time must far exceed tau_slow; in BPTI, interconversion is more than 1e3x slower than local relaxation [E15]. Where it breaks: entropic/persistence regimes [E33, E39], cooperative first-order transitions under temperature tempering [E40], and unknown slow CVs. The accuracy floor is force-field error of ~1-2 kcal/mol [B71].
information_vs_computation: Information: the force field, whose 1-2 kcal/mol error sets the accuracy floor. Computation: sampling the slow interdomain modes, which is genuinely expensive. The coherent oracle is so costly that a quadratic gain cannot pay, and pragmatic classical practice already trades exactness for 1e3x speed (ML coarse-grained models, BioEmu).
relation_to_S29_S33: Materially different: a physical all-atom energy at 300-1000 aa, never tested. The OLD FAILURE that still applies is the quadratic-overhead trap (CA-1, [A56]; [A55]: matching a special-purpose MCMC machine needs ~1 ns logical gates). There is also a condition-C analogue: a better-sampled ensemble under a force field with 1-2 kcal/mol error need not be closer to experiment.
kill_result: A written fault-tolerant cost for one coherent all-atom Delta-E or force evaluation that shows R >= 1e10. That puts break-even at >= 1e20 classical steps, far beyond the ~1e12 steps of any millisecond campaign, and kills every quadratic primitive.
minimal_classical_first_test: Paper study plus micro-benchmark, 1 day or less. Count Toffolis for one coherent LJ+erfc pair term at 20-bit fixed point using published arithmetic blocks, multiply by realistic neighbour counts, and time the classical step (numpy or OpenMM-CPU). Compute R and n* = R^2 and compare n* with the published step counts of millisecond Anton campaigns. Kill if n* >> 1e13.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low (<1%): the gain is quadratic, and each coherent step costs roughly 1e10-1e12x a classical step, while the best classical route is special-purpose hardware plus ML coarse-graining.
classical_primitive_replaced: MD/MC propagation used for equilibrium sampling.
expected_speedup: None at wall-clock. A formal quadratic in 1/delta only.
prior_art_known: Under scope (repo bibliography plus this lane), the search found no evidence of a fault-tolerant resource estimate for all-atom protein MC/MD sampling; published estimates cover Ising, SK and LABS only (repo G-2).

title: Rare conformational transitions in >100-residue proteins (ms-s kinetics): splitting methods vs quantum hitting time
protein_question: Rates, pathways and transition-state ensembles of slow (ms-s) conformational changes in proteins over 100 aa (kinase activation, transporter alternating access, metastable serpin-like transitions) under a specified energy.
quantum_primitive: Quantum-walk search and hitting (MNRS, Krovi et al., Ambainis et al. [A2-A4]) and amplitude estimation of transition probabilities [B1, B12].
mechanism: Walk search reaches a marked set (the product basin) in O(sqrt(HT)) steps against the chain's O(HT). Amplitude estimation (AE) estimates a transition probability p to relative error eps in O(1/(eps*sqrt(p))), against Monte Carlo's O(1/(eps^2*p)). Neither can be copied for a brute-force chain. But splitting already beats both asymptotically when a usable reaction coordinate (RC) exists. Adaptive multilevel splitting and weighted ensemble have relative variance growing only ~log(1/p) with an ideal RC (Cerou-Guyader, Stoch Anal Appl 25:417, 2007, 10.1080/07362990601139628; Cerou et al., JCP 134, 2011, 10.1063/1.3518708; the exact variance form is quoted from memory and is UNVERIFIED). Classical cost is then ~log(1/p)/eps^2 against quantum ~1/(eps*sqrt(p)): for p = 1e-12, roughly 28/eps^2 against 1e6/eps. The quantum sqrt(HT) helps only where no usable RC exists and splitting variance explodes; that is the true breaking point.
oracle_and_state_prep: A coherent Markov chain of the physical model (the card-3 oracle problem, ~1e7-1e12 Toffolis per step) plus a native-free marking predicate (a product-basin CV indicator, which is cheap). MNRS search needs the stationary state, which is the card-1/3 problem. The speedup is erased.
strongest_classical_competitor: Weighted ensemble: unbiased with 'superlinear scaling', and folding times of 10 us-100 ms estimated with less compute than one conventional folding event [E62, E63]. Also FFS/AMS; TPS, whose cost scales with path length rather than waiting time [E60]; milestoning [E64]; MSMs [E66, E67], e.g. Src kinase activation (Shukla et al., Nat Commun 5, 2014, 10.1038/ncomms4397); and learned RCs (committor/VAMP-type; specific refs UNVERIFIED). Scaling: brute force ~ exp(beta*dG_barrier) (Kramers [E10]); splitting ~ poly(log 1/p) x path cost with a good RC. Where it breaks: hidden orthogonal slow DOFs, multiple channels, and 'significant' WE run-to-run variance [E63].
information_vs_computation: Information: the energy model and knowledge of the RC. Computation: splitting variance when the RC is poor. Kinetics lie outside this program's structure endpoint.
relation_to_S29_S33: Materially different (kinetics; never tested); repo M3 is WEAK. OLD FAILURE analogue: benchmarking against the brute-force waiting time is the weak-baseline error of DNR-05. The fair comparator is WE or AMS.
kill_result: WE/AMS cost measured to grow at most polylogarithmically in 1/p with learned RCs on realistic transitions over 100 aa. The quantum sqrt(1/p) is then exponentially worse in log(1/p), before counting the card-3 oracle cost.
minimal_classical_first_test: Runs in 1 day or less. On a Calpha Go model or the learned-energy model (a ~56-aa GB1-like chain and a ~100-aa two-state chain), estimate switching or unfolding probabilities p from 1e-3 to 1e-12 with AMS, using (a) fraction of native contacts as the RC and (b) a deliberately degraded RC (mixed with a random projection). Fit cost against log(1/p). Kill if the cost stays <= poly(log 1/p) under (a) and degrades only polynomially under (b).
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low: splitting is exponentially better than sqrt(1/p) wherever an RC exists, and kinetics lie off the structure endpoint.
expected_speedup: sqrt(HT) against HT only relative to the unbiased chain; against splitting there is none.
prior_art_known: [A2-A4] walk search (MNRS SICOMP 2011; Krovi et al., Algorithmica 2016; Ambainis et al., STOC 2020). Under scope, the search found no evidence of a quantum rare-event method compared against WE, AMS or TPS on any biomolecule.

title: Exact, reweightable Boltzmann sampling beyond hexapeptides (flow + importance weights) vs quantum rejection sampling
protein_question: Can independent samples with exact, reweightable Boltzmann weights be generated for 20-150-residue chains under a specified energy, so that ensemble averages and free energies are asymptotically unbiased?
quantum_primitive: Quantum rejection sampling / amplitude amplification from a coherent proposal (Ozols-Roetteler-Roland [A36]; Low-Yoder-Chuang [A37]); QSA along an annealing path as the SMC analogue [A7, A8].
mechanism: Plain importance or rejection sampling from a flow proposal q has an effective sample size that decays exponentially in the mismatch dimension: ESS/n ~ exp(-Var log w), with Var log w growing ~linearly in d for weakly correlated mismatch (Snyder et al., MWR 136:4629, 2008, 10.1175/2008MWR2529.1; Agapiou et al., Stat Sci 32, 2017, 10.1214/17-STS611). Amplitude amplification of the accept flag needs O(P_acc^-1/2) coherent proposal calls, halving the exponent from c*d to c*d/2. That is an absolute exponential ratio classical plain rejection cannot copy. But the right classical twin is not plain IS. SMC tempering with MCMC rejuvenation is stable with O(d) intermediate distributions (Beskos-Crisan-Jasra, AAP 24, 2014, 10.1214/13-AAP951), which is polynomial when a gapped path exists. Against SMC, the quantum analogue is QSA, which is back to card 1's gap-quadratic regime.
oracle_and_state_prep: A coherent, reversible evaluation of the flow (1e6-1e8 parameters; each b-bit multiply ~b^2 ~ 250-400 Toffolis, i.e. ~1e8-1e10 Toffolis per call, plus the Jacobian log-determinant), and of the target energy. Because of no-cloning, every accepted sample costs P_acc^-1/2 coherent calls. The speedup is erased unless P_acc is exponentially small AND no classical annealing path exists.
strongest_classical_competitor: Sequential Boltzmann generators, which achieved the first equilibrium sampling of tri-, tetra- and hexapeptides in Cartesian coordinates [E79]; transferable Boltzmann generators [E78]; Timewarp [E77]; SMC and AIS [E74, E75]; flow-augmented MCMC (Gabrie et al. 2022); BioEmu as an approximate proposal [E83]. Scaling: plain IS is exp(c*d); SMC is ~O(d^2) under regularity. Where it breaks: flow expressivity at large d, and SMC rejuvenation kernels that inherit metastability, which reduces to card 1.
information_vs_computation: Information: the learned flow, a classical model, sets P_acc, and better flows are classical ML progress (repo gap G-12: the frontier is moving). Computation: only the correction of the residual mismatch.
relation_to_S29_S33: Materially different: exact reweighting of a specified energy, not argmin or tail readout. The S33 Born-machine failure (K-007: Metropolis came closer to exact Gibbs on 9 of 10) is the small-scale analogue. Repo M6 is WEAK.
kill_result: SMC-tempering cost (energy evaluations to a fixed relative ESS and fixed log Z error) measured to scale polynomially in L on 20-60-aa chains, at <= 1e8 evaluations at 60 aa. Quantum rejection sampling is then being compared with the wrong baseline, and QSA reduces to card 1.
minimal_classical_first_test: Runs in 1 day or less on 8 cores with the esmprior/A80 Calpha energy. Proposal: a Gaussian mixture on the decoder minima, or the esmprior (theta,tau) plus distance heads. At L = 20, 30, 40, 50 and 60, measure log-ESS per residue for plain IS (fitting c), and the cost for adaptive SMC tempering (100-1,000 particles, HMC rejuvenation) to reach ESS >= 0.5 and a seed-stable log Z. Kill if SMC cost grows no faster than ~L^3 and stays at <= 1e8 evaluations at 60 aa.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low: the exponential IS decay is real, but the classical fix (tempering/SMC) is polynomial on funnel-like targets, and coherent flows are prohibitively expensive.
classical_primitive_replaced: The importance/rejection correction of an amortised proposal.
expected_speedup: exp(c*d) -> exp(c*d/2) relative to plain IS only; relative to SMC, the card-1 quadratic in the gap.
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: Flows, sequential Boltzmann generators and BioEmu are themselves the classical ML reproduction; tensor-train proposals are an alternative (Dolgov 2020).

title: Alternative-state and fold-switch discovery from sequence
protein_question: Given only a sequence, which alternative folds or states carry non-negligible population (e.g. the GA/GB designed switch pair, KaiB, RfaH-CTD, alternative transporter states)?
quantum_primitive: None known. Candidates would be the posterior samplers of cards 1-2, or amplitude amplification of rare-state detection.
mechanism: No quantum mechanism reaches the breaking point. The classical failure is that the learned model assigns near-zero mass to the alternative state, through memorisation rather than learned energetics. Any quantum sampler or search samples the SAME model distribution and, by the data-processing inequality, cannot create mass the model lacks. A quantum primitive could matter only if the model does contain the alternative basin and classical samplers fail to reach it, which is the card-1/2 mixing problem.
oracle_and_state_prep: The learned energy, implemented coherently (as in cards 1-2). A native-free predicate for 'alternative state' does not exist: using the known alternative structure as a marker would violate oracle discipline (a native indicator).
strongest_classical_competitor: AF-Cluster and subsampled-MSA AF2 [E97, E101]; BioEmu [E83]; metadynamics/OPES [E41-E45]; Anton MD. Scaling evidence that compute is not the limit: more than 280,000 AF models gave a 35% success rate, and only 1 of 7 fold switchers outside the training set was captured [E100]. AF2 captured only one conformation for 94% of 98 fold switchers [E94]. Between 0.5% and 4% of PDB proteins switch folds [E95]. Where it breaks: training-set memorisation, i.e. information.
information_vs_computation: Information-limited: more samples from the same distribution did not help [E100], and a quantum component adds no information.
relation_to_S29_S33: The OLD FAILURE applies directly: K-012/DNR-16 (native-free recognition from existing inputs is information-limited; reopen only with a new information source). This is the H-002 null seen in another guise, not a new quantum mechanism.
kill_result: At certified convergence, the learned-energy posterior assigns < 1% mass to the experimentally known alternative fold, independent of sampler. Neither a classical nor a quantum sampler can then recover it.
minimal_classical_first_test: Runs in 1 day or less. Use the GA/GB designed pair (~56 aa, length from memory), where a single substitution switches 4beta+alpha to 3alpha, each fold >90% populated (Alexander et al., PNAS 106:21149, 2009, 10.1073/pnas.0906408106). Run non-reversible PT plus darting on the esmprior energy for both sequences, after a leakage check (esmprior crops <= 72 aa may include GB1/GA homologues). ORACLE-labelled diagnostic: posterior mass within 3 A of each NMR fold. Kill (information-limited) if posterior mass does not shift between the folds with the mutation.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low (very low): information-limited, and the data-processing inequality applies.
prior_art_known: Under scope, the search found no evidence of a quantum method for alternative-state discovery tested against AF-Cluster or BioEmu.

title: Free energies of large conformational changes (Delta-G between functional states, >200 aa)
protein_question: The free-energy difference (population ratio) between two functional states, such as kinase active/inactive or transporter open/closed, and its shift on mutation or ligand binding, to <= 1 kcal/mol.
quantum_primitive: Amplitude estimation / quantum mean estimation [B1, B12]; quantum partition-function estimation (Wocjan et al.; Montanaro; Harrow-Wei; Cornelissen-Hamoudi [B24, B26-B28]).
mechanism: AE needs O~(sigma/eps) samples against Theta(sigma^2/eps^2): quadratic in precision. Quantum partition-function algorithms need O~(log^{3/4}|Omega|/(eps*sqrt(delta))) walk steps against O~(log|Omega|/(eps^2*delta)). Both need coherent stationary states, and the sqrt(delta) factor IS card 1's walk speedup; the eps factor attacks variance. The classical breaking point is not variance but (i) force-field bias (RMS 1-2 kcal/mol [B71]) and (ii) slow orthogonal modes that cause hysteresis between windows, which is a mixing problem. (i) is information, and (ii) reduces to card 1. Statistical precision of <= 0.1 kcal/mol is routine, and MBAR is optimal [E69].
oracle_and_state_prep: A coherent Boltzmann state per lambda-window or string image (the card-1/3 oracle) plus a coherent observable. Grover-Rudolph loading gives no speedup [B37]. Break-even needs sigma/eps >= ~1e4 (repo CA-4 arithmetic), while protein decisions need sigma/eps ~ 10-100. The speedup is erased.
strongest_classical_competitor: String method in CVs (Maragliano et al., JCP 125, 2006, 10.1063/1.2212942) with umbrella sampling and MBAR [E69]; metadynamics/OPES [E41-E45]; MSMs (e.g. Shukla et al. 2014); staged nonequilibrium work (single-step exponential averaging needs N ~ exp(beta*W_d), which staging removes [E72]); alchemical FEP+ for mutations [E73]; BioEmu Delta-G at ~1 kcal/mol for monomers [E83]. Where it breaks: hysteresis from hidden slow DOFs, and force-field error.
information_vs_computation: Information: the accuracy of the force field or learned energy sets the 1-2 kcal/mol floor. Computation: mixing of the slow orthogonal modes, not variance.
relation_to_S29_S33: The OLD FAILURE applies: repo M4 is KILLED (practical) and M5 is WEAK, and S29-S33 H-005 was retired because every limit was bias or information. Only the mixing part survives, and that is card 1.
kill_result: Replicate runs show bootstrap sigma_stat << the protocol-to-protocol systematic spread (hysteresis plus energy-model error) at feasible budgets. A precision speedup is then irrelevant.
minimal_classical_first_test: Runs in 1 day or less. On the learned Calpha energy at 40-60 aa, take two decoder-found basins per target and compute Delta-F by (a) MBAR over non-reversible PT, (b) darting plus bridge sampling, and (c) umbrella sampling along an RMSD path, with 4 seeds each. Compare sigma_stat with the method-to-method spread. Kill if sigma_stat < 0.2 x the systematic spread.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low (very low): bias- and mixing-limited, not variance-limited.

title: Cryo-EM heterogeneity inference: pose and state marginalisation over 1e5-1e7 particles
protein_question: Recover the discrete classes and the continuous conformational landscape, with populations, of a macromolecule from 1e5-1e7 noisy 2D projections of unknown pose.
quantum_primitive: Grover / Durr-Hoyer maximum finding over each particle's pose-by-state grid; amplitude estimation of marginal likelihoods (the E-step).
mechanism: Each particle's search runs over N_pose (SO(3) x shifts, ~1e5-1e6 at 1-2 degrees) times K states. Grover would find the best pose in sqrt(N_pose*K) coherent likelihood calls. Classically, the E-step is embarrassingly parallel and linear in particle count, and it is already pruned by branch-and-bound (cryoSPARC) or amortised by encoders (cryoDRGN, cryoFIRE). The real breaking point is statistical: at per-particle SNR ~0.01-0.1 the pose and state posteriors are broad, so even the Bayes-optimal estimator errs. That is information, not search. RELION's E-step is also a marginalisation (a sum over poses), and exact grid sums leave no variance for AE to reduce.
oracle_and_state_prep: A coherent image-formation model: a Fourier-slice projection of a D^3 volume (D = 128-400) at a superposed pose, the CTF, and a Gaussian log-likelihood against the particle. Each particle's D^2 ~ 1e4-1e5 pixels must be loaded per query (via QRAM or re-encoding, Omega(D^2) [CA-5, F56]), which matches the classical per-pose FFT cost and erases the sqrt(N_pose) gain. The readout gives only the argmax, not the marginals the method needs.
strongest_classical_competitor: RELION Bayesian EM with pose marginalisation (Scheres, JMB 415:406, 2012, 10.1016/j.jmb.2011.11.010); cryoSPARC SGD plus branch-and-bound (Punjani et al., Nat Methods 14:290, 2017, 10.1038/nmeth.4169); 3DFlex (Nat Methods 20:860, 2023, 10.1038/s41592-023-01853-8); cryoDRGN (Nat Methods 18:176, 2021, 10.1038/s41592-020-01049-4); RECOVAR (Gilles-Singer, PNAS 122, 2025, 10.1073/pnas.2419140122); MD-ensemble reweighting against particle images (Tang et al., JPCB 127:5410, 2023, 10.1021/acs.jpcb.3c01087; BioEM, CPC 210:163, 2017). Benchmark: CryoBench (arXiv 2408.05526). Scaling: O(N_particles x N_pose_eff x K x D^2 log D), GPU-hours to days. Where it breaks: SNR, particle count, and forward-model mis-specification.
information_vs_computation: Mostly information (SNR, particle count, model mis-specification). The computation is linear and parallel.
relation_to_S29_S33: A materially different domain (an experimental inverse problem, never tested). OLD FAILURE analogue: DNR-03 (quantum search over enumerable registers); per-particle pose grids are enumerable and are enumerated.
kill_result: Exact exhaustive-grid Bayesian marginalisation gives no class or pose accuracy gain over branch-and-bound or amortised heuristics at realistic SNR. Then no search speedup has headroom.
minimal_classical_first_test: Runs in 1 day or less. Simulate 2e4 particles (64^2 px, with CTF) from two conformations of a ~100-aa protein at SNR 0.1, 0.03 and 0.01. Compare class-assignment and population accuracy of (a) exhaustive grid marginalisation (~5k orientations x shifts, FFT, 8 cores), (b) coarse-to-fine branch-and-bound, and (c) plain EM. Kill if the (a)-(b) gap is within noise while all three degrade with SNR (information-limited).
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low (very low): the computation is linear and prunable, and the limit is information.
prior_art_known: Under scope (one WebSearch on 2026-09-26 plus the repo bibliography), the search found no evidence of a quantum algorithm for cryo-EM pose or heterogeneity inference.

title: Low-SNR heterogeneous orbit recovery (cryo-EM/MRA) as planted inference: the only super-quadratic (Kikuchi-quartic) match found
protein_question: At very low SNR (small proteins, few particles per state), is there a statistical-computational gap in which heterogeneous structures are information-theoretically recoverable but no known polynomial-time classical algorithm recovers them?
quantum_primitive: Kikuchi-method guided-sparse-Hamiltonian phase estimation (Schmidhuber-O'Donnell-Kothari-Babbush, PRX 15:021077, 2025, arXiv 2406.19378 [C71]; Hastings, tensor PCA [C72]).
mechanism: For planted noisy kXOR and tensor PCA, the best known classical algorithm builds a Kikuchi matrix of dimension ~n^l and finds its top eigenvector (cost ~n^l). The quantum algorithm prepares a guiding state with inverse-polynomial overlap and runs phase estimation on the sparse Kikuchi Hamiltonian using ~log(n^l) qubits, at cost ~n^{l/4}. That is nearly quartic, and the classical power method must touch the matrix entry by entry. The protein mapping is structural: heterogeneous orbit recovery is solved by invariant methods (moments, bispectrum), i.e. low-rank decomposition of noisy tensors. Homogeneous cryo-EM needs ~sigma^6 samples with invariants of degree <= 3 (Bandeira et al., ACHA 2023, 10.1016/j.acha.2023.06.001; Perry et al., SIMODS 1:497, 2019, 10.1137/18M1214317). A computational gap for heterogeneous MRA is conjectured in the literature (UNVERIFIED; e.g. Boumal et al., CISS 2018, 10.1109/ciss.2018.8362313). No mapping of cryo-EM to a sparse Kikuchi instance exists.
oracle_and_state_prep: Sparse access to a Kikuchi matrix built from empirical image moments: aggregating the moments is classical, O(n*D^2), which is fine. A guiding state is also needed. It is unknown whether the SO(3)-plus-projection structure yields a sparse Kikuchi instance at all, and the level l needed for signals with ~1e6 voxels (D^3) is probably enormous. That likely erases the gain.
strongest_classical_competitor: EM/ML with pose marginalisation (RELION); bispectrum inversion (Bendory et al., IEEE TSP 2018, 10.1109/tsp.2017.2775591); spectral and Kam invariant methods; and collecting more particles, because information can be bought with microscope time. Where it breaks: only inside a hypothetical computational-gap window of SNR and sample count.
information_vs_computation: The target regime is by definition one where information suffices but computation does not. In practice cryo-EM escapes by buying information (more particles), so any gap is probably not economically binding.
relation_to_S29_S33: NEW MECHANISM relative to S29-S33 (super-quadratic planted inference, never tested). The repo's M12 verdict (WEAK: 'requires information present but hidden') applies in spirit.
kill_result: Toy heterogeneous-MRA instances show polynomial classical algorithms (multi-restart EM, bispectrum) reaching the information-theoretic sample threshold within a constant factor for all K. With no gap there is no room for a Kikuchi speedup.
minimal_classical_first_test: Runs in 1 day or less. 1-D heterogeneous MRA over Z/p (p = 21-41, K = 2-8 classes, sigma from 1 to 8). Estimate the information-theoretic threshold by exact likelihood or posterior on small instances, and compare the sample thresholds of multi-restart EM, bispectrum inversion and a spectral method. Kill if the thresholds coincide across K. If a K-dependent gap appears, write the Kikuchi mapping as a theory note only.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low (~1-2%): the mapping is unproven, data can be bought, and signals are D^3-scale.
expected_speedup: Near-quartic over the Kikuchi spectral method, if a mapping exists (polynomial, super-quadratic).
prior_art_known: [C71] Schmidhuber et al., PRX 2025; [C72] Hastings, Quantum 2020. Under scope, the search found no evidence of planted-inference quantum speedups being mapped to cryo-EM or MRA (repo gap G-9).

title: IDP ensemble inference against SAXS / NMR / smFRET data
protein_question: Which conformational ensemble of a 50-500-residue disordered region is consistent with ensemble-averaged experimental observables, and with what uncertainty?
quantum_primitive: None known. Candidates would be quantum convex solvers or QSVT for the reweighting program, or quantum samplers for the prior pool.
mechanism: There is no mechanism to accelerate. The classical pipeline has two steps. (i) Generate a prior pool with a coarse-grained model, already done at proteome scale (28,058 IDRs, CALVADOS [E88]). (ii) Max-entropy / Bayesian reweighting, a convex problem whose dual has dimension m = number of observables (10-1,000) and solves in seconds (BME: Bottaro-Bengtsen-Lindorff-Larsen 2020, 10.1007/978-1-0716-0270-6_15; metainference: Bonomi et al., Sci Adv 2, 2016, 10.1126/sciadv.1501177). The breaking points are underdetermination (m << 3N x n_conf, so many ensembles fit), forward-model error (SAXS hydration layer, chemical-shift predictors) and prior coverage (collapse of the Kish ESS). All three are information.
oracle_and_state_prep: Not applicable. A quantum convex solver would need QRAM loading of an n_conf x m forward-model matrix; classically this problem is dequantised and takes milliseconds (CA-5, CA-6).
strongest_classical_competitor: CALVADOS with BME, EOM or metainference; idpGAN / ML coarse-grained generators [E82]; coarse-grained MD. Scaling: pool generation is linear in the pool size; reweighting is a convex program in m dimensions. Where it breaks: information (few, noisy observables).
information_vs_computation: Entirely information-limited.
relation_to_S29_S33: The OLD FAILURE applies directly: DNR-18 / K-011 (classical convex readout programs dressed as quantum, solved in milliseconds).
kill_result: Already killed by construction; demonstrate once. Convex reweighting runs in seconds, and the family of ensembles that fit the data is broad.
minimal_classical_first_test: Runs in 1 day or less. For a synthetic 100-aa IDR, generate a 1e4-member coarse-grained pool, a hidden 'true' reweighted ensemble, and synthetic SAXS plus PRE data. Run BME and report solve time, Kish ESS, and the diversity of weight vectors fitting within chi^2. Kill confirmed if the solve takes < 1 min and the fitting family is broad.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low (very low): convex and information-limited.

title: Structure from sparse NMR distances (discretizable molecular distance geometry): branch-and-prune vs quantum backtracking
protein_question: Enumerate all backbone embeddings consistent with sparse, interval-valued NOE-like distances and covalent geometry, for 60-150 aa.
quantum_primitive: Montanaro quantum backtracking, O(sqrt(T) n^{3/2} log n) on the same tree [C57], and tree-size estimation [C58]. Also Grover over 2^{n-3} leaf strings (Lavor-Marquezino-Oliveira-Portugal, QIP 21:239, 2022, 10.1007/s11128-022-03583-w, compared only against brute force).
mechanism: The discretizable molecular distance geometry problem (DMDGP) has a finite binary tree: each new atom sits at one of two positions fixed by its three predecessors. Branch-and-prune (BP) explores this tree with a native-free pruning predicate (the placement must satisfy the available distances). Quantum backtracking traverses a T-node tree in ~sqrt(T) poly(n) walk steps with the same predicate, a quadratic gain over the same tree. Classical pruning, however, shrinks T sharply: for protein-like pruning patterns the number of realisations is bounded (Liberti et al., DAM 165:213, 2014, 10.1016/j.dam.2013.01.020; the exact bound is from memory and UNVERIFIED). When T does explode (sparse or ambiguous NOEs, interval branching), the square root of an exponential is still exponential.
oracle_and_state_prep: A coherent predicate: fixed-point placement of atom i from three predecessors (sqrt and trig), then checks against O(#pruning distances) intervals, ~1e4-1e6 Toffolis per node (I(prog)). Interval data force discretisation into k samples per interval, giving 2k-way branching. The FT overhead plus a reversible predicate erase a quadratic gain unless T >~ 1e12+.
strongest_classical_competitor: BP/iBP (Lavor et al., COA 52:115, 2012, 10.1007/s10589-011-9402-6; Liberti et al., SIAM Rev 56:3, 2014, 10.1137/120875909); torsion-angle simulated annealing (CYANA/XPLOR-NIH; refs UNVERIFIED here); SDP relaxations; and today, AF2/ESMFold models refined against NOEs. Scaling: worst case 2^{n-3} leaves, often far smaller with pruning. Where it breaks: sparse or ambiguous data, where the solution set itself grows.
information_vs_computation: Where T explodes, the number of feasible embeddings grows too (underdetermination, which is information). Where the data are rich, T is small. Learned priors now supply the missing information classically.
relation_to_S29_S33: Analogous to repo M10 (backtracking, WEAK) and to K-005/DNR-03 (search over enumerable structural registers). It differs only in using a feasibility predicate on real NMR input rather than an H-001 argmin; the CSP result that speedups 'disappear' once decoding costs are counted [C63] applies.
kill_result: T(n) measured on realistic restraint sets grows slowly, OR the number of feasible leaves S grows in proportion to T (the problem is underdetermined). Either leaves no useful quadratic window.
minimal_classical_first_test: Runs in 1 day or less. From 20 PDB proteins (60-150 aa), derive NOE-like interval sets (H-H <= 5 A, +/-20% intervals, 30% random dropout). Run iBP (Python plus numba, 8 cores), counting nodes T and feasible leaves S, and fit log T and log S against n. Kill if log T grows slowly or S/T stays bounded below.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low (very low): classical pruning collapses the tree, and where it cannot, the problem is information-limited.
prior_art_known: Lavor et al., QIP 2022 (Grover versus brute force only; no BP baseline). Under scope, the search found no evidence of quantum backtracking benchmarked against iBP on protein data.

title: Integrative-modelling posteriors of large assemblies (sparse crosslinks + low-resolution EM + learned priors)
protein_question: Sample, to certified exhaustiveness, the posterior over positions and orientations of tens to hundreds of subunits given sparse heterogeneous data (e.g. the nuclear pore complex; Kim et al., Nature 555:475, 2018, 10.1038/nature26003).
quantum_primitive: Quantum walk / QSA on the integrative score (the card-1 machinery).
mechanism: The resource is the same as in card 1: walk steps, quadratic in the gap of the quantised replica-exchange Gibbs chain. The classical breaking point is many near-degenerate arrangements consistent with sparse data (high posterior entropy and comparable-mass modes, which is persistence-like [E39]), together with rigid-body moves that are rarely accepted at high packing. Exhaustiveness is certified empirically by split-sample tests (Viswanath et al., Biophys J 113:2344, 2017, 10.1016/j.bpj.2017.10.005).
oracle_and_state_prep: A coherent score: crosslink restraints (O(#XL)), cross-correlation of bead Gaussians against the EM map (O(#beads x voxels within cutoff)), and excluded volume. That is ~1e8-1e10 Toffolis per step (I(prog)) plus QRAM loading of the map. The speedup is erased.
strongest_classical_competitor: IMP replica-exchange Gibbs sampling MC with the split-sample exhaustiveness protocol; non-reversible PT; SMC; hierarchical coarse-to-fine sampling; initialisation from learned priors such as AF-Multimer subcomplexes assembled with CombFold (Shor and Schneidman-Duhovny, Nat Methods 21:477, 2024, 10.1038/s41592-024-02174-0). Scaling: not characterised in the literature found; the exhaustiveness protocol reports the achieved precision, not cost against subunit count. Where it breaks: many comparable-mass modes and dense packing.
information_vs_computation: Sparse data make the posterior genuinely broad, and that width is the scientific answer (information). The computational part is exhaustiveness at the stated precision.
relation_to_S29_S33: A new target distribution (physically and data-defined, not learned), never tested. The generic conditions of card 1 apply, and DNR-10 requires a measured mixing failure first.
kill_result: Split-sample exhaustiveness is reached with <= 1e9 score evaluations at realistic subunit counts, with cost growing polynomially in the number of subunits.
minimal_classical_first_test: Runs in 1 day or less. Build a synthetic assembly of 10-40 rigid bodies from a PDB complex, with 3-5 simulated crosslinks per interface and a 20 A density map. Run RE-Gibbs, non-reversible PT and SMC, and measure the evaluations needed to pass the Viswanath four-test protocol against subunit count. Kill if the growth is a low-degree polynomial with <= 1e9 evaluations at 40 bodies.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low: the gain is quadratic, the oracle is heavy, and the posterior width is largely information.

title: Exponential-dimension simulation of protein mechanics (coupled-oscillator and Carleman quantum ODE solvers)
protein_question: Global dynamical observables of elastic-network or MD models of very large assemblies (1e5-1e7 beads), such as energy transfer between domains or the response to a local perturbation.
quantum_primitive: Simulation of 2^n coupled classical oscillators (Babbush-Berry-Kothari et al., PRX 13:041041, 2023, arXiv 2303.13012); quantum Carleman linearisation for dissipative nonlinear ODEs (Liu et al., PNAS 2021, arXiv 2011.03185).
mechanism: Newton's equations for harmonic springs map to a Schrodinger equation whose amplitudes encode the momenta and displacements of 2^n oscillators. With efficiently queryable masses and springs and an efficiently preparable initial state, the cost is poly(n), and classical algorithms provably need 2^{Omega(n)} oracle queries for observables such as the kinetic energy of a subset. This is a genuine exponential, but only for exponentially many oscillators whose springs are given by a compact formula. For anharmonic, chaotic protein MD, any algorithm that outputs the normalised solution state costs exponentially in time when Lyapunov exponents are positive (Lewis et al., Quantum 8:1509, 2024, arXiv 2307.09593), and Carleman linearisation needs a dissipation-dominated regime (R < 1).
oracle_and_state_prep: Protein elastic-network models (ENMs) are defined by N explicit coordinates, with N <= ~1e7 even for the largest assemblies. The spring oracle needs those coordinates loaded, at Omega(N) cost or via QRAM, so the problem size is polynomial and the 2^n regime is never entered. The speedup is erased entirely.
strongest_classical_competitor: Sparse Lanczos / shift-invert normal modes of the ENM Hessian (3N x 3N, O(N) work per iteration), with exact analytic harmonic propagation from the modes; Anton or GPU MD for the nonlinear case. Scaling: poly(N), minutes to hours at N ~ 1e6. Where it breaks: large conformational changes are anharmonic, where ENMs lose meaning rather than becoming hard.
information_vs_computation: Information: the coordinates and the spring model (classical). The harmonic model carries little information about large conformational change.
relation_to_S29_S33: A NEW MECHANISM (genuinely exponential, simulation type; absent from S29-S33). It is killed by CA-5 (data loading) and by the input size being polynomial rather than exponential.
kill_result: Exact classical computation of the target observable at the largest biologically relevant N finishes in <= CPU-hours.
minimal_classical_first_test: A few hours or less. Build Calpha ENMs (10-15 A cutoff) from 1e3 up to 1e6 beads by tiling a large complex. Compute the lowest 200 modes with a sparse eigensolver and propagate a local perturbation analytically, recording wall-clock and RAM (under the 95% ceiling). Kill if N = 1e6 completes in a few CPU-hours.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low (~0): the exponential needs exponentially many formula-defined oscillators, and proteins supply neither.
expected_speedup: Exponential in the query model for 2^n oscillators; none for explicitly specified N-bead proteins.

title: Ensemble-based design scoring: conformational partition functions over rotamers (K*)
protein_question: For each candidate sequence, compute bound and unbound conformational partition functions over side-chain rotamers (plus limited backbone flexibility) to eps-accuracy, in order to rank binders or stabilisers.
quantum_primitive: Quantum counting / quantum partition-function estimation (Wocjan et al., Montanaro, Harrow-Wei, Cornelissen-Hamoudi [B24, B12, B26, B28]); Grover-type enumeration of low-energy conformations.
mechanism: Quantum counting estimates the number or weight of conformations below an energy threshold with square-root queries relative to classical Monte Carlo counting, and quantum partition-function algorithms improve sqrt(delta) and eps quadratically over MCMC estimators. But the classical incumbents are not MCMC. A*/DEE enumeration in energy order with provable eps-bounds (BBK*: Ojewole et al., J Comput Biol 25:726, 2018, 10.1089/cmb.2017.0267) and cost-function networks or tree decomposition [C82, C83] cost as much as the number of conformations inside the energy window needed for eps, which is small on real designs.
oracle_and_state_prep: A coherent pairwise rotamer-energy table (O(n_res^2 x rot^2) entries via QROM) plus a threshold comparator. Loading costs as much as the classical precomputation, which erases the gain unless the window holds astronomically many states.
strongest_classical_competitor: OSPREY K*/BBK*, toulbar2 cost-function-network counting, tree decomposition. Design is NP-hard in the worst case (Pierce and Winfree, PEDS 15:779, 2002, 10.1093/protein/15.10.779) but solved exactly in practice. Scaling: exponential in treewidth, small on protein interaction graphs. Where it breaks: very flexible designs with many mutable positions.
information_vs_computation: Information: the accuracy of the rotamer energy function dominates design outcomes. Computation: enumeration within a window, which is typically small.
relation_to_S29_S33: Repo M5 is WEAK (deterministic incumbents; only sqrt(delta) matters) and M10 is WEAK; the DNR-03 analogue (enumerable registers) applies.
kill_result: BBK* or A* needs <= 1e6 enumerated conformations per sequence to reach an eps = 0.1 bound at realistic design sizes (seconds of CPU). Then there is no quantum window.
minimal_classical_first_test: Runs in 1 day or less. Write a small A*/DEE bound enumerator in Python for 10-25 flexible positions (Dunbrack-like rotamers, simple pairwise energy). Count the conformations needed for an eps-bounded log Z, and compare with the square-root count a quantum counter needs plus QROM loading. Kill if the counts are <= 1e6.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low (very low): incumbents are exact and bound-based, and the enumeration windows are small.

title: Low-SNR heterogeneous cryo-EM as planted tensor inference: Kikuchi-type quartic quantum spectral methods
protein_question: Can the K conformational states and pose distribution of a small (<~60 kDa) or flexible protein be recovered from 10^5-10^7 cryo-EM particle images whose per-image SNR is too low for pose assignment? This is the regime where the structure is information-theoretically recoverable from aggregate statistics (invariant moments, multi-frequency pairwise relations) but polynomial-time algorithms are conjectured to fail (a statistical-to-computational gap).
representation: Invariant moment tensors of the image distribution: power spectrum and bispectrum/3rd-order moments. Heterogeneity is a mixture of K orbits, which may make the tensor decomposition overcomplete. Alternative: multi-frequency group synchronization over SO(2)/SO(3) with pairwise common-line relations (the Perry-Wein-Bandeira-Moitra model).
quantum_primitive: A Kikuchi-hierarchy spectral method run as quantum phase estimation on the sparse level-l Kikuchi matrix, with a guiding state built from the input tensor plus amplitude amplification (Hastings 2020 [C72]; Schmidhuber et al. 2025 [C71]).
classical_primitive_replaced: Power iteration / Lanczos on the n^l-dimensional Kikuchi (or sum-of-squares) matrix, the best known classical algorithm inside the conjectured-hard band.
mechanism: Inside a statistical-computational gap, the best known classical algorithms are subexponential spectral methods. Their cost is set by the dimension n^l of a Kikuchi matrix; the level l grows as SNR falls. The planted signal is that matrix's top eigenvector, separated from the random bulk by a spectral gap. Quantum: phase estimation isolates the planted eigenspace. A guiding state built from the input tensor has quadratically larger overlap than a random state (Hastings), and amplitude amplification takes a further square root, so the cost is ~n^{l/4} vs ~n^l: the 'nearly quartic' speedup of [C71]. A classical computer cannot copy this: the gain comes from phase estimation plus amplitude amplification acting on amplitudes of an n^l-dimensional vector, which a classical algorithm must store and multiply explicitly. The resource is the dimension of the spectral certificate, not sampling or search. Caveats: this is a speedup over the best KNOWN classical algorithm, conditional on low-degree/SoS hardness, not a proven separation. It exists only if practical instances actually sit inside the gap.
expected_speedup: Up to ~quartic in Kikuchi dimension (n^l -> ~n^{l/4}) relative to classical Kikuchi at the same level. Zero if practical cryo-EM instances lie outside the gap (EM/AMP succeed) or below the information threshold.
oracle_and_state_prep: Input: moment tensors computed classically from N images, O(N d^3) flops after dimension reduction to d ~ 10^2-10^3. Needs sparse coherent access to Kikuchi entries, which are products of tensor entries, i.e. a QROM over d^3 words (10^6-10^9). QROM cost per query is ~linear in table size (I(prog)), so the speedup survives only when l is large enough that n^{l/4} dominates the per-query loading cost. The guiding state is built from the data (no free state prep), and no native indicator is used. OPEN: the mapping from SO(3) heterogeneous cryo-EM to a problem whose best classical algorithm is Kikuchi-type is not established.
strongest_classical_competitor: Maximum-likelihood EM with pose marginalisation (RELION/cryoSPARC class); amortised neural inference (cryoDRGN/cryoFIRE-type); AMP for multi-frequency synchronization (Perry-Wein-Bandeira-Moitra 2018); method of moments with frequency marching, Jennrich or SoS tensor decomposition. Experimental workarounds (scaffolds, fiducials, phase plates) raise per-image SNR and can remove the gap regime entirely.
information_vs_computation: Information: the particle images. They are a new per-target information source, exactly what DNR-16/K-012 say is missing. Computation: extracting information that is statistically present in aggregate but conjecturally hidden from polynomial-time algorithms. The quantum part adds only computation and cannot help below the information-theoretic threshold.
relation_to_S29_S33: Materially different. OLD MECHANISM: quantum distributions over diagonal register costs, read out via argmin/prefix/convex functionals (H-001, K-001..K-011). OLD FAILURE: classical reproducibility plus an information-limited endpoint (H-002, DNR-16). NEW MECHANISM: spectral planted inference on experimental data (the super-quadratic family M12). WHY OLD CONTROL NO LONGER APPLIES: M12 was rated WEAK because the ESM-only endpoint lacks the information. Here the input is experimental data in which the information is present in aggregate, so the relevant regime is a statistical-computational gap, not an information gap. No DNR entry covers it.
kill_result: Any one of: (a) on synthetic heterogeneous MRA / multi-frequency synchronization at realistic d, K, SNR and N, randomly initialised EM/AMP/moment methods match the truth-initialised (ORACLE) estimator everywhere recovery is information-theoretically possible, i.e. no gap in the practical band; (b) a gap appears only at N > 10^8 particles or SNR < 10^-3, beyond data-collection reality; (c) inside the gap the best classical algorithm is not Kikuchi-type, so [C71] does not transfer; (d) the level l needed gives n^{l/4} x QROM cost > 10^20 T gates.
minimal_classical_first_test: Heterogeneous 1D multi-reference alignment (cyclic shifts, numpy FFT) with signal length d = 16-64, K = 1-16 classes, noise sigma = 0.5-8, N = 10^4-10^6. Run four estimators: (i) EM from 20 random inits; (ii) EM from the true signals (ORACLE upper bound); (iii) bispectrum + Jennrich/power-method tensor decomposition; (iv) a spectral method. Map the (K/d, sigma, N) region where (ii) succeeds and (i), (iii) and (iv) all fail. Repeat for multi-frequency U(1) synchronization with AMP vs ORACLE initialisation. A few hours on 8 cores. No gap region at K <= d and realistic N -> kill for practical cryo-EM.
track: C theory/query first; B fault-tolerant if it survives
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low. A genuine super-quadratic mechanism attached to a real protein data source, but practical cryo-EM probably operates outside the conjectured-hard band (either EM has enough signal or the data are information-starved), and the Kikuchi mapping for SO(3) heterogeneity is unproven.
prior_art_known: [C71] Schmidhuber, O'Donnell, Kothari et al., PRX 15, 021077 (2025), arXiv 2406.19378 (repo-verified). [C72] Hastings, Quantum 4, 237 (2020), arXiv 1907.12724 (repo-verified). Perry, Wein, Bandeira, Moitra, CPAM (2018), arXiv 1610.04583 (verified by web search; multi-frequency synchronization, cryo-EM motivated). Z. Li, arXiv 2601.20522 (2026; verified abstract: statistical-to-computational gap in multi-frequency synchronization when the number of frequencies is large). Kunisky, Moore, Wein, FOCS 2024, arXiv 2404.18735 (verified; low-degree hardness for invariant distributions). Henderson, Q. Rev. Biophys. 28:171 (1995) (verified; dose limit). The search (repo 448-paper bibliography plus web, 2026-09) found no evidence of quantum planted-inference algorithms applied to cryo-EM or MRA.
measurement_readout: Phase estimation leaves the planted eigenvector as a quantum state. Only its order-1 marginals (the d-dimensional signal/orbit parameters) are needed: O(d/eps^2) measurements followed by classical rounding.
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: EM and amortised neural inference are the practical reproductions; SoS/Kikuchi is the classical twin. If practical instances are undercomplete (K <= d), Jennrich's algorithm solves them in polynomial time and the card dies.

title: Quantum simulation of many-body nuclear-spin dynamics as the forward model for protein NMR structure inference
protein_question: Can quantitative 1H-1H distances (3-8 A, including relayed multi-spin transfer) be extracted from fast-MAS solid-state NMR (RFDR, proton spin diffusion, multiple-quantum or OTOC-echo experiments) on fully protonated proteins, or from partially aligned samples? In these experiments the signal comes from coherent, strongly coupled dipolar many-body dynamics that classical forward models only approximate (rate-matrix spin diffusion, low-order clusters). The resulting restraints would be per-target structural information, exactly what the program's endpoint lacks.
representation: Proton coordinates of a candidate structure or ensemble define the secular dipolar Hamiltonian H(r) = sum_ij D_ij(r_ij, MAS phase)(3 I_zi I_zj - I_i.I_j) over a local patch of 30-100 protons (qubits), time-dependent under MAS. Observables: polarization transfer, MQ coherence or OTOC vs mixing time.
quantum_primitive: Hamiltonian simulation of a 2-local time-dependent Hamiltonian (Trotter/qDRIFT or qubitization) plus expectation-value estimation. Used either inside a classical Bayesian inversion or to generate training data for a classical surrogate.
classical_primitive_replaced: Rate-matrix spin-diffusion models, and exact simulation of small strongly coupled spin systems under MAS (SIMPSON/SpinEvolution class; typical practical limit ~10-14 spins, UNVERIFIED).
mechanism: Real-time dynamics of a dense, interacting spin-1/2 network is BQP-complete in general. Exact classical simulation costs 2^{N_s}. Controlled approximations (cluster-correlation expansion, Pauli-path truncation, MPO/TN) fail once operator growth and entanglement are large at the mixing times used; the same physics makes Google's OTOC(2) classically hard [F30]. A quantum computer applies e^{-iHt} in poly(N_s, t) gates. The resource is the Hilbert-space dimension of genuinely non-commuting dynamics. A classical computer can copy it only where the dynamics is effectively classical (incoherent spin diffusion), and that is exactly what the kill test measures. The sample itself is an analog quantum simulator; the QC is needed only to compute the forward map for candidate geometries, so that the data can be inverted quantitatively instead of used as qualitative contacts.
expected_speedup: Exponential in the number of strongly coupled spins that must be treated coherently, if classical approximations miss the observable by more than experimental noise. None if rate-matrix or cluster models are already within noise.
oracle_and_state_prep: No oracle problem: couplings are computed classically from coordinates (O(N_s^2)) and compiled as explicit 2-local rotations. The high-temperature NMR initial state is emulated with random product states / typicality (DQC1-like, cheap). Cost estimate (I(prog)): N_s = 30-60 qubits and ||H||t ~ 10-100 rad give 10^3-10^4 Trotter steps x ~N_s*z terms, i.e. 10^6-10^7 rotations (~10^8 T after synthesis) per circuit, x ~10^4 shots per observable. That is early-FT scale per forward evaluation. Inversion needs 10^3-10^5 forward calls, so the realistic architecture has the QC produce exact curves for a few hundred local geometries and a classical surrogate interpolate between them. This multiplies cost but does not erase the exponential if classical exact generation is impossible.
strongest_classical_competitor: Rate-matrix (incoherent) spin diffusion; cluster-correlation expansion; Pauli-path/operator truncation; MPO time evolution; exact <=24-spin clusters with embedding; ML surrogates. Experimental workaround: perdeuteration with sparse 1H back-labelling, or 13C/15N REDOR-type isolated-pair distances, which make the dynamics weakly coupled and classical. Out of scope: solution-NMR NOESY, whose full-relaxation-matrix forward model is classical.
information_vs_computation: Information: experimental NMR data, a new per-target information source. Computation: a quantum forward model that turns currently discarded multi-spin signal into quantitative restraints. No learned model is assumed free; candidate geometries come from the classical pipeline.
relation_to_S29_S33: Materially different. OLD MECHANISM: diagonal costs with argmin/prefix/convex readout (H-001). NEW MECHANISM: non-commuting real-time dynamics, for which no diagonal reduction exists, so H-001's premise fails. WHY OLD CONTROL NO LONGER APPLIES: the quantum output is an expectation value of a non-diagonal unitary evolution, not a distribution over a classical cost, and DNR-16's reopening condition (a new information source) is met. The literature phase (lit_F P2) rated the NMR route a 'WEAK curiosity' because no study shows protein NMR is limited by classical spin-dynamics cost; this card turns that into an explicit kill test.
kill_result: Any one of: (a) for realistic protein 1H patches, classical approximations (rate matrix, CCE-3, embedded exact 20-24-spin clusters) reproduce exact build-up/echo curves within 3-5% (experimental noise) at the mixing times used, and the error does not grow with patch size; (b) the Fisher information about a 0.2 A distance change carried by the part of the signal the approximations miss is below noise; (c) backbone accuracy saturates with qualitative (<5-7 A) contacts, so quantitative distances do not transmit (restraint-value curve, card 5); (d) sparse labelling gives equivalent restraints classically at lower total cost.
minimal_classical_first_test: Download one protein NMR ensemble entry with explicit hydrogens (e.g. ubiquitin), or add H to a structure. Take clusters of the N = 10...22 protons nearest a target amide H. Build the static secular dipolar Hamiltonian (a few powder orientations; zeroth-order MAS average Hamiltonian as a first cut) and evolve exactly with scipy expm_multiply (2^22 amplitudes, 64 MB). Compute polarization transfer vs mixing time and compare with (i) rate-matrix spin diffusion (rates proportional to D_ij^2) and (ii) 2- and 3-spin cluster expansions. Report RMS error vs N, and the Fisher information for a +/-0.2 A perturbation under exact vs approximate models. Approximation error <3% and flat in N -> kill. Hours on 8 cores.
track: E hybrid: quantum forward-model calls inside classical inversion. D-adjacent: the Google NMR-OTOC prototype [F34] ran on hardware.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low, but the highest in this lane. The mechanism is exponential, physically grounded and protein-sized. However, protein NMR deliberately avoids strongly coupled regimes (deuteration, solution NMR), incoherent spin-diffusion approximations may be adequate at long mixing times, and quantitative 1H distances may not transmit to backbone accuracy.
prior_art_known: [F34] Zhang et al., arXiv 2510.19550 (repo-verified): NMR OTOCs of small molecules in a liquid crystal, interpreted by simulation on Willow; self-declared 'not yet beyond classical'. [F30] Google Quantum AI, Nature 646, 825 (2025) (repo-verified): OTOC(2) classical hardness. The search (repo bibliography plus web, 2026-09) found no protein-scale study showing solid-state NMR structure determination is limited by classical spin-dynamics simulation, and no quantum forward model for protein NMR. Classical spin-diffusion modelling literature was not re-verified this session (UNVERIFIED).
measurement_readout: Expectation values (per-site magnetization, OTOC) to additive ~1e-2, i.e. ~10^4 shots per observable per geometry. Output is scalar curves, so there is no exponential readout problem.
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: MPO, Pauli-path and CCE are the direct twins. The strongest practical twin is an ML surrogate trained on exact <=24-spin simulations with embedding. The advantage requires patches where these demonstrably fail.

title: Quantum-memory learning from single-molecule spin sensors: Heisenberg-limited and entangled-measurement structure restraints
protein_question: Can the conformational state of ONE protein molecule be determined from nanoscale NV-diamond NMR with far fewer experimental repetitions than conventional repeat-and-measure? Examples: which fold a metamorphic protein adopts, or a few inter-nuclear distances in a heterogeneous or rare state. The proposed route stores sensor/nuclear-spin quantum states in a quantum memory and measures several copies jointly.
representation: The unknown local spin Hamiltonian (dipolar couplings of 1H/13C near the sensor), or the channel it induces on the sensor. Fold hypotheses A/B become two candidate Hamiltonians.
quantum_primitive: Quantum-enhanced learning from experiments with a quantum memory (Huang et al. 2022); Heisenberg-limited Hamiltonian learning (Huang, Tong, Fang, Su 2023); quantum-logic readout with an ancillary nuclear memory (Lovchinsky et al. 2016); collective multi-copy quantum hypothesis testing.
classical_primitive_replaced: Repeated single-copy sensor readout plus classical Bayesian estimation.
mechanism: Two separate resources. (i) Precision: coherent phase accumulation under the unknown coupling gives error ~1/T_total (Heisenberg) instead of ~1/sqrt(repetitions), capped by sensor/nuclear T2. (ii) Number of experiments: when the answer is a nonlinear functional of the state or channel (many non-commuting observables, purity/symmetry, channel eigenvalues), single-copy protocols need exponentially many experiments. Protocols that store copies in quantum memory and measure them jointly (e.g. Bell measurements on rho(x)rho) need polynomially many. Huang et al. 2022 prove this separation information-theoretically. Classical post-processing cannot recover it, because the information is destroyed at the measurement step, before any computer sees it.
expected_speedup: (i) Quadratic in precision per unit coherent time, capped by T2. (ii) Exponential in the number of experiments, but only for tasks needing many non-commuting observables. Distance restraints are commuting zz-type couplings, so plain distance estimation is not expected to be in that regime.
oracle_and_state_prep: No computational oracle. Physical requirements: coherent transfer of the sensor state into a memory (NV electron -> 13C/15N nuclear memory, already demonstrated for readout), memory coherence >> experiment time, and at least two copies stored jointly. On a single molecule the 'copies' are sequential repetitions, so the molecule must stay in the same state (static heterogeneity); dynamics decorrelates them.
strongest_classical_competitor: Conventional NV-NMR with repeated single-shot readout and Bayesian estimation; ensemble NMR (10^17 copies, so copies are not scarce there); single-molecule FRET (3-8 nm distances); DEER/EPR; cryo-EM heterogeneity analysis; AlphaFold-class prediction with MSA subsampling for alternative folds.
information_vs_computation: Pure information acquisition: the quantum resource cuts the number of experiments needed to acquire per-target structural information. No computational speedup is claimed. This is consistent with H-002: only new information moves an information-limited endpoint.
relation_to_S29_S33: Materially different: no register, no diagonal cost, no optimisation. It meets DNR-16/K-012's reopening condition (a new information source). None of QX-01..31 applies.
kill_result: Any one of: (a) the structural question reduces to a few commuting couplings measurable with standard sequences at standard scaling, so the Huang-type separation does not apply and only the T2-capped Heisenberg gain remains; (b) the number of experiments is not binding (molecule lifetime and photobleaching are not limiting, or ensembles suffice); (c) the restraint-value curve shows backbone accuracy saturates at NOE-level precision (~1 A), so Heisenberg precision is worthless.
minimal_classical_first_test: (1) Restraint-value curve on mid30/long40: add K in {5,10,20,50} synthetic distance restraints drawn from natives (ORACLE-labelled scientific analysis), with noise sigma in {0.1,0.3,1,2} A, to the A80 energy as flat-bottom terms; decode with 32 restarts; measure RMSD vs (K, sigma). If gains saturate at sigma ~ 1 A, precision-based quantum sensing is irrelevant. (2) Paper calculation (numpy): for fold-A vs fold-B discrimination on one NV-proximal proton patch with realistic T2 and decoherence, compare single-copy vs two-copy collective error exponents (quantum Chernoff bound). Ratio <2x -> kill the memory variant. Under 1 day.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low. The quantum resource is real and physically grounded, but protein structural questions map to commuting coupling estimates where the exponential-in-experiments separation does not apply, and ensemble methods have abundant copies.
prior_art_known: Huang, Broughton, Cotler et al., 'Quantum advantage in learning from experiments', Science 376, 1182 (2022), DOI 10.1126/science.abn7293 (verified). Huang, Tong, Fang, Su, PRL 130, 200403 (2023), arXiv 2210.03030 (verified). Lovchinsky et al., Science 351, 836 (2016), DOI 10.1126/science.aad8022 (verified; single-ubiquitin NMR with quantum logic). The search (web, 2026-09) found no quantum-memory learning protocol applied to protein structure.
measurement_readout: Joint (Bell-basis) measurements on memory-stored copies, followed by a Bayesian update over fold hypotheses.
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: No computational twin applies. The classical-measurement twin is the optimal single-copy adaptive strategy, which already reaches the Helstrom bound for pure-state binary discrimination (known result; not re-verified this session).

title: Interaction-free and multi-pass quantum electron microscopy to lift the radiation-dose limit for small proteins
protein_question: Can single-particle structures, and conformational heterogeneity, be determined for proteins below the practical cryo-EM mass limit (~40-50 kDa; Henderson's theoretical estimate ~38 kDa) if each electron gathers more phase information per unit radiation damage?
representation: Weak-phase projection images (Coulomb potential) of single particles.
quantum_primitive: Quantum-limited metrology of weak-phase objects: multi-pass phase accumulation (one probe interrogates the specimen N times coherently) and interaction-free (quantum Zeno) measurement.
classical_primitive_replaced: Single-pass phase-contrast TEM imaging.
mechanism: Radiation damage per unit information is the binding limit for unstained biomolecules (Henderson 1995). For a weak phase object with per-pass phase phi, N coherent passes accumulate N*phi while damage per electron grows ~N. At fixed total damage D there are ~D/N electrons, so SNR ~ N*phi*sqrt(D/N) = sqrt(N)*phi*sqrt(D): Fisher information per unit damage grows ~N until per-pass loss and decoherence cap N_eff. Interaction-free schemes aim to detect absorption or phase with interaction probability -> 0 via the Zeno effect. The gain lives in the measurement physics (coherent re-interrogation), so no classical computation can reproduce it. Honest labelling: multi-pass uses single-particle coherence, not entanglement, so this is quantum-limited metrology, not quantum computation.
expected_speedup: Information per unit dose ~N_eff (passes before loss). Plausible N_eff for electron optics is unknown (UNVERIFIED); optical multi-pass microscopy has shown ~26 dB variance reduction.
oracle_and_state_prep: No oracle. Hardware needs electron mirrors/cavities that re-image with low loss and aberration, and coherent electron sources. A per-pass loss l caps N_eff at ~1/l.
strongest_classical_competitor: Phase plates (Volta, laser); detector DQE improvements; scaffolds/fiducials that increase particle mass; microED; cryo-ET subtomogram averaging; computational denoising. For monomer structure, AlphaFold-class prediction plus NMR/X-ray.
information_vs_computation: Pure information acquisition (dose efficiency). Quantum computation plays no role.
relation_to_S29_S33: Materially different: not a computational architecture. Meets DNR-16's reopening condition (a new information source).
kill_result: Any one of: (a) a loss model gives N_eff < ~3, below what phase plates and detectors already provide; (b) an alignment-SNR model shows that even G = 10x information per dose does not lift 20-30 kDa particles above the alignment threshold; (c) the targets that would benefit (small monomers) are already solved by prediction or NMR, so the structural value is marginal.
minimal_classical_first_test: Henderson-style alignment-SNR simulation. Project Gaussian-atom Coulomb-potential models of 15, 30 and 60 kDa proteins (from PDB coordinates) at doses of 10-60 e/A^2, with an information-per-dose multiplier G in {1,2,5,10,30} and a per-pass loss model. Assign orientations by cross-correlation against templates on an SO(3) grid and record alignment success vs (mass, G). Report the G needed for 20-30 kDa and compare it with N_eff at loss l in {1%,5%,10%}. numpy FFT; hours.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low. It is a real physical lever on the actual (information) bottleneck, but the hardware is immature, gains are loss-capped and only linear in passes, the benefiting targets have strong classical alternatives, and it is metrology, not computational advantage.
prior_art_known: Henderson, Q. Rev. Biophys. 28:171-193 (1995) (verified). Putnam & Yanik, PRA 80, 040902(R) (2009) (verified). Kruit et al., Ultramicroscopy 164:31-45 (2016) (verified). Juffmann et al., 'Multi-pass microscopy', Nat. Commun. 7, 12858 (2016) (verified; 25.9 dB variance reduction in light microscopy). Juffmann et al., 'Multi-pass transmission electron microscopy', Sci. Rep. (2017), arXiv 1612.04931 (listing verified; volume/page UNVERIFIED).
measurement_readout: Detector images; the downstream classical alignment and reconstruction are unchanged.
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: Not applicable (physical measurement). Computational denoising and cryoDRGN-type inference extract information but cannot add any.

title: Quantum-accelerated Bayesian experimental design: choosing which structural restraints to measure
protein_question: Given an information-limited posterior over a target's structure (the regime S29-S33 measured), which small set of experiments maximally reduces structural uncertainty or expected RMSD risk? Candidates: k DEER spin-label pairs, crosslinks or NMR labels among ~L^2/2 options.
representation: A posterior ensemble over CA traces, plus Gaussian measurement models for each candidate restraint.
quantum_primitive: Nested amplitude estimation / quantum multilevel Monte Carlo for the expected information gain (EIG); quantum minimum finding over candidate designs; walk-based qsampling of the posterior.
classical_primitive_replaced: Nested Monte Carlo EIG with exhaustive or greedy design ranking.
mechanism: EIG(d) = E_theta E_{y|theta,d} [log p(y|theta,d) - log E_theta' p(y|theta',d)] is a nested expectation. Classical nested MC costs ~eps^-3 (~eps^-2 with MLMC). Quantum nested estimation can reach ~eps^-1 in the query model, and Durr-Hoyer maximisation over D designs costs sqrt(D). Both gains are quadratic interference effects a classical computer cannot copy; everything else (ensemble reuse, greedy selection) it can.
expected_speedup: At most quadratic in 1/eps and in D. Zero if the design ranking is stable at modest sample counts.
oracle_and_state_prep: Needs a coherent posterior qsample (the M1 walk operator at >=60 aa: 10^6-10^8 Toffolis per step, I(agent)), coherent likelihoods (cheap distance-to-Gaussian arithmetic) and a coherent log. Posterior preparation dominates and erases the gain unless M1 is justified on its own.
strongest_classical_competitor: Ensemble-based EIG with one posterior ensemble reused across all designs (O(M*D), cheap); greedy submodular selection; Laplace/Gaussian approximations; variational EIG bounds.
information_vs_computation: Information: the prior comes from the learned energy, and future experiments supply new information. Computation: the design decision. The quantum part speeds only that decision.
relation_to_S29_S33: The formulation is new (the objective is an experiment choice), but the quantum parts reduce to M4 (amplitude estimation; KILLED in practice because estimates are bias/mixing-limited and break-even needs sigma/eps >~ 10^4), M1 (qsampling) and M9 (Grover; KILLED). OLD FAILURE: decisions were not variance-limited (H-005 retired). WHY THE OLD CONTROL MIGHT NOT APPLY: design rankings could be more precision-sensitive than structure decisions, and the test checks exactly that.
kill_result: Top-10 design ranking stable (bootstrap Kendall tau > 0.9) at M <= 10^3-10^4 posterior samples, or full greedy design at L = 150 costs under 1 CPU-hour.
minimal_classical_first_test: On mid30/long40, draw a posterior ensemble (256 decoder restarts plus short MCMC under A80). Compute ensemble EIG for every single-pair distance measurement (noise 1-3 A) and measure ranking stability vs M (32...4096) by bootstrap. As ORACLE-labelled scientific analysis, check whether top-EIG pairs simulated from the native reduce RMSD more than random pairs. This doubles as the shared restraint-value curve for cards 2-4. Under 1 day.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low, and very low for the quantum part; the classical test is worth running for its own sake.
prior_art_known: No quantum EIG / experimental-design paper for protein structure is in the repo bibliography. No dedicated web search was run (gap UNVERIFIED). Quantum MLMC literature was not re-verified this session (UNVERIFIED).
measurement_readout: Scalar EIG estimates via amplitude estimation; the argmax design via quantum minimum finding.
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: Ensemble reuse with importance weights; Gaussian/Laplace EIG; learned amortised EIG estimators.

title: Competing-fold hypothesis testing: quantum distribution testing and swap-test fidelity between structure posteriors
protein_question: For a fold-switching sequence (e.g. RfaH C-terminal domain, KaiB, lymphotactin): does the learned-energy posterior put mass >= eps on the alternative fold B? What is the Bayes factor / Delta F between folds A and B? Are the posteriors of the wild type and a mutant distinguishable (Hellinger/TV distance)?
representation: Posterior over CA traces/torsions under the esmprior/A80 energy. Fold indicator: fraction of fold-specific contacts relative to classically generated hypothesis structures.
quantum_primitive: Amplitude amplification/estimation of a basin projector on a posterior qsample |sqrt(pi)>; swap test (or AE) for the Bhattacharyya fidelity <sqrt(pi_A)|sqrt(pi_B)>; quantum l1-closeness testing (Bravyi-Harrow-Hassidim).
classical_primitive_replaced: Brute-force posterior sampling to count rare-fold mass.
mechanism: With coherent qsample access, the mass p_B of a region can be estimated with ~1/sqrt(p_B) preparations vs ~1/p_B classical samples, and the posterior fidelity with ~1/eps vs ~1/eps^2. These are amplitude-level interference effects that a classical sampler cannot copy. BHH's O(sqrt N) vs Omega(N^{1-o(1)}) support-size gain applies to unstructured distributions; for Gibbs posteriors the relevant parameters become p_B, eps and the mixing gap.
expected_speedup: Quadratic in 1/p_B or 1/eps, conditional on cheap qsamples. None against stratified classical estimators when both fold hypotheses are known.
oracle_and_state_prep: Needs |sqrt(pi)> at >=60 aa (M1 cost) and a native-free coherent fold-B indicator: a reversible contact/topology signature relative to a hypothesis structure generated classically (e.g. by AF2 MSA subsampling). Using that structure is allowed because it is a hypothesis, not a native. Qsample preparation dominates and erases the gain unless M1 is justified.
strongest_classical_competitor: Umbrella sampling or metadynamics along a fold-A-vs-B collective variable with MBAR; bridge sampling / BAR for Bayes factors; parallel tempering; sampling seeded in both basins (both hypotheses are known); AF2 MSA subsampling/clustering to generate alternative folds.
information_vs_computation: Whether the learned energy encodes fold B at all is an information question; AF2-class models have documented blind spots for alternative folds [E105]. Computation only estimates the mass given the energy.
relation_to_S29_S33: A sub-case of M4/M5/M6 (KILLED/WEAK) applied to a new question. OLD FAILURE: estimation is bias/mixing-limited, not variance-limited. WHY THE OLD CONTROL STILL LARGELY APPLIES: when fold B is a known hypothesis, stratified classical estimators remove the 1/p_B factor. Amplification helps only for undiscovered hidden modes, which reduces to M1/M2 hide-and-seek (H-007).
kill_result: Either: (a) classical umbrella/MBAR gives Delta F_AB under the learned energy to +/-0.5 kT with <= 10^8 energy evaluations at L = 60-100; or (b) the learned energy puts fold B more than 10 kT above fold A for every tested fold-switcher (an information failure, making computation irrelevant).
minimal_classical_first_test: Take 3-5 fold-switchers of <= ~100 aa, leakage-checked against esmprior_v1 training crops. Relax both experimental folds under A80/esmprior (ORACLE-labelled analysis). Run 16-32-window umbrella sampling along Q_A - Q_B with MBAR; record Delta F and cost. Under 1 day on 8 cores.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low. Quadratic, gated on M1, and stratified classical estimators remove the rare-mass factor whenever the competing fold is a known hypothesis.
prior_art_known: Bravyi, Harrow, Hassidim, IEEE TIT 57, 3971 (2011) (verified). Gilyen & Li, 'Distributional property testing in a quantum world', ITCS 2020 (listing seen; details UNVERIFIED). [E105] Chakravarty, Lee, Porter, arXiv 2410.14898 (repo-verified). MSA-subsampling (AF-Cluster-type) fold-switching work: citation UNVERIFIED. No quantum fold-switching study is in the repo bibliography.
measurement_readout: Amplitude estimation of the basin projector; swap-test ancilla statistics.
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: Umbrella sampling with MBAR; flow-based importance samplers with exact reweighting.

title: Protein knot invariants by quantum Jones-polynomial approximation (AJL / one-clean-qubit)
protein_question: What is the knot type of a protein chain (trefoil 3_1 up to the 7_1 knot, plus composite knots)? And the scientifically live question: what is the knotting probability of folding/unfolded ensembles, and how do knotted proteins fold?
representation: Closed chain -> projection -> braid word (strands, crossings).
quantum_primitive: Additive approximation of the Jones polynomial at roots of unity: plat closure (BQP-complete; Aharonov-Jones-Landau) and trace/Markov closure (DQC1-complete; Shor-Jordan). Implemented end-to-end on trapped ions (Quantinuum).
classical_primitive_replaced: Exact Kauffman-bracket, Alexander or HOMFLY evaluation on reduced diagrams.
