mechanism: The Jones polynomial is a weighted trace of a unitary braid-group representation (the Temperley-Lieb path model) whose dimension grows exponentially with the number of strands. A quantum computer applies the representation directly and estimates the trace with a Hadamard test. Classical exact evaluation is #P-hard in general and exponential in diagram treewidth. This is a genuine non-commuting (non-diagonal) mechanism, unlike H-001's class. BUT the approximation is additive on a normalised scale (error ~ representation dimension/poly), which is exponentially coarse relative to |V(t)| for most knots, and it beats classical methods only for large, high-treewidth braids.
expected_speedup: None at protein scale. After standard reduction, protein knots have at most 7 minimal crossings, and classical exact invariants take milliseconds.
oracle_and_state_prep: Input chain -> closure (direct or probabilistic) -> projection -> braid word, all polynomial classical preprocessing. Circuits are poly(strands, crossings). No oracle issue. Readout is an additive estimate of a normalised trace, needing ~1/eps^2 shots.
strongest_classical_competitor: KMT/Taylor reduction plus the Alexander polynomial (a determinant, polynomial time) and HOMFLY-PT on reduced diagrams (KnotProt/Topoly/pyknotid-class tools); Kauffman-bracket state sums (2^c states with c <= ~20 after reduction); tensor-network contraction (Quantinuum's classical benchmarks find DQC1 instances no easier classically than BQP ones).
information_vs_computation: Information: the coordinates (classical). Computation: invariant evaluation, trivial at protein size. The protein-relevant questions (knotting probability, folding pathways) are sampling problems in which the invariant is a cheap per-sample indicator, so they reduce to M1.
relation_to_S29_S33: Materially different mechanism (a unitary braid representation, not a diagonal cost), so H-001 does not cover it. It fails for a different reason: instance size.
kill_result: Reduced crossing numbers <= ~20 and exact invariant time <= 1 s for every chain in PDB/AFDB and for compact random ensembles up to L = 1000. That is far below the minimum link size where Quantinuum's resource estimate places quantum advantage.
minimal_classical_first_test: Implement KMT reduction (numpy) and the Alexander polynomial (sympy determinant). Run on (i) ~50 knotted entries downloaded from public databases, including AF prediction Q9PR55 (7_1), and (ii) compact random CA-trace ensembles (confined random walks and A80-decoder outputs) at L = 100-1000. Record reduced crossing number and wall-clock vs L. Hours.
track: A NISQ (DQC1 on trapped ions) / C theory
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low (very low). Protein knots are 1-2 orders of magnitude below the size where classical evaluation gets hard, and the open knot questions in protein science are sampling questions.
prior_art_known: Aharonov, Jones, Landau, Algorithmica 55, 395 (2009), arXiv quant-ph/0511096 (verified). Shor & Jordan, QIC 8, 681 (2008), arXiv 0707.2831 (verified). Quantinuum, 'End-to-end quantum algorithms for the Jones polynomial', PRX Quantum (2026), arXiv 2503.05625 (verified: DQC1-complete for Markov closure, BQP-complete for plat closure, classical cost of the DQC1 version at least as high; a ~100-crossing hardware demo per the company blog, detail UNVERIFIED). Brems et al., Protein Sci. 31, e4380 (2022), arXiv 2207.07410 (verified: 7_1 knot in AF prediction Q9PR55). The search (web, 2026-09) found no quantum knot algorithms applied to proteins.
measurement_readout: Hadamard-test ancilla, ~1/eps^2 shots.
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: Tensor-network contraction of the braid representation (Quantinuum's classical benchmark); exact state sums at protein size.

title: Quantum topological data analysis of conformational ensembles: Betti numbers and hole persistence
protein_question: What is the topology of a protein's conformational landscape or ensemble? That means: separated basins (beta_0 across scales), cyclic transition pathways (beta_1), and cavities/tunnels (beta_1/beta_2 of atomic point clouds). Does a specific hole persist across length scales, e.g. a putative cyclic folding route or a ligand tunnel seen in some conformers?
representation: Vietoris-Rips/clique complex of conformers (RMSD graph) or of atomic point clouds.
quantum_primitive: LGZ phase estimation on the combinatorial Laplacian of a clique complex for normalised Betti numbers; guided persistence testing via a sparse Hamiltonian with a harmonic-representative guiding state (Gyurik et al. 2026, BQP1-hard).
classical_primitive_replaced: Boundary-matrix reduction (Ripser/GUDHI).
mechanism: beta_k = dim ker Delta_k. For clique complexes the number of k-simplices can grow like n^k, so the Laplacian is exponentially large in k. The quantum algorithm samples k-cliques (Grover), phase-estimates Delta_k and reads out the zero-eigenvalue fraction: beta_k/|S_k| to additive eps in poly(n, 1/eps, 1/sqrt(gap)). The persistence-testing variant is BQP1-hard, a superpolynomial separation under complexity assumptions for general inputs. Limits: a normalised additive estimate is useless unless beta_k is a sizeable fraction of |S_k| (clique-dense, high-Betti complexes). Schmidhuber-Lloyd show LGZ is only quadratic in almost all cases, and the Apers et al. classical path-integral Monte Carlo matches it at constant gap and precision.
expected_speedup: Exponential only for clique-dense, high-Betti, high-k complexes; otherwise quadratic or none. Protein data sit in the 'none' regime.
oracle_and_state_prep: The input graph (conformers as vertices, edges where RMSD < r) is built classically in O(n^2). A coherent clique-membership oracle is cheap. The persistence algorithm's guiding state needs a harmonic representative computed classically at one scale. Producing the ensemble itself costs M1-type sampling.
strongest_classical_competitor: Ripser/GUDHI persistent homology (seconds to minutes for 10^4-10^5 points, k <= 2); the Apers-Gribling-Sen-Szabo classical Betti estimator; MSM/PCCA+ and TICA/VAMP for metastable basins (beta_0 of kinetic basins); alpha-shape/cavity finders for tunnels.
information_vs_computation: Information: the ensemble, from classical sampling of the learned energy. Computation: topology, which the quantum part accelerates only in regimes protein data do not reach.
relation_to_S29_S33: Materially different: a non-diagonal Laplacian, not covered by H-001. It fails on regime mismatch, not on the S29-S33 mechanisms.
kill_result: For protein ensembles and structures, the relevant homology is k <= 2 with small Betti numbers (<= 10^2); normalised beta_k/|S_k| < 10^-3 wherever |S_k| is classically intractable; exact persistence runs in minutes classically.

Compute exact beta_0..beta_3 (boundary-matrix ranks via scipy, or pip-installed ripser), |S_k| for k <= 6, normalised Betti numbers and the Laplacian gap; record wall-clock. Hours.

title: Normalised-trace and characteristic-function estimators (DQC1, probe-qubit Lee-Yang/Fisher zeros) for metastable-state census and folding-transition order
protein_question: Is the folding transition of a learned-energy chain first-order-like (two-state; Fisher zeros pinching the real temperature axis under finite-size scaling)? That decides whether tempering is torpid at 100-300 aa (gap G-11). How many metastable states does the landscape have?
representation: Diagonal learned energy over discretised conformations; the Metropolis transition operator.
quantum_primitive: One-clean-qubit (DQC1) normalised trace Tr(U)/2^n; a Hadamard-test probe qubit coupled to a Gibbs-state register via exp(-i tau sigma_z (x) E) (the Wei-Liu / Peng et al. Lee-Yang-zero protocol); quantum fast-forwarding for Tr(P^t).
classical_primitive_replaced: Wang-Landau density of states; MSM spectral analysis.
mechanism: The claim: DQC1 estimates exponential-dimension traces in polynomial time; the probe's coherence equals Z(beta + i tau)/Z(beta), whose zeros locate the transition and its order; the normalised trace of P^t counts slow eigenvalues (metastable states). Three lemmas (I(prog)) show why this fails. (i) For a diagonal energy, Tr f(E)/2^n = E_{x~uniform} f(E(x)) and <exp(-i tau E)>_beta = E_{x~pi_beta} exp(-i tau E(x)). Classical Monte Carlo has the same additive error (quantum AE improves it only quadratically), and classical pi_beta samples cost no more than the quantum register's Gibbs preparation. (ii) For a two-state transition, the leading Fisher zero sits at tau ~ pi/Delta E (Delta E ~ L), where the characteristic function is O(1), so a probe qubit and classical sampling both resolve it with ~1/eps^2 samples. Higher zeros sit where the envelope exp(-tau^2 Var(E)/2) is tiny, and there both need exponentially many shots. Wang-Landau/multicanonical densities of states give ln g(E) at uniform relative accuracy and yield all the zeros directly. The genuinely hard step is sampling pi_beta at a first-order transition (torpid mixing), which is the M1/M2 problem, not the readout. (iii) Tr(P^t)/N is the uniform-start return probability, which a classical chain estimates without bias. For intermediate t it is about (#metastable states)/N, which is exponentially small and below any additive resolution.
expected_speedup: None beyond quadratic (via amplitude estimation or fast-forwarding).
oracle_and_state_prep: The probe protocol needs Gibbs-state preparation (M1 cost); the trace needs a coherent walk operator. A physical probe qubit cannot couple to a protein's learned energy, so the Peng et al. experiment has no protein analogue; only the computational version exists.
strongest_classical_competitor: Wang-Landau / multicanonical DOS for Fisher zeros; energy-histogram bimodality with finite-size scaling; MSM/PCCA+ for metastable counting; transfer-matrix DP for low-cutwidth chain models.
information_vs_computation: Pure computation on a classical energy; no new information.
relation_to_S29_S33: An extension of H-001/H-009. OLD MECHANISM: quantum distributions over diagonal costs consumed by argmin/prefix/convex functionals. NEW MECHANISM: complex-valued linear functionals (normalised traces, characteristic functions). WHY THE OLD CONTROL STILL APPLIES: any linear functional of a diagonal-energy distribution is an expectation, and classical Monte Carlo reproduces it. Proposed as a T1 lemma (the 'DQC1-diagonal lemma').
kill_result: Theorem-level kill (lemmas i-iii), plus a measurement: Wang-Landau resolves the Fisher zeros at L = 30-60 on the learned energy, and the classical estimate of <exp(-i tau E)> reaches its noise floor at the same tau a probe qubit would.
minimal_classical_first_test: (1) Torsion-discretised A80 chain at L = 10-12 (4 states per residue, ~10^6 states): exact DOS by enumeration, and the exact spectrum of the single-residue Metropolis matrix by sparse Lanczos. Count eigenvalues near 1; compute Tr(P^t)/N exactly and with the classical return-probability estimator. (2) Wang-Landau at mid30 length: Fisher zeros from the DOS, compared with PT-sample estimates of the characteristic function. Hours.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low (killed by argument). Kept as a written lemma so the family is not reopened.
prior_art_known: Shor & Jordan 2008 (verified). Knill & Laflamme, PRL 81, 5672 (1998) (canonical DQC1; not re-verified this session). Wei & Liu, PRL 109, 185701 (2012) (verified). Peng et al., PRL 114, 010601 (2015) (verified). Apers & Sarlette [A35], QIC 19 (2019), arXiv 1804.02321 (repo-verified). Fisher-zero studies of lattice proteins: UNVERIFIED.
measurement_readout: Clean-qubit or probe-qubit coherence estimates.
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: Transfer-matrix DP for low-cutwidth models; Monte Carlo with identical additive error.

title: Multistate negative design as a zero-sum game solved by quantum Gibbs-sampling game/LP solvers
protein_question: Which sequence stabilises a target fold while destabilising a set of competing decoy folds (misfolds, alternative states, wrong oligomers), i.e. maximises the worst-case or soft-min energy gap? This is the negative-design problem behind fold specificity and conformational switches.
representation: A payoff matrix over (sequence, decoy fold) pairs with pairwise contact energies.
quantum_primitive: Quantum zero-sum-game / LP solvers that use quantum Gibbs sampling inside multiplicative weights (van Apeldoorn & Gilyen 2019).
classical_primitive_replaced: Classical multiplicative weights / LP.
mechanism: Payoff A[s,f] = E(s,f) - E(s,target) for sequence s and decoy f. An eps-Nash equilibrium via multiplicative weights needs Gibbs samples over pure strategies. Amplitude amplification prepares them with ~sqrt(n+m) work instead of ~(n+m): O~(sqrt(n+m)/eps^3) quantum vs classical Grigoriadis-Khachiyan O~((n+m)/eps^2). The gain is quadratic in the number of pure strategies, worse in eps, and holds only for unstructured payoffs. With 20^L sequences the payoff is pairwise-decomposable, so the designer's best response is a Potts ground-state/sampling problem that classical CFN or MCMC solves by exploiting that structure; the quantum version then reduces to walk-based Potts sampling (quadratic in the gap).
expected_speedup: Quadratic in strategy count for unstructured payoff tables; none against structure-exploiting classical design.
oracle_and_state_prep: The coherent payoff oracle is reversible energy evaluation for (sequence, decoy fold) pairs (pairwise contact potential, O(L^2) arithmetic). The decoy set is generated classically. No oracle is assumed free, and the gain disappears once structure is exploited.
strongest_classical_competitor: Cost-function-network / DEE multistate design; Rosetta-style multistate design; inverse-folding networks conditioned on multiple states; LP with column generation over a small decoy set; MCMC over Potts sequence models.
information_vs_computation: Information: the design energy and the decoy set (classical models). Computation: game solving, which is structured and classically efficient.
relation_to_S29_S33: OLD MECHANISM: quantum optimisation of a diagonal cost (K-002, DNR-02). NEW MECHANISM: a min-max game rather than a single argmin. WHY THE OLD CONTROL STILL APPLIES: each best-response step is an argmin/Gibbs step over a diagonal pairwise cost (DNR-02, plus M9's Grover kill); the game layer adds only a quadratic factor in an unstructured dimension.
kill_result: Classical multiplicative weights with a Potts best response (or LP with column generation) reaches eps = 0.01 kT on a 30-60 aa target with 10^2-10^3 decoys in at most 1 CPU-hour.
minimal_classical_first_test: One mid30/long40 target. Decoys: A80 decoder minima of other targets threaded onto its length, plus shuffled-contact controls. Energy: a pairwise contact potential on contact maps. Solve the game by multiplicative weights with a Potts Gibbs-sampling best response and by LP column generation; record time-to-eps and decoy count. Hours.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low (very low). The gain is quadratic in an unstructured dimension that real design never searches unstructured.
prior_art_known: van Apeldoorn & Gilyen, arXiv 1904.03180 (2019) (verified: O~(sqrt(n+m)/eps^3)). Grigoriadis & Khachiyan (1995), sublinear classical game solver (UNVERIFIED this session). No quantum negative-design study in the repo bibliography; no dedicated web search was run (gap UNVERIFIED).
measurement_readout: Strategies sampled from quantum Gibbs states.
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: Potts-model message passing / CFN for best responses.

title: Committors and folding rates via quantum linear-system solvers for the backward Kolmogorov equation
protein_question: What are the committor function (the transition-state ensemble at q = 1/2) and the rate constant k_AB between two metastable states of a protein under a given energy?
representation: Grid discretisation of torsion or Cartesian space; the generator of overdamped Langevin dynamics under the learned energy.
quantum_primitive: Quantum linear-system / QSVT solvers for the discretised elliptic PDE L q = 0 (q = 0 on A, q = 1 on B), with amplitude estimation of a flux functional.
classical_primitive_replaced: Grid PDE solvers and trajectory Monte Carlo.
mechanism: On a grid with m points per coordinate in d = 3L (or torsional) dimensions there are N = m^d unknowns. QLSA costs poly(d, log N, kappa, 1/eps), an exponential saving over deterministic grid solvers. But three things erode it. kappa grows like h^-2 and picks up an e^{beta Delta} factor whenever intermediate metastable states lie outside A and B. Relative-precision readout of an exponentially small rate by AE still costs ~k_AB^{-1/2}. And the committor has a Feynman-Kac trajectory representation, q(x) = P[hit B before A | x], so classical trajectory Monte Carlo is dimension-free, and splitting methods remove most of the rare-event factor. Linden-Montanaro-Shao prove, for the heat equation, that the QLSA route is never faster than the best classical algorithm and that the best quantum route (AE on an accelerated random walk) is at most quadratically faster. Stochastic-unraveling principle (I(prog)): for any quantity with a positive stochastic representation, QLSA stays at most quadratically ahead of Monte Carlo.
expected_speedup: At most quadratic vs Monte Carlo; exponential only vs grid solvers, which nobody uses in high dimension.
oracle_and_state_prep: Block-encoding the generator needs a coherent gradient oracle grad E for the learned energy on a fine grid (gap G-6: uncosted, likely expensive). Boundary sets A/B are defined classically. Reading out k_AB needs amplitude estimation.
strongest_classical_competitor: Forward-flux sampling, weighted ensemble, adaptive multilevel splitting, TPS, milestoning, MSM committors, neural-network variational committor solvers, the string method.
information_vs_computation: Pure computation on a classical energy. Rates are kinetics, outside the structure endpoint (M3, WEAK).
relation_to_S29_S33: Not tested in S29-S33; adjacent to M3 (walk hitting times, WEAK) and M2 (quadratic in e^{beta Delta}). NEW MECHANISM: PDE solving instead of walks. WHY IT STILL DIES: the stochastic unraveling gives classical dimension-free estimators, and Linden-Montanaro-Shao make the bound explicit for the diffusion prototype.
kill_result: On the learned energy between two decoder-found basins at mid30 length, AMS/WE estimate k_AB to 10% relative error at a cost polynomial in L and polylogarithmic in 1/k_AB. The quantum route is then at most quadratic in a factor splitting already removed.
minimal_classical_first_test: (1) 2D/4D toy (Muller-Brown-type, or esmprior projected onto two collective variables): exact grid committor vs AMS/FFS, cost vs beta. (2) mid30 target under overdamped Langevin on the A80 energy: WE/AMS between two basins; record force evaluations to reach 10% error. Under 1 day.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low (very low). There is a provable barrier in the diffusion prototype, and splitting methods already defeat the rare-event factor.
prior_art_known: Montanaro & Pallister, PRA 93, 032324 (2016) (verified: polynomial speedup growing with dimension; no superpolynomial speedup in fixed dimension). Linden, Montanaro, Shao, Commun. Math. Phys. 395, 601 (2022), arXiv 2004.06516 (verified: QLSA never faster than the best classical method for the heat equation; AE on random walks at most quadratic for d >= 2). Devereux & Datta, PRA (2025/26), arXiv 2505.21221 (verified: QFT diagonalisation advantageous for linear drift-diffusion at fixed final time; applicability to rugged potentials UNVERIFIED).
measurement_readout: Amplitude estimation of the flux functional.
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: Neural variational committors; tensor-train PDE solvers at moderate dimension.

title: Exponential simulation of coupled classical oscillators (Babbush et al.) for vibrational energy flow in macroscopic protein assemblies
protein_question: How does vibrational energy, heat or a mechanical perturbation propagate through very large non-periodic protein assemblies (protein crystals with defects, amyloid fibril networks, viral capsids, cytoskeletal meshes)? For example: the kinetic energy reaching a distant site at time t in an elastic network model.
representation: Elastic network (masses and springs) over 2^n nodes.
quantum_primitive: The Babbush-Berry-Kothari-Somma-Wiebe mapping of Newton's equations for 2^n harmonic oscillators onto Schrodinger evolution; Hamiltonian simulation plus amplitude estimation of subsystem kinetic energy.
classical_primitive_replaced: Sparse Verlet/Krylov propagation.
mechanism: Amplitudes encode sqrt(m)*xdot and sqrt(K)*x. With efficiently queryable masses and springs the cost is poly(n) for 2^n oscillators, while estimating a subsystem's kinetic energy needs 2^Omega(n) classical queries (a glued-trees embedding, proved in the oracle model). Conservative wave dynamics has no positive stochastic unraveling, so unlike card 11 the exponential survives in principle. It fails on instance class. Every protein object either has <= ~10^8 explicit degrees of freedom (solved classically with sparse O(N)-per-step methods), or is periodic (Bloch reduction), or is macroscopic and homogenisable (continuum elasticity). The exponential regime needs 2^n oscillators with an algorithmically generated, non-periodic, non-homogenisable structure.
expected_speedup: Exponential in oscillator count in principle; zero at protein scale.
oracle_and_state_prep: Needs an efficient circuit giving spring constants from a node index. A real assembly's elastic network is an explicit coordinate list, so QROM loading costs O(N) per query and erases the exponential unless the structure is procedurally generated (lattice plus defect rule). The initial displacement state must also be efficiently preparable.
strongest_classical_competitor: Sparse Verlet/Krylov propagation and ARPACK normal modes (O(N) per step, GPU, N <= 10^8); Bloch theory for crystals; homogenisation/continuum elasticity; kernel polynomial methods; disorder averaging.
information_vs_computation: Pure computation on a classical elastic model, itself a crude approximation. No structural information is gained.
relation_to_S29_S33: Materially different (linear wave dynamics, not a diagonal cost) and outside the structure endpoint. It fails on scale and instance class, not on the S29-S33 mechanisms.
kill_result: The largest biologically meaningful non-periodic elastic network (<= 10^7-10^8 nodes) is solved classically in minutes to hours, and no protein-science question needs 2^n >> 10^9 non-periodic oscillators with a succinct description.
minimal_classical_first_test: Build synthetic assemblies by symmetry-tiling a CA trace to 10^4-10^6 nodes (icosahedral/helical) with random defects. Use an ENM with an 8-10 A cutoff. Time sparse Verlet propagation and lowest-mode Lanczos on 8 cores, and extrapolate cost to 10^8 nodes. Hours.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low (very low). A real exponential mechanism with no protein-sized instance; the nearest application (centimetre-scale graphene) is materials science.
prior_art_known: Babbush, Berry, Kothari, Somma, Wiebe, PRX 13, 041041 (2023) (verified). Kolotouros et al., 'Quantum elastic network models and their application to graphene', arXiv 2601.05161 (verified: centimetre-scale graphene with ~160 logical qubits; no proteins). The search (web, 2026-09) found no protein application.
measurement_readout: Amplitude estimation of subsystem kinetic energy.
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: Bloch reduction and homogenisation; sparse solvers.

title: Exponential quantum-walk / stoquastic-adiabatic traversal of conformational graphs (glued trees, hierarchical graphs, GHV)
protein_question: Can a folding pathway be found (a path in the discretised conformational graph from an extended state to a low-energy, native-like state) when the landscape has entropic bottlenecks, a Levinthal-type traversal, that defeat local classical walks?
representation: Discrete conformational graph (lattice or torsion bins) with local moves.
quantum_primitive: Continuous-time quantum walks with exponential traversal speedups (Childs et al. 2003 glued/welded trees; Balasubramanian-Li-Harrow random hierarchical graphs); sign-free adiabatic paths with superpolynomial advantage (Somma-Nagaj-Kieferova 2012; Gilyen-Hastings-Vazirani 2021); GHV compiled into standalone discrete and continuous cost functions (Leng, Wu, Wu, Zheng 2025).
classical_primitive_replaced: Random-walk, PERM or guided classical search.
mechanism: When vertices group into 'supervertices' (columns) arranged along a low-dimensional lattice, with random edges between groups, the quantum walk stays in the symmetric subspace and moves ballistically along the columns. Any classical algorithm with only adjacency-oracle access to randomly labelled vertices gets lost in the exponentially large middle. These separations are proven in the oracle model. GHV extends them to stoquastic (sign-free) adiabatic paths, and a 2026 result shows guided stoquastic ground states on expander-plus-tree graphs resist classical sampling even with warm starts. Why a classical computer may copy it here: conformational graphs are explicit, so the 'labels' are structures whose column index (energy, compactness, secondary-structure content) is computable, and label-guided classical search walks the quotient chain directly. Physical graphs also carry energy disorder, which breaks the column symmetry and localises the quantum walk, and the 'exit' vertex must be recognised by a native-free predicate.
expected_speedup: None known for explicit conformational graphs; exponential only in the oracle model.
oracle_and_state_prep: Adjacency and energy oracles are explicit and cheap (local moves plus reversible energy evaluation), but that explicitness is exactly what voids the oracle-model lower bound. The start state is simple; the target must be identified without a native oracle.
strongest_classical_competitor: PERM/pull-move Monte Carlo; Wang-Landau; energy- or collective-variable-guided search; string/milestoning path methods; restart-saturated continuous decoding (QX-30).
information_vs_computation: Pure computation. It is relevant only if the landscape is golf-course-like, in which case it is also information-poor (no energetic guidance).
relation_to_S29_S33: OLD FAILURE: restart saturation (DNR-07) and funnelled landscapes; DNR-11 (transverse-field mixers that carry no problem information). NEW MECHANISM: coherent transport driven by graph symmetry, not Grover/QAOA/annealing on a diagonal cost. WHY THE OLD CONTROL STILL APPLIES: the separation needs hidden labels, which explicit energies do not provide, and at <= 60 aa search is already saturated.
kill_result: On enumerable lattice/torsion conformational graphs (L <= 16), label-guided classical search reaches the target in time polynomial in L whenever the quantum walk does, and the continuous-time quantum walk shows no exponential gap over PERM (energy disorder localises it).
minimal_classical_first_test: 2D HP lattice chains, L = 8-16: enumerate conformations and pull-move adjacency (<= ~10^6-10^7 states). Compute continuous-time quantum-walk transport (scipy expm_multiply, with and without an energy potential) from extended states to the ground state, and compare with a classical random walk and with PERM/greedy-by-energy. Fit scaling with L and measure the walk's localisation length. Hours.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low (very low). The only exponential traversal separations need oracle-hidden structure that explicit, disordered protein energies lack.
prior_art_known: Childs et al., STOC 2003, arXiv quant-ph/0209131 (verified). Balasubramanian, Li, Harrow, Commun. Math. Phys. (2025), arXiv 2307.15062 (verified). Somma, Nagaj, Kieferova, PRL 109, 050501 (2012) (verified). Gilyen, Hastings, Vazirani, STOC 2021, arXiv 2011.09495 (verified). Leng, Wu, Wu, Zheng, arXiv 2504.14841 (verified: oracle-defined, constructed objectives). 'Dequantization barriers for guided stoquastic Hamiltonians', arXiv 2602.23183 (abstract verified; authors not recorded). Kempe, hypercube hitting times (2005; not re-verified).
measurement_readout: Measure the vertex at the exit time.
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: Classical search guided by collective variables on the quotient chain.

title: Allosteric coupling and conformational entropy via quantum distribution-functional estimators (and entanglement as a representation of correlated modes)
protein_question: How strongly are distant sites coupled (mutual information between their conformational states, i.e. allostery)? What is the conformational-entropy change on ligand binding, a major unknown term in binding free energies?
representation: Posterior qsample over torsions; residue-cut bipartitions.
quantum_primitive: Quantum estimators of distribution functionals (Shannon/Renyi entropy, mutual information) with qsample or purified-query access (Li & Wu 2019; Gilyen & Li 2020); entanglement of the posterior qsample across residue cuts as a representation of correlated modes.
classical_primitive_replaced: kNN / thermodynamic-integration entropy estimators.
mechanism: For an unstructured distribution over N outcomes, quantum entropy estimation needs ~sqrt(N) queries (up to eps factors) vs Theta(N/log N) classical samples: quadratic in support size. Three facts cap this. (a) With a known energy, S = beta(<E> - F) comes from free energy and mean energy by thermodynamic integration/MBAR, with no dependence on support size. (b) For sample-only generators, the qsample needs the generator run coherently (M6: prohibitive), and N ~ e^S stays exponential for both sides. (c) A qsample's entanglement across a residue cut is fixed by the classical distribution's correlations, and by the Holevo bound it carries no more accessible information than the classical distribution. It would matter only against tensor-network twins (bond dimension ~e^{I_cut}, with I_cut ~ L^{2/3} for compact globules), not against MCMC, which stores one O(L) sample.
expected_speedup: Quadratic in support size, only for unstructured sample access; irrelevant when the energy is known.
oracle_and_state_prep: Needs a posterior qsample (M1 cost) or a coherent generator (M6, prohibitive). Functional estimators also need coherent log arithmetic.
strongest_classical_competitor: Thermodynamic integration / MBAR for conformational entropy; MIST and quasi-harmonic expansions; kNN estimators (Kozachenko-Leonenko, KSG) on low-dimensional site descriptors; normalising flows with exact likelihoods; MSM-based allosteric coupling.
information_vs_computation: Pure computation given the energy. Accuracy is limited by force-field / learned-energy bias (information), as with M4.
relation_to_S29_S33: A sub-case of M4/M13 (KILLED). OLD FAILURE: bias/mixing-limited estimation, and 'trainable implies classical surrogate'. NEW: entropy and mutual-information functionals, plus an explicit test of the 'entanglement as a resource' claim. WHY THE OLD CONTROL STILL APPLIES: with a known energy, the Boltzmann form removes support-size dependence.
kill_result: On mid30/long40 posteriors, TI/MBAR conformational entropy converges to +/-0.5 kT and KSG mutual information between distant sites converges at M <= 10^4 samples.
minimal_classical_first_test: On A80-energy MCMC ensembles for mid30 targets: conformational entropy by temperature TI and by kNN on torsions; KSG mutual information between distant residue pairs; the sequence-cut mutual-information profile (block kNN), which shows what a qsample's entanglement would encode (area- vs volume-law). Hours.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low (very low). With a known energy, classical TI/MBAR has no support-size dependence, and qsample entanglement carries no information beyond the classical distribution (Holevo).
prior_art_known: Li & Wu, IEEE TIT 65, 2899 (2019) (verified). Gilyen & Li, ITCS 2020, arXiv 1902.00814 (listing seen; bounds UNVERIFIED). Bravyi-Harrow-Hassidim 2011 (verified). No quantum allostery/entropy study in the repo bibliography.
measurement_readout: Functional estimates via amplitude estimation.
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: An MPS over residues would need bond dimension ~e^{I_cut}; MCMC needs no tensor network.

title: Analog quantum simulation of nuclear quantum effects in protein hydrogen-bond networks (and analog polymer emulators)
protein_question: Do nuclear quantum effects (zero-point energy, proton delocalisation in low-barrier hydrogen bonds, proton wires, e.g. in GFP-like chromophore pockets or ketosteroid isomerase) change which hydrogen-bond geometry, tautomer or protonation state is structurally stable?
representation: Quantum nuclear Hamiltonian of an active-site H-bond network: a few protons plus heavy-atom modes.
quantum_primitive: Analog quantum simulators (trapped ions, Rydberg arrays, superconducting circuits) emulating quantum-nuclear Hamiltonians or polymer models; annealers as physics emulators.
classical_primitive_replaced: Path-integral MD/MC.
mechanism: The claim: native quantum hardware reproduces quantum nuclei. Why a classical computer copies it: equilibrium properties of distinguishable nuclei (and bosons) follow from imaginary-time path integrals with positive weights, so there is no sign problem. Path-integral MD/MC costs only a polynomial factor (P ~ 16-32 beads, fewer with GLE-accelerated variants). Real-time tunnelling dynamics does carry a dynamical sign problem, but that is kinetics, not structure, and ring-polymer/instanton approximations often suffice. Analog emulators of classical polymer thermodynamics produce quantum states that differ from the classical Boltzmann law, and PERM/Wang-Landau already handle 10^3-10^6-mers.
expected_speedup: None for equilibrium structure.
oracle_and_state_prep: Mapping an ML/ab-initio potential for an active-site cluster onto analog hardware couplings is uncontrolled (the analog-programming problem), and controlled temperature is not available (M8).
strongest_classical_competitor: PIMD/PIGLET with ML potentials; ring-polymer MD and instantons for rates; grid diagonalisation for 1-3 proton coordinates; PERM/Wang-Landau for polymer models.
information_vs_computation: Pure computation. Structural NQE effects are small corrections on top of an information-limited backbone endpoint.
relation_to_S29_S33: M8 (annealer Boltzmann sampling, KILLED) and K-007 cover the emulator version. NEW: a physically quantum question (quantum nuclei). WHY IT STILL DIES: equilibrium quantum statistics of distinguishable particles is sign-free.
kill_result: PIMD converges the NQE structural shift (e.g. the O-O distance distribution of a model low-barrier H-bond) with <= 32 beads, at polynomial cost in the number of coupled protons.
minimal_classical_first_test: A 1D/2D double-well proton coupled to a heavy-atom O-O coordinate: exact quantum equilibrium by grid diagonalisation vs path-integral MC with P = 4-64 beads (numpy). Then a 4-8-proton wire. Show that cost is polynomial in protons and beads. Minutes to hours.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low (very low). Equilibrium quantum statistics of distinguishable nuclei is sign-free, so path-integral MD reproduces it at polynomial cost.
prior_art_known: M8 / [A61-A64] (repo-verified: annealers are noisy Gibbs samplers). Sign-freeness of path integrals for distinguishable particles is textbook (e.g. Ceperley, Rev. Mod. Phys. 67, 279 (1995); not re-verified this session).
measurement_readout: Analog-device observables.
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: PIMD; MCTDH for real-time dynamics of a few modes.

title: Quantum-native function as the objective: radical-pair spin dynamics in cryptochromes for structure inference and design
protein_question: Which structural features of a cryptochrome (radical-pair separation and orientation along the Trp tetrad, hyperfine environment, dynamics) produce its anisotropic magnetic-field effect? Can geometry be inferred from measured magnetic-field effects, or designed for them? Here the protein's function is itself quantum spin dynamics.
representation: Radical-pair spin Hamiltonian: 2 electrons plus n nuclei, with dipolar/exchange terms from geometry and hyperfine tensors.
quantum_primitive: Hamiltonian simulation of open-system radical-pair dynamics (two electron spins plus n nuclear spins with anisotropic hyperfine tensors; Haberkorn/Lindblad recombination); estimation of singlet yields; embedded in inversion or design.
classical_primitive_replaced: Exact Krylov or semiclassical propagation.
mechanism: The Hilbert-space dimension is 4*prod(2I_k + 1), about 2^{n+2}. Exact classical propagation is exponential in the number of hyperfine-coupled nuclei (realistic FAD/Trp pairs have ~20-30 significant nuclei), whereas a quantum computer needs poly(n) gates. The classical escape routes are unusually strong. The central-spin structure (nuclei couple mainly to the electrons) makes semiclassical and spin-coherent-state sampling accurate for many nuclei. Symmetry reduces equivalent nuclei. Typicality lets random nuclear states estimate the nuclear trace. The advantage survives only if these approximations miss the anisotropy by more than the parameter uncertainty.
expected_speedup: Exponential in the number of nuclei treated exactly, if approximations fail; likely none at the accuracy the biology can use.
oracle_and_state_prep: The Hamiltonian is explicit: hyperfine tensors from classical DFT/EPR, exchange/dipolar terms from geometry. No data-loading problem. Needs ~25-40 qubits plus ancillas for dissipation; the initial singlet state is trivial.
strongest_classical_competitor: Exact Krylov propagation up to ~20-25 nuclei with symmetry; Schulten-Wolynes semiclassics; spin-coherent-state / Monte Carlo sampling of nuclear configurations; truncation to dominant couplings; tools such as RadicalPy.
information_vs_computation: Information: magnetic-field-effect data (a few scalar yields, which weakly constrain geometry) plus classical hyperfine parameters. Computation: an exact forward model. The inverse problem is likely information-limited whatever the forward-model accuracy.
relation_to_S29_S33: Materially different (non-commuting open-system dynamics, not covered by H-001), but marginal to backbone structure. Like card 2, it tests whether a quantum-native forward model limits structural inference.
kill_result: Either: truncated-exact or semiclassical methods reproduce singlet-yield anisotropy within 5% (or within hyperfine-parameter uncertainty) at realistic nuclear counts; or the Fisher information of magnetic-field-effect data about geometry is too small for any forward model to constrain structure.
minimal_classical_first_test: Radical-pair model with n = 6-20 nuclei, hyperfine tensors with a realistic magnitude spread (a few ~1 mT, many ~0.1 mT). Compute the exact singlet yield vs field direction with expm_multiply on 2^{n+2} states (n = 20 gives ~4x10^6). Compare semiclassical and top-k truncation; report error vs n and the Fisher information about a radical-pair orientation angle under exact vs approximate models. Hours.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low. An exponential, quantum-native forward model, but the central-spin structure favours classical approximations and the structural payoff is small.
prior_art_known: 'Quantum simulation of the radical pair dynamics of the avian compass', arXiv 2211.15427 (listing seen; authors/venue UNVERIFIED). 'Simulating spin biology using a digital quantum computer', APL Quantum 1, 036114 (2024), arXiv 2406.12986 (listing seen). arXiv 2208.10107 (Trotterised radical-pair quantum beats; listing seen). RadicalPy, J. Chem. Theory Comput. (2024) (listing seen). These are demonstrations and none shows advantage over classical methods. The search found no study using quantum radical-pair simulation for protein structure inference.
measurement_readout: Singlet-yield expectation via ancilla or amplitude estimation.
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: Spin-coherent-state sampling; MPO for the nuclear bath; symmetry-adapted exact propagation.

title: (a) Quantum walk / QSA / quantum Metropolis / Langevin-RELD sampling of protein conformational posteriors
protein_question: Can a quantum sampler draw near-independent samples from the Boltzmann posterior over backbone internal coordinates, under a learned energy (A80/esmprior) or a physical one, at 60 residues or more, faster than best-tuned PT/REMD/SMC? That would make posterior averages (the 1.40x soft-average signal) available at lengths where classical mixing might fail.
quantum_primitive: Three families. (1) Szegedy/Metropolis quantum walks with quantum simulated annealing (QSA), or a QFold-style quantum Metropolis on discretised torsions. (2) Operator-level Langevin and replica-exchange Langevin (RELD) samplers that block-encode a first-order factorisation of the Witten Laplacian and apply QSVT singular-value thresholding (Leng, Ding, Chen & Lin, PNAS 2026). (3) Continuous Gibbs sampling on the torus with QSVT thresholding plus temperature annealing (Olivucci et al. 2026).
mechanism: Prior-art mechanism. For walks: phase estimation on the Szegedy walk operator, whose eigenphases scale as sqrt(delta), isolates the stationary state. QSA over a slowly varying sequence of chains needs Õ(1/sqrt(delta)) walk steps where a classical chain needs Õ(1/delta). A classical chain can only apply P; it cannot apply the coherent reflection whose phase gap is the square root of P's gap. For the Leng et al. sampler: sqrt(Gibbs) is the kernel of a first-order operator whose singular values are the square roots of the Laplacian's eigenvalues, so the QSVT filter degree scales as 1/sqrt(gap). Classical Langevin must instead diffuse for a time of about 1/gap. The abstract claims 'up to quartic' relative to MALA; exact exponents were not re-derived here. Olivucci et al. prove, on T^d with barrier amplitude alpha = e^{beta*Delta}, that any classical algorithm querying the value or any-order derivatives needs Omega(alpha) queries, while the quantum algorithm needs Õ(sqrt(alpha)) gradient-oracle queries. The gain is quadratic, and the quantum cost stays exponential in d at low temperature. Protein applications so far: QFold (≤4 residues; 1–5 bits per torsion; Psi4 energies precomputed as lookup tables; TTS exponent 0.53 with random initialisation and 0.89 with a Minifold warm start, against classical Metropolis only). Hauke/Faccioli (PRL 2021; Sci Rep 2022; JCTC 2024) sample transition paths on D-Wave over an ML-coarse-grained network. Micheletti, Hauke & Faccioli (PRL 2021) sample lattice polymer mixtures on D-Wave.
speedup_type: walk-steps (quadratic in 1/gap or in the barrier amplitude alpha; query model)
oracle_and_state_prep: Needs coherent, reversible evaluation of E(x) or grad E(x) on a superposition of discretised conformations. For A80 at n=60 that means about n^2/2 ≈ 1800 soft-binned pair lookups (28 bins) plus the (theta,tau) head, sterics and NeRF coordinate construction in fixed-point trigonometry, per call. The per-step Toffoli count is unmeasured; the literature analogues suggest 1e6–1e8 (gaps G-2 and G-6). The ESM-2 features are fixed per target and can be precomputed classically, but loading them by QROM is linear in table size (UNVERIFIED claim from Babbush 2018). Leng et al. need a warm start with |<phi|sigma>| = Omega(1). On a multimodal posterior, building such a warm start already requires knowing the modes and their weights. QFold's lookup tables grow exponentially with length and do not scale. Does it erase the speedup? Probably yes, unless classical mixing needs at least about 1e12 steps per independent sample (the program's rough B(L)).
strongest_classical_competitor: Parallel tempering or REMD with optimised ladders, REST2/Hamiltonian tempering, SMC or annealed importance sampling, Wang–Landau/multicanonical sampling. For learned posteriors, also generative proposals with exact reweighting (Boltzmann generators, BioEmu-class models). And random prior sampling plus relaxation, which beat VQE in S33 (QX-25).
information_vs_computation: All information comes from classical sources: ESM-2 features become the pair-distance distributions that define the energy. The quantum part only speeds up mixing on a fixed target distribution, so the achievable accuracy is capped by the classical posterior (the 1.40x soft-average gain was from an exact sum over 262,144 enumerated states).
relation_to_S29_S33: NEW MECHANISM relative to K-001..K-006. The output is a set of samples from a walk or Lindbladian stationary state, consumed as expectations, not an argmin, prefix or convex readout of a diagonal energy. H-001 does not cover this, per the KILLBOOK scope warning. OLD FAILURE risks: K-007/DNR-10 (Gibbs readouts on enumerable spaces lost to Metropolis) applies to any instance of 2^24 states or fewer. QX-25 (the random prior sampler won) is the classical twin that must be beaten. Condition C, now 'sample quality must transmit to the chain', must pass. WHY THE OLD CONTROL MAY NO LONGER APPLY: only in continuous, non-enumerable spaces at 60 aa or more, and only if classical mixing is measured to be slow. This is C-1/AA-1.
kill_result: Existing work already kills: QFold-style lookup-table quantum Metropolis (exponential tables; compared only with plain Metropolis; the warm start shrank the exponent advantage); D-Wave transition-path sampling (the underlying shortest path on a weighted graph is in P, and classical k-shortest-path and MSM path ensembles are polynomial); QAOA peptide sampling (Boulebnane et al., npj QI 2023, arXiv 2204.01821, V). Existing work leaves open: G-1 (no classical mixing measurement on a learned-energy protein posterior), G-2 (no fault-tolerant resource estimate for a walk or Langevin sampler on a continuous molecular or learned energy; the search found none), G-4 (no comparison against PT/REMD/SMC). Kill the lead if best-tuned PT/SMC shows ESS per CPU-second decaying at most polynomially, with tau_int ≤ ~1e6 energy evaluations at 60–150 aa. Also kill it if the posterior shows no persistence or hide-and-seek structure, so that PT gaps stay polynomial, or if B(L) exceeds the measured classical cost.
minimal_classical_first_test: Instrument: A80 energy on long40 (44–60 aa), plus 3–5 crops of 80–100 aa. Caveat: esmprior was trained on crops of 72 aa or less. Run PT with 16–32 replicas on geometric ladders plus SMC with 32 tempering stages, about 3 CPU-hours per target on the 8-core box. Measure: tau_int of energy and of RMSD to consensus; replica round-trip time; the number of basins (2 Å clustering) and their occupancy stability; split-R-hat over 8 independent runs; the slowest-mode autocorrelation as a gap proxy. Fit each against L. Kill if tau_int grows as L^3 or slower and round-trips stay under 1e5 sweeps at 60 aa (runs in under a day).
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low. The gain is quadratic only and the coherent oracle is heavy. No classical mixing bottleneck has ever been measured on a learned protein posterior, and funnelled landscapes plus PT give polynomial gaps. Olivucci-type hardness needs 'hidden' wells, which a learned prior tends to reveal.
classical_primitive_replaced: MCMC / Langevin / replica-exchange mixing steps
expected_speedup: Quadratic in 1/gap (Szegedy/QSA; Leng et al.); provably quadratic in alpha on T^d (Olivucci et al.); super-quadratic claims only heuristic (Incudini & Mazzola, arXiv 2607.22818, dense Ising).
measurement_readout: Conformation samples feeding posterior expectations (a soft structural average), not an argmin.
representation: Internal coordinates (theta,tau) or torsions, either discretised to 2^b bins (QFold used b = 1–5) or on a grid over T^d for the Witten-Laplacian and continuous-Gibbs methods.
prior_art_known: Verified in this session: QFold, Casares, Campos & Martin-Delgado, Quantum Sci. Technol. 7, 025013 (2022), arXiv 2101.10279, DOI 10.1088/2058-9565/ac4f2f. Leng, Ding, Chen & Lin, PNAS 123(8) e2512789123 (2026), arXiv 2505.05301. Olivucci et al., arXiv 2608.24527 (2026). Leng, Jiang & Lin, 'Accelerating quantum Gibbs sampling without quantum walks', arXiv 2604.22996 (2026). Hauke, Mattiotti & Faccioli, PRL 126, 028104 (2021), arXiv 2007.13788. Ghamari, Hauke, Covino & Faccioli, Sci Rep (2022), arXiv 2201.11781, DOI 10.1038/s41598-022-20032-x. Ghamari, Covino & Faccioli, JCTC (2024), arXiv 2311.15891, DOI 10.1021/acs.jctc.3c01174. Micheletti, Hauke & Faccioli, PRL 127, 080501 (2021), arXiv 2104.10102. Boulebnane et al., arXiv 2204.01821. Crosson & Harrow, FOCS 2016, arXiv 1601.03030. Patil, Bonde & Choubey, 'A Quantum Circuit Framework for Protein Ensemble-Level Energetics', arXiv 2608.05491 (2026; two states per residue, no strong baseline). Already in the bibliography: Szegedy (#1), Temme (#19), Ozgul (#35), Motamedi–Ronagh (#36), Claudon (#37), Campos QMS (#178), Incudini–Mazzola (#40), Layden (#41), Orfi–Sels (#42, #43). Not found in the search: any quantum sampler applied to a neural or language-model-derived molecular energy.
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: If mixing is fast, the target can already be sampled classically. Classical ML generators with exact reweighting, and random prior sampling plus relaxation, reproduce the value of posterior averaging (the S33 evidence). Nothing tensor-network-based is needed.

title: (b) Quantum simulation of nuclear-spin (NMR) many-body dynamics as the forward model for protein structure inference
protein_question: Can multi-spin NMR observables, such as dipolar echoes, OTOCs, proton spin diffusion in solids, strongly aligned samples or ZULF spectra, constrain long-range protein geometry beyond what two-spin NOE, RDC and chemical-shift analyses give? The assumption is that the forward model of such experiments is classically intractable and that a quantum processor can compute it.
quantum_primitive: Hamiltonian simulation (Trotterised or qubitised) of the secular dipolar, J and chemical-shift spin Hamiltonian; OTOC and echo estimation; on-device Jacobian and Hessian estimation for Hamiltonian learning (O'Brien et al. 2022); variational Bayesian inference with a quantum simulator (Sels et al. 2020); compressed sensing of spectra (Seetharam et al. 2023).
mechanism: Prior-art mechanism. Each nuclear spin maps to a qubit, and the device evolves under the same Hamiltonian at poly(k·t) gate cost. Classically, exact Liouville-space simulation of k strongly coupled spins costs 4^k. The speedup is physical, not generic: it holds only where the dynamics build high-weight operator correlations across many spins (the ergodic, OTOC regime), which defeats cluster expansions, restricted state spaces and tensor networks. The structural inversion then fits the dipolar couplings, which scale as r^-3(3cos^2θ − 1), to measured correlators. O'Brien et al. find that learnability tracks the ergodic-to-non-ergodic transition: the Hessian is degenerate in some regimes. So the regime that is hard classically is not automatically the one that is informative.
speedup_type: exponential-simulation (conditional on the classically hard regime)
oracle_and_state_prep: There is no black-box oracle. A hypothesised geometry is turned into a spin Hamiltonian classically: dipolar couplings from coordinates, shifts and J couplings from classical predictors. The state is the high-temperature NMR mixed state, handled with random-state typicality or an ancilla. The readout is expectation values with shot noise, where amplitude estimation is possible. Qubit count equals the number of spins in the correlated cluster (about 20–100); Elenewski et al. give explicit fault-tolerant circuit costs for ZULF, including protein examples (numbers not extracted). The erasing risk comes from inference: every candidate geometry and every gradient needs a new forward simulation, so the cost is multiplied by the number of forward calls in the Bayesian loop. Fast T2 relaxation in large proteins also truncates correlation growth, which helps classical methods too.
strongest_classical_competitor: Classical cluster approximations with linear scaling in spin count, which perform well in typical and somewhat beyond-typical regimes (Fratus et al., HQS, arXiv 2508.06448). Spinach restricted state spaces: polynomial simulation of 2D and 3D liquid-state experiments with relaxation on ubiquitin, over 1000 spins (Edwards et al., JMR 243:107, 2014). Tensor-train exact 15N ubiquitin simulation (Savostyanov et al., PRB 90:085139, 2014). Cluster-correlation expansion and Pauli-path truncation at short times. Most importantly, the practice of protein NMR avoids many-body analysis by design (isotope labelling, decoupling, weak-alignment RDCs, Solomon-equation NOEs, chemical-shift structure methods), and AlphaFold-class predictors now supply most folds.
information_vs_computation: This is the only direction in the lane where the quantum computation could unlock new physical information: new experimental data whose interpretation is currently blocked by the cost of the forward model. That matches the requirement in DNR-16 and K-012 for a new information source. The computation is the spin-dynamics forward model. Its value depends on the many-body observable carrying structural information that pairwise NMR observables or ML predictors do not already provide. That has not been shown for any protein.
relation_to_S29_S33: MATERIALLY DIFFERENT. OLD MECHANISM: quantum optimisation or sampling over classical diagonal energies (H-001, K-001..K-008). NEW MECHANISM: Hamiltonian simulation of a genuinely quantum physical system as the forward model for inverting experimental data. WHY THE OLD CONTROL NO LONGER APPLIES: H-001 and the prefix/solver-equivalence theorems assume a diagonal classical cost, while spin dynamics are non-diagonal and physically quantum. What still applies is an analogue of condition C: the inferred Hamiltonian parameters must transmit to structure accuracy. I(prog) is also satisfied in principle, because the new information comes from the experiment, not from the quantum computer.
kill_result: Existing work: Sels et al. 2020 (small molecules, variational Bayesian inference, no protein); Seetharam et al. 2023 (4-qubit ZULF spectrum of acetonitrile on trapped ions); O'Brien et al. 2022 (ubiquitin-in-membrane benchmark, but only small isolated spin clusters were learned); Google Quantum AI, Zhang et al. 2025 (OTOC of toluene and dimethylbiphenyl in a liquid crystal, geometry estimated, no advantage claimed); Burov et al. 2025 (up to 34 spins on IBM and IonQ with error mitigation); Stadler et al. 2026 (effective 21-spin model on Quantinuum H2, agrees with the classical reference); Elenewski et al. 2026 (fault-tolerant prospects for ZULF). Against these, Fratus et al. 2025 and 2026 report linear-scaling classical clusters that are accurate in typical regimes, and Kuprov 2014 simulated protein-scale liquid-state NMR in polynomial time. Open: (i) a protein NMR observable that is classically hard and carries structural information beyond the two-spin level; (ii) any end-to-end protein structure inference that uses a quantum forward model. Kill if classical cluster or restricted-state methods converge at cluster size ≤ ~14 spins for the structure-informative observables, or if two-spin rate-matrix models already capture the structural Fisher information.
minimal_classical_first_test: Take GB1 (56 aa) or ubiquitin (76 aa) from the PDB and add protons. Build secular dipolar Hamiltonians for (i) static or slow-MAS proton spin diffusion and (ii) a strongly aligned OTOC echo. Include a phenomenological T2. For an observable such as polarisation transfer between two residues about 8–12 Å apart at 0.5–5 ms, compute a cluster expansion at increasing cluster size k, with exact diagonalisation up to 14–16 spins (8 cores, in under a day). Measure: (1) convergence against k; (2) the Fisher information of the observable with respect to a 1 Å change in a long-range distance, captured at order k versus a two-spin rate-matrix model. Kill if it has converged by k ≤ 12–14 within experimental noise, or if the Fisher information is already captured at k = 2.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low. Relaxation and dilution make typical protein NMR regimes classically tractable (linear-scaling clusters), and the field avoids the hard regimes by design. Among the lane directions it has the best mechanism, because it is the only one with physical exponential hardness and a new information source.
classical_primitive_replaced: Classical spin-dynamics forward model (Liouville-space simulation) inside Bayesian or least-squares structure refinement
expected_speedup: Exponential in the size of the correlated spin cluster, but only in regimes (ergodic dynamics, strong coupling, ZULF, dense solids) where classical cluster, TN and restricted-state methods fail.
measurement_readout: Expectation values of spin correlators (spectra, echoes, OTOCs), compared with experiment to give a likelihood over geometries.
representation: A nuclear spin Hamiltonian whose parameters (dipolar couplings, shifts, J) are functions of 3D coordinates; qubits are spins.
prior_art_known: All verified in this session. Sels, Dashti, Mora, Demler & Demler, Nat Mach Intell 2, 396 (2020), arXiv 1910.14221, DOI 10.1038/s42256-020-0198-x. Seetharam et al., Sci Adv 9, eadh2594 (2023), arXiv 2109.13298, DOI 10.1126/sciadv.adh2594. O'Brien, Ioffe, Su, Fushman et al., PRX Quantum 3, 030345 (2022), arXiv 2109.02163, DOI 10.1103/PRXQuantum.3.030345. Zhang et al. (Google Quantum AI), arXiv 2510.19550 (2025). Google Quantum AI, Nature 646, 825 (2025), arXiv 2506.10191 (bibliography #376), with Bermejo et al., arXiv 2604.15427 (#377). Elenewski, Camara & Kalev, PRR 8, 013315 (2026), arXiv 2406.09340, DOI 10.1103/km66-ltpl. Burov, Baglio & Javerzac-Galy, arXiv 2512.14513 (2025). Stadler et al., arXiv 2609.17102 (Sep 2026). Fratus et al., arXiv 2508.06448 (2025). Edwards, Savostyanov, Welderufael, Lee & Kuprov, JMR 243, 107 (2014), arXiv 1402.6139, DOI 10.1016/j.jmr.2014.04.002. Savostyanov, Dolgov, Werner & Kuprov, PRB 90, 085139 (2014), arXiv 1402.4516. Not found in the search: any quantum proposal using ssNMR spin-diffusion data for protein structure.
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: Cluster and CCE expansions, Spinach restricted state spaces, tensor trains, and Pauli-path or Heisenberg-operator truncation. TN with belief propagation fails for Google's echo circuits (#377), but that is a synthetic circuit, not a protein NMR experiment.

title: (c) Quantum Hamiltonian Descent / continuous-space quantum optimisation for molecular or protein structure
protein_question: Does Schrödinger-dynamics optimisation, with tunnelling through barriers in continuous torsion or internal-coordinate space, find lower minima of a protein energy at 60 aa or more faster than classical global optimisers? And do those minima improve structure accuracy?
quantum_primitive: Quantum Hamiltonian Descent (QHD): H(t) = e^{phi_t}(−½∇²) + e^{chi_t} f(x). Digital implementations use a pseudo-spectral/QFT kinetic term and a phase oracle for f; analog implementations embed it in D-Wave. Variants: Riemannian QHD (QRHD, arXiv 2603.28624) for manifolds such as a torsion torus; AL-QHD for constraints; stochastic and non-smooth QHD.
mechanism: Prior-art mechanism. The kinetic term delocalises amplitude, and interference plus tunnelling moves it through barriers that classical gradient flow cannot cross. In the late 'descent' phase the dissipation factor concentrates the state in low-f basins (Leng et al.'s three-phase picture). Proven separations: Leng, Zheng & Wu construct a family with 2^d local minima that QHD solves in Õ(d^3) queries, while Gurobi and other classical solvers appear super-polynomial (empirically). Leng, Wu, Wu & Zheng 2025 compile the Gilyén–Hastings–Vazirani construction into a (sub)exponential oracle separation. Negative results: Chakrabarti et al. 2025 find no QHD speedup for convex problems over classical zeroth-order methods with exact oracles, only better noise tolerance. Resource estimates: AL-QHD needs about 9.4e8 T gates at about 530 variables (ACOPF). The 2026 encoding study finds that synthesising the potential dominates the cost for non-analytic objectives.
speedup_type: query (instance-specific; super-polynomial only on constructed instances)
oracle_and_state_prep: A phase oracle e^{−i h f(x)} on a d-dimensional grid, with binary encoding using O(d log N) qubits. For a protein with d = 2n ≈ 120 at 60 aa and 2^6–2^8 points per angle, that is about 700–1000 data qubits plus arithmetic ancillas for about 1800 pair terms and the NeRF build, per Trotter step, over many steps. The uniform initial state is cheap. The readout is a single measured x, which is an argmin readout, and that re-enters H-001's consumption class. Potential synthesis for a learned, tabulated energy is the dominant cost (per arXiv 2607.16996) and likely erases any gain.
strongest_classical_competitor: L-BFGS with 32–64 restarts, which already saturates at 44–60 aa (S-4, QX-30); basin hopping; PT quenches. Classical 'quantum-inspired' smoothing and tunnelling surrogates, which are the historical analogues of QHD's mechanism: the diffusion-equation method (Piela, Kostrowicki & Scheraga, J Phys Chem 1989, DOI 10.1021/j100345a090; applied to oligopeptides by Kostrowicki & Scheraga 1992, DOI 10.1021/j100197a057); imaginary-time Schrödinger searches (Amara, Hsu & Straub 1993, DOI 10.1021/j100127a023); classical quantum annealing of multidimensional functions (Finnila et al., CPL 1994, DOI 10.1016/0009-2614(94)00117-0).
information_vs_computation: All the information is in the energy function, and QHD adds only optimisation. At 9–60 aa, accuracy is information-limited (decoder 4.35 Å vs information floor 4.21 Å), and condition C fails (within-target rho −0.08), so lower energies do not transmit to structure accuracy.
relation_to_S29_S33: OLD FAILURE applies directly. Consuming the output as an argmin of a classical cost is K-002/DNR-02. Random prior sampling and the register-free decoder beating quantum search is K-006. Continuous decode saturates classically (S-4). Condition C and the energy–structure disconnect are I-5/I-6. QHD is continuous and has no register, but it only changes the search mechanism, not the endpoint. Reopen only if the C-2 test shows a growing search gap beyond 60 aa and condition C passes near the decoder's answer.
kill_result: Prior art: the search found no QHD or continuous quantum optimisation applied to molecules or proteins (arXiv abstract search for 'Hamiltonian descent' plus molecule/protein/conformation, 2023–2026). The classical versions of the same physical intuition (DEM smoothing, Gaussian wave-packet and imaginary-time searches) were applied to oligopeptides and LJ clusters in 1989–1994 and were not adopted over later methods. The direction is killed at 9–60 aa by restart saturation plus condition C. It stays open only as a conditional follow-up to C-2, and even then the separations known so far are on contrived instances.
minimal_classical_first_test: The C-2 test. On long40 plus 80–120 aa crops, compare L-BFGS multi-start (up to 1024 restarts), basin hopping and PT-quench on A80. Record best energy against budget, and the RMSD of the best-energy structure against budget. Compute within-target Spearman(E, RMSD) over the best 100 distinct minima. Kill if best energy saturates within about 1e3 restarts, or if |rho(E, RMSD)| ≤ 0.1.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low. The output is consumed as an argmin, the direction is killed by condition C and restart saturation, known separations are on constructed instances, and potential synthesis dominates the cost.
classical_primitive_replaced: Multi-start gradient descent / basin hopping
expected_speedup: None expected on protein energies; polynomial to (sub)exponential only on constructed instances.
measurement_readout: A single measured conformation (argmin-like).
representation: Continuous internal coordinates on a grid (torus for torsions; QRHD handles the manifold metric).
prior_art_known: Verified in this session: Leng, Hickman, Li & Wu, arXiv 2303.01471 (2023). Leng, Zheng & Wu, arXiv 2311.00811 (2023). Leng, Wu, Wu & Zheng, '(Sub)Exponential Quantum Speedup for Optimization', arXiv 2504.14841 (2025). Chakrabarti et al., arXiv 2503.24332 (2025). Kushnir et al., QHDOPT, arXiv 2409.03121. Leng et al., non-smooth QHD, arXiv 2503.15878. Abe & Nagai, QRHD, arXiv 2603.28624 (2026). Wu et al., AL-QHD resource analysis, arXiv 2605.12066 (2026). Liu et al., encoding and fault-tolerant resources for digital QHD, arXiv 2607.16996 (2026). The classical precursors are the Crossref DOIs listed above.
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: Classical smoothing and continuation (DEM), path-integral or semiclassical 'quantum annealing' surrogates, and multi-start L-BFGS reproduce the endpoint at the lengths tested.

title: (d) Quantum algorithms for knot invariants / topology of protein chains
protein_question: What is the knot type or entanglement (knots, slipknots, lassos, links) of a protein chain or a predicted model? And what is the distribution of knot types across a conformational ensemble?
quantum_primitive: The Aharonov–Jones–Landau (AJL) additive approximation of the Jones polynomial at roots of unity: BQP-complete for plat closures and DQC1-complete for trace closures. The end-to-end Jones pipeline on Quantinuum H2 (Laakkonen et al., PRX Quantum 7, 020355, 2026). A quantum algorithm for Khovanov homology (Schmidhuber et al. 2025).
mechanism: Prior-art mechanism. A closed braid is mapped to a unitary Temperley–Lieb/Fibonacci representation, and a Hadamard test estimates a normalised trace or matrix element that equals the Jones value up to an additive error. That error scales with the representation normalisation, which grows exponentially in the number of strands. Exact classical evaluation is #P-hard in general, but tensor-network contraction is efficient for low-treewidth diagrams. The Khovanov algorithm is efficient only if the Hodge Laplacian thermalises in polynomial time with a large gap.
speedup_type: none-known for protein-sized knots (exponential only for additive approximation on large high-treewidth braids)
oracle_and_state_prep: No oracle is needed. Chain to closure to braid word is classical and polynomial. The additive error cannot resolve low-crossing knots better than exact classical evaluation, so it adds nothing for this problem.
strongest_classical_competitor: Topoly (Dabrowski-Tumanski et al., Brief Bioinform 2020, DOI 10.1093/bib/bbaa196): Alexander, HOMFLY-PT and Jones invariants over many random closures after KMT reduction. KnotProt 2.0 (NAR 2019, DOI 10.1093/nar/gky1140). AlphaKnot and AlphaKnot 2.0 (NAR 2022, DOI 10.1093/nar/gkac388; NAR 2024, DOI 10.1093/nar/gkae443). HOMFLY-PT for proteins (Comoglio & Rinaldi, PLoS ONE 2011, arXiv 1104.3405). Tensor-network Jones solvers benchmarked by Laakkonen et al.
information_vs_computation: Knot type is a deterministic function of the given coordinates, so no information is missing. The computation is trivial for the low-crossing knots found in proteins (6_3 reported in AlphaFold models of the human proteome, bioRxiv DOI 10.1101/2021.12.30.474018, V). The claim of 7_1 as the most complex protein knot is UNVERIFIED.
relation_to_S29_S33: Materially different (computing a topological invariant, not optimisation), but it falls to the same kind of kill as K-011/DE-5: classical polynomial time, in milliseconds to seconds. Predicting whether a sequence folds into a knot is an information or learning problem (as in I-1).
kill_result: Killed by existing work. Protein knots have few crossings after reduction, and classical tools compute their invariants in seconds. Laakkonen et al. say near-term advantage needs large links 'if a candidate set of links are provided', i.e. there is no natural source of hard instances, and proteins are not one. The only open protein-topology question, the knot-type distribution of an ensemble, reduces to sampling (card a). The search found no quantum knot-invariant work applied to proteins (arXiv abstract search for knot + protein + quantum).
minimal_classical_first_test: Run Topoly on the most complex AlphaKnot or KnotProt entries plus the long40 decodes. Record wall time per structure (100 random closures), crossing number after KMT, and exact Jones and HOMFLY-PT. Expect under 1 s per protein, which kills the direction (runs in minutes).
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low (near zero): there is no computational bottleneck to accelerate.
classical_primitive_replaced: Knot-invariant evaluation (Alexander / HOMFLY-PT / Jones)
expected_speedup: None for protein knots.
measurement_readout: Hadamard-test estimate of the Jones value (additive error).
representation: Closed polygonal chain to braid word.
prior_art_known: Verified in this session: Aharonov, Jones & Landau, STOC 2006, arXiv quant-ph/0511096. Laakkonen, Rinaldi, Self, Chertkov et al., PRX Quantum 7, 020355 (2026), arXiv 2503.05625, DOI 10.1103/jgv8-l3j1. Kuperberg, Theory Comput. 11 (2015), arXiv 0908.0512. Schmidhuber, Reilly, Zanardi, Lloyd et al., arXiv 2501.12378 (2025). Passante et al., PRL 103, 250501 (2009), arXiv 0909.1550. The protein-knot tools are the Crossref DOIs listed above.
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: Exact classical invariants (Topoly), tensor-network Jones, and ML knot classifiers from sequence (Sikora et al., Protein Sci 2024, DOI 10.1002/pro.4998).

title: (e) Quantum topological data analysis (persistent / Mayer homology) for biomolecules, and its dequantisation
protein_question: Compute persistent Betti numbers, or Mayer Betti numbers, of protein structures or conformational ensembles as features for flexibility, folding, binding or metastable-state classification.
quantum_primitive: LGZ quantum TDA: uniform clique or Dicke state preparation, then phase estimation on a block-encoded combinatorial Laplacian to estimate beta_k/|S_k|. Improved versions add Chebyshev projectors and Kaiser-window amplitude estimation (Berry et al. 2024), and a streamlined algorithm (McArdle, Gilyén & Berta 2026). Quantum walks on simplicial complexes (Hayakawa et al. 2026). Quantum Mayer homology (Nghiem, Babbush, Zalcman, Berry, Phan, Wei & Hayakawa, 23 Sep 2026).
mechanism: Prior-art mechanism. A superposition over the k-simplices of a clique complex (up to C(n,k+1) of them) is measured by phase estimation, and the fraction of zero eigenvalues gives the normalised Betti number. An exponential advantage requires beta_k and |S_k| to be exponentially large, plus a multiplicative-error target. Otherwise the gain is at most quadratic (Berry et al.). The classical path-integral Monte Carlo of Apers et al. matches the quantum algorithm when the gap is large. Clique homology is QMA1-hard (Crichigno & Kohler), which rules out a general classical algorithm. Average-case hardness follows from planted clique (Strelchuk et al., Sep 2026). The Mayer-homology paper claims that Mayer Betti numbers are exponentially large for high-order simplices in the dense regime, that dequantisations lose their guarantees there, and that a few hundred qubits with about 6e7 Toffolis would exceed known classical methods.
speedup_type: exponential-simulation (conditional; only for dense, high-order simplicial complexes)
oracle_and_state_prep: The graph adjacency is classical and cheap. Preparing a uniform clique state costs amplitude amplification of about sqrt(C(n,k+1)/#cliques). The readout is beta_k/|S_k|, which is exponentially small unless beta_k is exponentially large. Biomolecular complexes built from 3D point clouds have small high-order Betti numbers, so the quantum readout carries almost no signal there.
strongest_classical_competitor: Ripser/GUDHI persistent homology in dimensions 0–2 on alpha or Vietoris–Rips complexes of 1e3–1e5 atoms (seconds). The Wei group's element-specific persistent homology and persistent Mayer Laplacians (Shen, Liu & Wei, arXiv 2312.01268; Feng et al., arXiv 2408.13299), all computed classically. Classical Betti estimators (Apers et al., Quantum 7, 1202, 2023; Sorci, arXiv 2509.16171).
information_vs_computation: The features are deterministic functions of the coordinates and add no new information. Biomolecular persistent homology uses low-dimensional homology of 3D point sets, where classical computation is polynomial and trivial. No evidence was found that high-order homology carries predictive structural information.
relation_to_S29_S33: Materially different (linear algebra over simplicial complexes), but the K-011 type of kill (classical, polynomial, fast) applies. Using topological features to predict structure is also information-limited (DE-6: feature engineering cannot create missing per-target information).
kill_result: The search found no quantum TDA applied to proteins or biomolecules (arXiv abstract search for TDA or persistent homology plus quantum plus protein or molecule). Existing work largely kills generic quantum TDA outside dense, high-order regimes (Gyurik, Cade & Dunjko 2022; Schmidhuber & Lloyd 2023; Berry et al. 2024; Apers et al. 2023). The new Mayer-homology claim targets dense high-order complexes, while its cited biomolecular use (protein–ligand affinity features) is low-order and trivially classical, so the two regimes do not overlap. What is left open is theoretical (Mayer TDA in dense regimes), and it is not a protein question.
minimal_classical_first_test: Compute Rips and alpha persistent homology (Ripser) of CA and heavy-atom clouds for long40 targets and for a PT ensemble, and time it. At several scales, compute beta_k and beta_k/|S_k| for k ≤ 6 on dense Rips complexes (the quantity the quantum algorithm estimates), and Mayer Betti numbers (N = 3) where feasible. Separately, test whether k ≥ 3 features improve basin classification AUC over k ≤ 2. Kill if beta_k/|S_k| is exponentially small or if k ≤ 2 features saturate AUC (runs within hours).
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low: the quantum advantage regime and the biomolecular application regime are disjoint.
classical_primitive_replaced: Boundary-matrix reduction / Laplacian kernel counting
expected_speedup: None for biomolecular TDA (low-order); exponential only for dense high-order complexes with large Betti numbers.
measurement_readout: Normalised (Mayer) Betti number via phase estimation / amplitude estimation.
representation: Point cloud to Vietoris–Rips/clique complex to combinatorial (Mayer) Laplacian.
prior_art_known: Verified in this session: Lloyd, Garnerone & Zanardi, arXiv 1408.3106. Gyurik, Cade & Dunjko, Quantum 6, 855 (2022), arXiv 2005.02607. Berry et al., PRX Quantum 5, 010319 (2024), arXiv 2209.13581. Schmidhuber & Lloyd, PRX Quantum 4, 040349 (2023), arXiv 2209.14286. Crichigno & Kohler, Nat Commun (2024), arXiv 2209.11793. Apers, Gribling, Sen & Szabó, Quantum 7, 1202 (2023), arXiv 2211.09618. Akhalwaya et al., ICLR 2024, arXiv 2209.09371. McArdle, Gilyén & Berta, Quantum 10, 2058 (2026), arXiv 2209.12887. Hayakawa, Chen & Hsieh, Quantum 10, 2138 (2026), arXiv 2404.15407. Strelchuk, Subramanian & Wesołowski, arXiv 2609.12777 (2026). Nghiem et al. (Mayer), arXiv 2609.28058 (2026). Xia & Wei, IJNMBE 30, 814 (2014), arXiv 1412.2779. Feng, Shen, Liu & Wei, arXiv 2408.13299 (2024).
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: Exact persistent homology (Ripser/GUDHI) in dimensions 0–2, classical Monte Carlo Betti estimators, and ML on persistence features.

title: (f) Quantum distribution property testing (closeness / identity / entropy) applied to structural ensembles
protein_question: With fewer samples, decide whether two conformational ensembles are the same or epsilon-far apart: two MD runs, a sampler against a reference, mutant against wild type, or prior against posterior. Or estimate the entropy or independence of structural features.
quantum_primitive: Quantum distribution testing with purified query access (Bravyi, Harrow & Hassidim 2011; Gilyén & Li 2019), surveyed by Montanaro & de Wolf (2016). Lower bounds come from quantum sample-to-query lifting (Wang & Zhang, SICOMP 2025; Chen, Wang & Zhang 2025).
mechanism: Prior-art mechanism. Given a unitary U_p|0> = sum_i sqrt(p_i)|i>|psi_i>, amplitude estimation on overlaps and inner products estimates L1, L2 or Hellinger distances and entropies. For closeness on a domain of size N this takes about Õ(sqrt(N)/eps) queries, against about N^{2/3} classical samples (the classical bound is UNVERIFIED in this pass). The gain is polynomial in N and at most quadratic in 1/eps. Sample-to-query lifting bounds how far query access can beat quantum samples.
oracle_and_state_prep: Requires a coherent sampler U_p, which for a Boltzmann ensemble is coherent Gibbs-state preparation, i.e. problem (a) with its full cost. Given only classical MD samples, a quantum tester has no advantage. This erases the speedup unless (a) succeeds.
strongest_classical_competitor: Classical closeness and identity testers, plus the practical tools: block averaging, split-R-hat, KS or Wasserstein two-sample tests on collective-variable (CV) projections, and bootstrap. In practice the cost is producing decorrelated samples (tau_int), not the tester's sample complexity.
information_vs_computation: The information sits in the ensembles, which are generated by classical sampling. The quantum part only reduces oracle calls, and only if a coherent sampler exists.
relation_to_S29_S33: A new formulation (hypothesis testing), but the oracle is the sampler, so it reduces to card (a). There is an OLD FAILURE analogue: estimation is bias- and mixing-limited, not variance-limited, and C-3/OP-07 has never shown a variance-limited decision. The same logic killed amplitude estimation for ensembles.
kill_result: The search found no application of quantum property testing to structural biology or MD (arXiv abstract search). Existing theory already kills it: it needs purified query access, the lifting theorem bounds the gain, and practical domains (1e2–1e4 CV bins) make N^{1/2} against N^{2/3} a factor of only about 2–5. The kill is complete unless (a) provides a coherent sampler.
minimal_classical_first_test: For pairs of PT ensembles on A80 at 44–60 aa, run classical two-sample tests on 2D-CV histograms with N = 100–2500 bins. Measure the independent samples needed for a decision at eps = 0.1 and multiply by tau_int to get CPU cost. Kill if the tester's sample count is under 1% of the cost of generating decorrelated samples (runs in hours).
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low: it depends on (a), and the gain is at most polynomial in a small domain size.
classical_primitive_replaced: Two-sample / convergence tests on sampled ensembles
expected_speedup: ≤ N^{1/6} factor (closeness) and ≤ quadratic in 1/eps, given a coherent sampler.
measurement_readout: Accept/reject or a distance/entropy estimate via amplitude estimation.
representation: Discretised CV histograms or conformational clusters, as a distribution on N elements.
prior_art_known: Verified in this session: Bravyi, Harrow & Hassidim, IEEE TIT 57, 3971 (2011), arXiv 0907.3920, DOI 10.1109/TIT.2011.2134250. Gilyén & Li, arXiv 1902.00814 (2019; ITCS 2020 venue UNVERIFIED). Montanaro & de Wolf, Theory of Computing Grad. Surveys 7 (2016), arXiv 1310.2035. Wang & Zhang, SICOMP 54(5), 1294 (2025), arXiv 2308.01794, DOI 10.1137/24M1638616. Chen, Wang & Zhang, arXiv 2512.01971 (2025). Wang, arXiv 2608.02600 (2026). Yu, arXiv 1904.03218. Apers & Sarlette, quantum fast-forwarding (bibliography #29). Tang, Wright & Zhandry 2025 (strengthened lifting) is UNVERIFIED, cited only inside 2512.01971.
