tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: Classical two-sample tests on low-dimensional projections are sufficient; the bottleneck is sample generation.

title: (g) Quantum computing for cryo-EM / crystallographic structure determination (inverse problems)
protein_question: Reconstruct 3D density and atomic models, including conformational heterogeneity, from about 1e5–1e7 noisy 2D projections at unknown orientations, or solve the crystallographic phase problem, faster or at lower dose.
quantum_primitive: No established primitive. Candidates proposed generically include quantum linear-system or QSVT solvers and QUBO or quantum-annealing reconstruction for tomography (Lee & Jun 2025, X-ray/CT), and amplitude estimation to marginalise over poses. Adjacent, but not computation: quantum metrology via interaction-free measurement or a 'quantum electron microscope' (Kruit et al. design), and multi-pass TEM.
mechanism: Prior-art mechanism. On the computational side, nothing has been demonstrated for cryo-EM. Tomography proposals solve small sinograms with QUBO or HHL-type methods. These face dequantisation for low-rank structure (Chia et al., STOC 2020) and a data-loading bottleneck: about 1e5–1e7 images of 1e4–1e6 pixels must be loaded through QRAM in linear time. On the metrology side, a quantum-Zeno or interaction-free scheme detects a scatterer while the probability that the electron interacts goes to zero as the number of passes grows. That raises information per unit dose, and dose (radiation damage) is the real physical bottleneck. No classical computation can copy this, but it is a hardware effect, not a quantum computer.
speedup_type: none-known (computational); the metrology route is a dose/precision gain, not a computational speedup
oracle_and_state_prep: A coherent pose-marginalisation oracle would need the Fourier-slice projection and the CTF/noise likelihood evaluated reversibly, per image, plus QRAM loading of all images. Loading cost is linear in data size, which erases any polylog gain. At high resolution, pose posteriors are sharply peaked, so there is little marginalisation for amplitude estimation to accelerate.
strongest_classical_competitor: GPU expectation-maximisation or stochastic-gradient reconstruction with branch-and-bound pose search (RELION or cryoSPARC class), deep heterogeneity models (cryoDRGN or 3DFlex class), automated model building, AlphaFold-guided fitting. For crystallography, molecular replacement with AlphaFold models. These tool names are UNVERIFIED in this pass (no DOIs fetched).
information_vs_computation: The bottleneck is information per electron dose (SNR, radiation damage) and whether heterogeneity is identifiable. Computation costs GPU-hours and keeps falling. Only the metrology route changes the information budget, and it does so physically.
relation_to_S29_S33: Materially different domain (experimental inversion), but I(prog) applies: no quantum computation creates information absent from its inputs. Amplitude estimation for ensembles was already killed (the literature phase). The metrology branch would supply new information per dose (as DNR-16 requires) but lies outside quantum computing.
kill_result: No quantum-computing cryo-EM work was found: arXiv abstract search for cryo-EM plus quantum computing, annealing, algorithm or qubit returned zero hits; OpenAlex title/abstract filters returned only a viXra item; Crossref returned nothing relevant. The only quantum tomography items are generic X-ray/CT work (Lee & Jun, arXiv 2502.04830; Ryou et al., QCE 2025, UNVERIFIED content). The gap is empty for structural reasons: the pipeline is data-I/O- and FFT-bound and embarrassingly parallel. Open: quantum-metrology dose reduction (Kruit et al.; Agarwal, Berggren & Goyal, PRA 99, 063809, 2019). No benefit on biological samples has been shown (not verified either way).
minimal_classical_first_test: Simulate projections of a 64^3 map built from a PDB entry at SNR 0.01–0.1 with a CTF. Compute each image's pose posterior over an SO(3) × shift grid (about 5k × 50) on CPU, and measure its effective support exp(H) and the time per image. Kill if, at resolution-limiting iterations, effective support is at most about 1e2 poses and the per-image cost is dominated by FFT and I/O (runs within hours).
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low for computation (information-limited, and data loading kills it); the metrology branch is a separate question outside this program's scope.
classical_primitive_replaced: Pose marginalisation / tomographic linear inversion
expected_speedup: None known for computation.
measurement_readout: Density map / pose posterior (computation); electron detection events (metrology).
representation: 2D projection images, SO(3) poses, 3D voxel density.
prior_art_known: Verified in this session: Kruit, Hobbs, Kim, Yang et al., 'Designs for a Quantum Electron Microscope', arXiv 1510.05946 (the Ultramicroscopy 2016 venue is UNVERIFIED). Agarwal, Berggren & Goyal, PRA 99, 063809 (2019), arXiv 1901.09702. Juffmann et al., 'Multi-pass transmission electron microscopy', arXiv 1612.04931. Chia, Gilyén, Li, Lin, Tang & Wang, STOC 2020, arXiv 1910.06151, DOI 10.1145/3357713.3384314. Lee & Jun, arXiv 2502.04830 (2025; claims 'quantum supremacy' in tomography, not assessed). Nothing was found for quantum cryo-EM or the quantum phase problem.
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: Classical GPU pipelines plus deep generative heterogeneity models; AlphaFold priors for model building and molecular replacement.

title: (h) Prior-warm-started quantum sampling / quantum Bayesian inference with learned structure priors
protein_question: Given a learned structure prior (ESM-derived esmprior/A80, or a generative model) and a likelihood (physics energy or experimental restraints), can a quantum algorithm starting from a coherent prior state produce posterior samples or the evidence Z quadratically faster? Routes include prior-to-posterior quantum rejection sampling, amplitude amplification, and QSA from the prior.
quantum_primitive: Quantum rejection sampling (Ozols, Roetteler & Roland, ITCS 2012). Quantum inference on Bayesian networks, quadratic in 1/P(evidence) (Low, Yoder & Chuang 2014). Adaptive QSA for Bayesian inference and partition functions (Harrow & Wei, SODA 2020). QSA over slowly evolving chains (Wocjan & Abeyesinghe 2008; Orsucci, Briegel & Dunjko 2018). Warm-start-dependent Gibbs samplers (Leng et al. PNAS 2026; Leng, Jiang & Lin 2026).
mechanism: Prior-art mechanism. Prepare |pi_prior> = sum_x sqrt(prior(x))|x>, then amplitude-amplify the likelihood-weighted component. This costs O(sqrt(M)) coherent prior preparations and likelihood calls, where M = sup L / E_prior[L], against O(M) for classical rejection. For annealing from the prior, a chain of Gibbs states with constant overlaps lets QSA use Õ(l/sqrt(delta)) walk steps. Harrow & Wei's adaptive schedule roughly matches the best classical schedule length and improves on non-adaptive schedules by about a quadratic factor. All gains are quadratic in M or 1/delta. A classical computer can resample but cannot amplify amplitudes.
oracle_and_state_prep: A coherent prior is the crux. For a neural or autoregressive prior, it needs coherent evaluation of the generative model on every branch. esmprior's pair-distance terms do not form a normalised product distribution, so the prior is not efficiently q-sampleable without its own walk. The likelihood oracle is the same coherent energy evaluation as in (a). If log M grows linearly with residue count L, sqrt(M) is still exponential. QFold is the only protein data point: with a Minifold warm start the quantum TTS exponent was 0.89, against 0.53 from random initialisation. So a better prior helped the classical chain about as much and shrank the quantum advantage.
strongest_classical_competitor: SMC or annealed importance sampling from the prior; tempering. From a warm start, classical mixing costs about t_rel·log(1/eps), with no log(1/pi_min) term. Importance reweighting of samples from learned generators (Boltzmann-generator or BioEmu class). Random prior sampling plus relaxation, which beat VQE in S33 (QX-25).
information_vs_computation: All information comes from classical sources: the ESM prior and the energy or restraints. The quantum part removes only a square root from M or from 1/delta. Better learned priors (more information) shrink M and 1/delta for classical and quantum alike, so progress in information closes the quantum window. Olivucci-type hardness assumes the sampler has no side information about hidden wells, and a learned prior is exactly such side information.
relation_to_S29_S33: Part of C-1/AA-1. NEW MECHANISM relative to K-001..K-008: amplitude amplification of a coherent prior, not a diagonal-cost argmin. OLD FAILURE threats: QX-25, random prior sampling as the classical twin that beat VQE; K-007 (Gibbs readouts on enumerable spaces lost to Metropolis); I-2/I-5 (when missing per-target information limits accuracy, a faster posterior sampler cannot help). WHY THE OLD CONTROL MIGHT NOT APPLY: at 60 aa or more, prior-to-posterior importance sampling collapses (its ESS falls exponentially). But then the right control is SMC or tempering, not rejection, and SMC is usually polynomial on funnelled targets.
kill_result: Existing work leaves the protein application untested: the search found no quantum rejection sampling, QSA or Bayesian-network inference applied with a learned protein prior. QFold is a lookup-table toy of 4 residues or fewer. The theory caps every route at quadratic gains. Kill if (1) SMC or tempering from the prior keeps ESS per CPU-second decaying only polynomially in L, or (2) log M ∝ L, so that sqrt(M) is exponential and worse than SMC, or (3) coherent prior preparation costs more than the whole classical SMC run.
minimal_classical_first_test: On tuning126, mid30 and long40, draw 1e5 samples from the esmprior (theta,tau) head plus the decoder, and importance-weight them to the A80 posterior at beta = 1. Measure log M (max weight over mean weight) and ESS/N as functions of L. Compare with SMC using 16–64 tempering stages plus MCMC moves (ESS, CPU time). Kill if log M grows linearly in L while SMC's cost grows polynomially, since quantum rejection is then dominated by classical SMC (runs in under a day).
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low: the gain is quadratic, preparing a coherent learned prior is expensive, and better priors help classical samplers equally (the QFold evidence).
classical_primitive_replaced: Rejection / importance sampling and annealing from a prior
expected_speedup: Quadratic in M (rejection constant) or 1/delta (gap); none against SMC if log M grows linearly in L.
measurement_readout: Posterior samples, or evidence (log Z) estimates via QSA and amplitude estimation.
representation: Discretised internal coordinates amplitude-encoded with prior weights.
prior_art_known: Verified in this session: Ozols, Roetteler & Roland, ITCS 2012, arXiv 1103.2774, DOI 10.1145/2090236.2090261. Harrow & Wei, SODA 2020, arXiv 1907.09965, DOI 10.1137/1.9781611975994.12 (resolves bibliography lead #7). Wocjan & Abeyesinghe, PRA 78, 042336 (2008), arXiv 0804.4259. Orsucci, Briegel & Dunjko, Quantum 2, 105 (2018), arXiv 1503.01334. Childs, Li, Liu, Wang et al., NeurIPS 2022, arXiv 2210.06539 (log-concave, warm start). Leng, Jiang & Lin, arXiv 2604.22996 (2026). QFold, arXiv 2101.10279. Already in the bibliography: Low, Yoder & Chuang, PRA 89, 062315 (2014), #31; Leng et al. PNAS (#38).
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: SMC or tempering from the learned prior, reweighted generative models, and random prior sampling with relaxation.

title: (i) [Additional direction found while scouting] Exponential quantum simulation of classical coupled oscillators / Koopman–von Neumann MD (quantum elastic network models) for proteins
protein_question: Protein vibrational and elastic dynamics under elastic-network or harmonic models, such as normal modes, allosteric signal propagation, heat flow, or the kinetic energy of a residue subset at time t, for very large assemblies. More generally, classical MD observables (Green–Kubo, transition-state-theory rates) computed via the Koopman–von Neumann (KvN) formulation.
quantum_primitive: Babbush, Berry, Kothari, Somma et al.: Hamiltonian simulation of 2^n coupled classical oscillators, with velocities and displacements amplitude-encoded. Quantum elastic network models (QENM; Kolotouros et al. 2026). KvN molecular dynamics with QPE and amplitude-estimation readouts (Watanabe et al., two 2026 preprints).
mechanism: Prior-art mechanism. Newton's equation M x'' = −K x maps to a Schrödinger equation whose Hamiltonian is built from B with B B† = M^{-1/2} K M^{-1/2}. The state amplitudes encode sqrt(M) x' and B†x for 2^n oscillators. Simulation is poly(n) when masses and springs are efficiently queryable and the initial state is efficiently preparable. Readout is limited to a few global scalars (for example the kinetic energy of a subset) via amplitude estimation. Classical algorithms provably need 2^{Omega(n)} queries, and the problem is BQP-complete with circuit oracles. KvN turns classical Liouville dynamics into unitary evolution on a phase-space grid.
oracle_and_state_prep: Requires spring constants and masses computable by a small circuit from the oscillator index, i.e. structured, lattice-like connectivity. A protein elastic network's K is a data table built from coordinates, with at most about 1e6 nodes even for large assemblies. QROM loading is linear in size, so it erases the exponential gain. The initial state must also be efficiently preparable. KvN of anharmonic MD needs grids in 3N dimensions, with readouts limited to a few correlators.
strongest_classical_competitor: Sparse Lanczos ANM/GNM normal-mode analysis (ProDy-class tools, UNVERIFIED), coarse-grained elastic networks of whole viral capsids with 1e5–1e6 nodes solved classically, and closed-form harmonic linear response. Any harmonic system up to about 1e8 nodes is classically tractable.
information_vs_computation: The information is the contact map from a known structure, and the harmonic model is crude. The exponential gain covers only the linear (harmonic) regime, not the anharmonic conformational transitions that matter for proteins. Nothing here adds information for structure prediction.
relation_to_S29_S33: Materially different: exponential simulation, not optimisation or sampling of diagonal energies. H-001 does not apply. But it lies outside the program's structure-accuracy endpoint (K-012/I-1 are untouched), and the protein instances are too small and data-defined for the speedup to exist.
kill_result: The search found no protein application: QENM has been applied to graphene only, and KvN MD to H2 only. Babbush et al.'s own conditions (2^n oscillators, oracle-structured couplings, efficient initial state, global readout) are not met by protein elastic networks, so the direction is killed for proteins. It remains a real exponential primitive for structured materials.
minimal_classical_first_test: Build an ANM for a large assembly (a capsid of about 1e5 CA atoms) on the 8-core box. Compute the lowest 100 modes with sparse Lanczos, and the time-dependent kinetic energy of a residue subset. Expect minutes, which kills the direction.
prior_probability_of_real_advantage: low (near zero for protein structure): protein instances are small and data-defined.
classical_primitive_replaced: Normal-mode / harmonic dynamics integration
expected_speedup: Exponential only for 2^n oracle-structured oscillator networks; none for protein ENMs.
measurement_readout: Amplitude-estimated global observables (kinetic energy of a subset, correlators).
representation: Masses and springs of an elastic network; a KvN phase-space grid.
prior_art_known: Verified in this session: Babbush, Berry, Kothari, Somma et al., PRX 13, 041041 (2023), arXiv 2303.13012, DOI 10.1103/PhysRevX.13.041041. Kolotouros, Sireesh, Ferguson, Thrasher et al., 'Quantum Elastic Network Models and their Application to Graphene', arXiv 2601.05161 (2026). Watanabe et al., KvN MD for Green–Kubo, arXiv 2605.30142 (2026). Watanabe et al., end-to-end MD with a Langevin thermostat on quantum circuits, arXiv 2605.30143 (2026). Lee & Kanno, modal analysis via qubitization, arXiv 2307.07478.
tn_or_classical_ml_reproduction: Classical sparse eigensolvers and direct integration at protein-relevant sizes.
